knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the compact smooth setting in which alphaBB curvature bounds and separable quadratic corrections are finite.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 11. The alphaBB for Box Constrained Twice-Differentiable NLPs: Theory p. 315

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A box-constrained twice-differentiable problem is
\[
\min\{f(x):x\in X\},\qquad X=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\ell_i\le x_i\le u_i,\ i=1,\ldots,n\},
\]
where \(X\) is nonempty and bounded and \(f\in C^2\) on a neighborhood of \(X\). Compactness and continuity imply that \(x\mapsto\lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2 f(x))\) attains a finite minimum on \(X\). Consequently, there exists \(\alpha\ge0\) such that \(\nabla^2 f(x)+2\alpha I\succeq0\) for every \(x\in X\), providing the foundational alphaBB applicability regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smooth objective on a nonempty bounded box has bounded curvature and therefore admits a finite diagonal convexifying correction.
knowledge_statements.title: Box-Constrained Twice-Differentiable Problems

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 11. The alphaBB for Box Constrained Twice-Differentiable NLPs: Theory p. 315

knowledge_statements.scope_note: The example isolates loss of a uniform curvature lower bound; some functions on unbounded domains still admit finite corrections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(x)=-x^4\) on \(\mathbb R\), \(f''(x)=-12x^2\). Thus for every finite \(\alpha\ge0\), \(f''(x)+2\alpha<0\) whenever \(|x|>\sqrt{\alpha/6}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The smooth function minus x to the fourth has curvature tending to minus infinity, so no finite uniform alphaBB correction convexifies it on the real line.
knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded-Domain Curvature Failure

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar-parameter alphaBB convexification of a twice-differentiable function on a box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let B=\prod_{i=1}^n[x_i^L,x_i^U] and \phi_\alpha(x)=f(x)+\alpha\sum_{i=1}^n(x_i^L-x_i)(x_i^U-x_i). If \lambda_j(\nabla^2f(x)) are the Hessian eigenvalues and \alpha\geq\max\left\{0,\max_{x\in B}\max_{1\leq j\leq n}\left(-\tfrac12\lambda_j(\nabla^2f(x))\right)\right\}, then \phi_\alpha is convex on B.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a twice-differentiable function on a box, the scalar alphaBB correction is convex whenever alpha is nonnegative and at least half the magnitude of every negative Hessian eigenvalue throughout the box.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Relaxed-dual representation by the AlphaBB objective
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent scalar-alpha representation of the relaxed dual for the associated box-constrained minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let B=\prod_{i=1}^n[x_i^L,x_i^U] and \mathcal L(x)=f(x)+\alpha\sum_{i=1}^n(x_i^L-x_i)(x_i^U-x_i). If \alpha\geq\max\left\{0,\max_{x\in B}\max_{1\leq j\leq n}\left(-\tfrac12\lambda_j(\nabla^2f(x))\right)\right\}, then the relaxed dual formulation of the associated minimization problem, and hence the original formulation, is equivalent to minimizing \mathcal L over B.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With alpha chosen from the Hessian-eigenvalue bound, the relaxed dual and the associated original box-constrained minimization problem admit the equivalent formulation of minimizing the alphaBB function over the box.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The relaxed dual and associated minimization problem are equivalent to }\min_{x\in B}\mathcal L(x)

knowledge_statements.title: Constrained Twice-Differentiable Nonlinear Programs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covers smooth nonlinear programs whose objective, inequalities, equalities, or any combination require convexification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A constrained twice-differentiable nonlinear program on a box has the form
\[
\min_{x\in X} f(x)\quad\text{subject to}\quad g_j(x)\le0\ \ (j=1,\ldots,m),\qquad h_k(x)=0\ \ (k=1,\ldots,p).
\]
For an alphaBB relaxation, every nonconvex function occurring on the left side of a required inequality is replaced by a convex underestimator on \(X\). Thus the objective \(f\), each \(g_j\), and both \(h_k\) and \(-h_k\) may require separate curvature corrections. The resulting convex problem supplies a lower bound and a convex outer approximation of the original feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smooth box-constrained nonlinear program may require separate convex underestimators for its objective, inequalities, and both signs of each equality.
assumptions_latex: \(f,g_1,\ldots,g_m,h_1,\ldots,h_p\) are twice continuously differentiable on an open neighborhood of \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Convex underestimators of the objective and each inequality function, including both signs of every equality, define a convex relaxation of the nonlinear program.

children.title: Generic Curvature-Corrected Terms
children.top_down_role: Nonconvex terms handled through whole-term regional curvature correction.

assumptions_latex: \(X=[\ell,u]\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty and bounded, and \(t\in C^2\) near \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The corrected term \(\underline t_a\) is convex on \(X\), underestimates \(t\), and agrees with \(t\) at every vertex of \(X\).

notation.meaning: Coordinate box factor, nonnegative on the box

knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the generic separable quadratic correction available without exploitable algebraic structure beyond smoothness and curvature bounds.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 11. The alphaBB for Box Constrained Twice-Differentiable NLPs: Theory p. 315

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a generic smooth term \(t\), define
\[
\underline t_a(x)=t(x)-\sum_{i=1}^n a_i(x_i-\ell_i)(u_i-x_i).
\]
Because each box factor is nonnegative on \(X\), one has \(\underline t_a(x)\le t(x)\) for all \(x\in X\). Moreover,
\[
\nabla^2\underline t_a(x)=\nabla^2t(x)+2\operatorname{Diag}(a)\succeq0,
\]
so \(\underline t_a\) is convex on \(X\). At every vertex \(v\) of \(X\), all box factors vanish and hence \(\underline t_a(v)=t(v)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding sufficient diagonal curvature through separable box factors gives a convex, vertex-exact underestimator of any smooth term.
knowledge_statements.title: Generic Curvature-Corrected Terms

children.title: Special-Structure Relaxation Candidates
children.top_down_role: Nonconvex terms whose recognized algebraic or compositional structure supports a specialized relaxation.

knowledge_statements.title: Special-Structure Relaxation Candidates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes candidates such as exact convex envelopes or tailored factorable relaxations by validity, convexity, tractability, and dominance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A special-structure relaxation candidate for \(t\) is any tractably representable convex function \(s:X\to\mathbb{R}\) satisfying
\[
s(x)\le t(x)\qquad\text{for every }x\in X.
\]
Candidates may arise from an exact convex envelope, a known convex-hull description, or a valid factorable reformulation. Relative to a generic alphaBB underestimator \(\underline t_a:X\to\mathbb{R}\), the candidate is termwise at least as strong whenever
\[
\underline t_a(x)\le s(x)\le t(x)
\]
for every \(x\in X\). This pointwise dominance implies \(\inf_{x\in Y}s(x)\ge\inf_{x\in Y}\underline t_a(x)\) for every nonempty \(Y\subseteq X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tractable structure-specific convex underestimator is termwise at least as strong when it pointwise dominates the generic alphaBB underestimator.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is a nonempty box and \(t:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is a nonconvex term.
\(s:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is a tractably representable convex function satisfying \(s(x)\le t(x)\) for every \(x\in X\).
\(\underline t_a:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is a generic alphaBB underestimator of \(t\) on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The function \(s\) is a valid structure-exploiting relaxation candidate; if \(s\) dominates \(\underline t_a\) pointwise, it yields no weaker termwise lower bounds.

children.title: Relaxation-Strategy Selection Boundary
children.top_down_role: Structural and computational criteria governing selection between generic curvature correction and specialized treatment.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Strategy Selection Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates pointwise objective-relaxation strength from computational cost; incomparable underestimators require problem-dependent evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Y\subseteq X\) be a nonempty common feasible set, and let \(c:X\to\mathbb{R}\) denote the unchanged portion of a minimization objective. If
\[
s(x)\ge\underline t_a(x)\qquad\text{for every }x\in X,
\]
then
\[
\inf_{x\in Y}\bigl(c(x)+s(x)\bigr)\ge
\inf_{x\in Y}\bigl(c(x)+\underline t_a(x)\bigr),
\]
so replacing \(\underline t_a\) by \(s\) cannot weaken the resulting objective lower bound. If the reverse pointwise inequality holds, the alphaBB underestimator is no weaker. If neither inequality holds throughout \(X\), validity and convexity alone do not order the alternatives; their full-relaxation bounds and solution costs must be assessed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pointwise dominance orders two underestimators used for the same objective term; if they cross, the complete relaxations and their computational costs must be compared.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty, and \(s,\underline t_a:X\to\mathbb{R}\) are tractably representable convex underestimators of the same term \(t:X\to\mathbb{R}\).
\(Y\subseteq X\) is a nonempty common feasible set, and \(c:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is the unchanged portion of the minimization objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pointwise dominance determines the objective-bound ordering; without dominance, termwise validity alone does not determine which complete relaxation gives the stronger bound.

notation.meaning: Common feasible set of the compared relaxations

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g:X\to\mathbb R\), and let \(r_1,r_2:X\to\mathbb R\) satisfy \(r_k(x)\le g(x)\) on \(X\). Define \(F=\{x\in X:g(x)\le0\}\) and \(R_k=\{x\in X:r_k(x)\le0\}\). Then \(F\subseteq R_k\). If \(r_1(x)\ge r_2(x)\) throughout \(X\), then \(R_1\subseteq R_2\). If the underestimators cross, validity alone need not order \(R_1\) and \(R_2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a relaxed inequality, the pointwise larger valid underestimator gives the tighter outer feasible set; crossing underestimators need not yield nested relaxations.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define
\[
F_a(x)=f(x)+\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i^2,
\qquad Q_a(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i^2.
\]
The curvature condition makes both \(F_a\) and \(Q_a\) convex on \(X\), and \(f=F_a-Q_a\) is therefore a difference-of-convex representation. For \(x_i\in[\ell_i,u_i]\), convexity gives \(x_i^2\le(\ell_i+u_i)x_i-\ell_i u_i\). Substituting these secants for \(Q_a\) produces
\[
F_a(x)-\sum_{i=1}^n a_i\bigl((\ell_i+u_i)x_i-\ell_i u_i\bigr)
=f(x)-\sum_{i=1}^n a_i(x_i-\ell_i)(u_i-x_i),
\]
which is the alphaBB underestimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: AlphaBB is a diagonal smooth DC decomposition followed by replacing each convex quadratic component with its secant over the box.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Choosing \(\alpha=\max\{0,-\beta/2\}\) yields a convex separable quadratic underestimator with one common correction coefficient.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses a single spectral curvature bound and the same diagonal correction in every coordinate.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 11. The alphaBB for Box Constrained Twice-Differentiable NLPs: Theory p. 315

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
\alpha=\max\{0,-\beta/2\},
\qquad
\underline f_\alpha(x)=f(x)-\alpha\sum_{i=1}^n(x_i-\ell_i)(u_i-x_i).
\]
Then \(\underline f_\alpha(x)\le f(x)\) on \(X\), because every box factor is nonnegative. Its Hessian satisfies
\[
\nabla^2\underline f_\alpha(x)=\nabla^2f(x)+2\alpha I\succeq(\beta+2\alpha)I\succeq0.
\]
Hence \(\underline f_\alpha\) is convex. This uniform construction uses the same curvature correction in every coordinate and is determined by a global lower bound on the least Hessian eigenvalue.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A common coefficient derived from a lower Hessian eigenvalue bound gives a convex underestimator on the entire box.

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 11. The alphaBB for Box Constrained Twice-Differentiable NLPs: Theory p. 315

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes the exact least uniform coefficient from coefficients based on conservative eigenvalue bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[m:=\min_{x\in X}\lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2f(x)).\] For \(\underline f_\alpha(x)=f(x)-\alpha\sum_i(x_i-\ell_i)(u_i-x_i)\), \[\underline f_\alpha\text{ is convex on }X\iff \alpha\ge\alpha_*:=\max\{0,-m/2\}.\] If only \(\beta\le m\) is known, then \(\max\{0,-\beta/2\}\) is sufficient but may exceed \(\alpha_*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The least common correction is half the magnitude of the worst negative Hessian eigenvalue; conservative bounds can overcorrect.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a compact box with nonempty interior.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha_* = \max\{0,-\tfrac12\min_{x\in X}\lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2f(x))\}\) is the least uniform convexifying coefficient.
knowledge_statements.title: Sharp Uniform Convexification Threshold

children.title: Nonuniform Diagonal Convexifiers
children.top_down_role: Coordinatewise curvature corrections adapted to directional information.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: A global optimization method, alphaBB, for general twice-differentiable constrained NLPs — I
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: A global optimization method, alphaBB, for general twice-differentiable constrained NLPs — I

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The coordinatewise corrected function is a convex underestimator, allowing different curvature compensation in different directions.

notation.meaning: Diagonal matrix with diagonal entries from the vector

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Permits coordinate-dependent corrections certified by a uniform positive-semidefinite Hessian condition over the box.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 11. The alphaBB for Box Constrained Twice-Differentiable NLPs: Theory p. 315

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For coordinatewise coefficients \(a_i\ge0\), define
\[
\underline f_a(x)=f(x)-\sum_{i=1}^n a_i(x_i-\ell_i)(u_i-x_i).
\]
The sign of the box factors gives \(\underline f_a\le f\) throughout \(X\), while differentiation gives
\[
\nabla^2\underline f_a(x)=\nabla^2f(x)+2\operatorname{Diag}(a).
\]
Thus the displayed matrix inequality is precisely a sufficient convexification condition. Unlike a uniform convexifier, the vector \(a\) can assign larger corrections to directions requiring more negative-curvature compensation and smaller corrections to directions already having favorable curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative coefficient per coordinate yields a convex underestimator whenever the corresponding diagonal Hessian shift is positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonuniform Diagonal Convexifiers

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 11. The alphaBB for Box Constrained Twice-Differentiable NLPs: Theory p. 315

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Convexity Condition for a Nonuniform Diagonal Shift
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp convexity characterization for the coordinatewise correction already defined by the seed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=[\ell,u]\) have nonempty interior, let \(f\in C^2\) on a neighborhood of \(X\), and let \(a\in\mathbb R_+^n\). Then \(\underline f_a(x)=f(x)-\sum_i a_i(x_i-\ell_i)(u_i-x_i)\) is convex on \(X\) if and only if \[\nabla^2f(x)+2\operatorname{Diag}(a)\succeq0\qquad\text{for every }x\in X.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The coordinatewise alphaBB model is convex exactly when its shifted Hessian is positive semidefinite throughout the box.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\underline f_a\text{ is convex on }X\iff \nabla^2f(x)+2\operatorname{Diag}(a)\succeq0\ \forall x\in X.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Convexity Condition for a Nonuniform Diagonal Shift

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orders coordinatewise corrections and characterizes monotonicity of the convexifying set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(a,b\in\mathbb R_+^n\) and \(a\le b\) componentwise, then \[\underline f_a(x)-\underline f_b(x)=\sum_i(b_i-a_i)(x_i-\ell_i)(u_i-x_i)\ge0\quad(x\in X).\] Thus \(a\) gives a pointwise tighter underestimator. If \(a\) convexifies \(f\), every \(b\ge a\) also convexifies it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Smaller feasible coordinate corrections give tighter models, while increasing corrections preserves convexity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\underline f_a\ge\underline f_b\) on \(X\), and convexification by \(a\) implies convexification by every \(b\ge a\).
knowledge_statements.title: Coefficientwise Strength and Upward Closure

children.title: Scaled Diagonal Convexifiers
children.top_down_role: Coordinate-scaled diagonal corrections used to redistribute conservatism.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The scaled diagonal correction is a convex underestimator whose coordinate penalties are redistributed according to the positive weights \(d_i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restricts nonuniform coefficients to a positive scaling ray, redistributing correction while retaining a scalar tuning parameter.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 11. The alphaBB for Box Constrained Twice-Differentiable NLPs: Theory p. 315

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given positive coordinate weights \(d_i\), define
\[
\underline f_{\gamma,d}(x)=f(x)-\gamma\sum_{i=1}^n d_i(x_i-\ell_i)(u_i-x_i).
\]
Because \(\gamma d_i\ge0\), this function underestimates \(f\) on \(X\). Furthermore,
\[
\nabla^2\underline f_{\gamma,d}(x)=\nabla^2f(x)+2\gamma\operatorname{Diag}(d)\succeq0,
\]
so it is convex. The effective nonuniform coefficients are \(a_i=\gamma d_i\). Scaling therefore preserves the separable alphaBB form while restricting the correction vector to a prescribed positive ray, which can reflect coordinate scaling or directional curvature information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive coordinate weights redistribute a scalar curvature correction while preserving alphaBB underestimation and convexity.
knowledge_statements.title: Scaled Diagonal Convexifiers

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 11. The alphaBB for Box Constrained Twice-Differentiable NLPs: Theory p. 315

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Least Convexifying Multiplier on a Fixed Scaling Ray
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp scalar threshold for a prescribed positive coordinate scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=\operatorname{Diag}(d)\) for \(d\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\), and define \[m_d:=\min_{x\in X}\lambda_{\min}\!\left(D^{-1/2}\nabla^2f(x)D^{-1/2}\right).\] Then \(\underline f_{\gamma,d}\) is convex on \(X\) exactly when \[\gamma\ge\gamma_*(d):=\max\{0,-m_d/2\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For fixed positive weights, the worst generalized Hessian eigenvalue gives the exact least scalar correction.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a compact box with nonempty interior and \(f\in C^2\) near \(X\).

notation.meaning: Worst generalized Hessian eigenvalue relative to the diagonal scaling
Least convexifying multiplier on the fixed scaling ray

knowledge_statements.title: Least Convexifying Multiplier on a Fixed Scaling Ray

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies the normalization freedom in the weight and multiplier parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(c>0\), \[\underline f_{\gamma,d}=\underline f_{\gamma/c,cd}.\] Hence only \(\gamma d\) determines the underestimator; a normalization of \(d\) is required to identify \(\gamma\) and \(d\) separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rescaling the weights and inversely rescaling the multiplier leaves the scaled convexifier unchanged.
knowledge_statements.title: Scaling-Ray Reparameterization Invariance

children.top_down_role: The roles played by convex underestimators in objective bounding and feasible-set relaxation.

children.title: Objective Underestimators
children.top_down_role: Curvature-based lower models used to generate regional objective bounds.

assumptions_latex: \(X=[\ell,u]\) is nonempty and bounded, and \(f\in C^2\) near \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Minimizing the alphaBB underestimator over any relaxation of the feasible set produces a valid regional lower bound on the original objective minimum.

notation.meaning: Original feasible region inside the box
Relaxed feasible region containing the original region

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Connects pointwise objective underestimation with valid regional lower bounds in deterministic global optimization.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 11. The alphaBB for Box Constrained Twice-Differentiable NLPs: Theory p. 315
9.3 Problems with General Nonconvex Objective Function p. 190

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the convex objective underestimator
\[
\underline f_a(x)=f(x)-\sum_{i=1}^n a_i(x_i-\ell_i)(u_i-x_i).
\]
Then \(\underline f_a(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in X\). If \(F\subseteq R\subseteq X\), where \(F\) is the original feasible region and \(R\) is a relaxation, then
\[
\inf_{x\in R}\underline f_a(x)
\le \inf_{x\in F}\underline f_a(x)
\le \inf_{x\in F}f(x).
\]
Thus the relaxed minimum is a valid regional lower bound; convexity permits its computation by convex optimization when \(R\) is convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimizing a convex alphaBB objective underestimator over an outer feasible relaxation gives a valid lower bound for the original problem.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective Underestimators

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 11. The alphaBB for Box Constrained Twice-Differentiable NLPs: Theory p. 315
9.3 Problems with General Nonconvex Objective Function p. 190

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Contact Certificate for an Exact Regional Objective Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient exactness certificate for the objective-underestimation interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq R\subseteq X\), let \(\underline f\le f\) on \(X\), and suppose \(x^*\in F\) minimizes \(\underline f\) over \(R\) and satisfies \(\underline f(x^*)=f(x^*)\). Then \[\inf_{x\in R}\underline f(x)=f(x^*)=\inf_{x\in F}f(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a relaxed-model minimizer is originally feasible and contacts the true objective, the regional lower bound is exact.
knowledge_statements.title: Contact Certificate for an Exact Regional Objective Bound

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pointwise Dominance Orders Objective Lower Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strength comparison for objective underestimators on a fixed relaxed feasible region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R\) be fixed and let \(\underline f_1,\underline f_2\le f\) on \(R\). If \(\underline f_1(x)\ge\underline f_2(x)\) for every \(x\in R\), then \[\inf_{x\in R}\underline f_1(x)\ge\inf_{x\in R}\underline f_2(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On the same relaxed region, pointwise dominance of objective underestimators implies dominance of their lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.title: Pointwise Dominance Orders Objective Lower Bounds

children.title: Inequality-Constraint Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Direction-sensitive convex relaxations for nonlinear inequalities.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The convex inequality \(\underline g_a(x)\le0\) is an outer relaxation of \(g(x)\le0\) on \(X\).

notation.meaning: Convex alphaBB underestimator of the inequality function

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses underestimation in the correct direction to enlarge a smooth sublevel constraint into a convex outer approximation.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 11. The alphaBB for Box Constrained Twice-Differentiable NLPs: Theory p. 315
9.2 Problems with General Convex Constraints p. 188

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the inequality \(g(x)\le0\), define
\[
\underline g_a(x)=g(x)-\sum_{i=1}^n a_i(x_i-\ell_i)(u_i-x_i).
\]
Since \(\underline g_a(x)\le g(x)\) on \(X\), every point satisfying the original inequality also satisfies \(\underline g_a(x)\le0\). Hence
\[
\{x\in X:g(x)\le0\}\subseteq\{x\in X:\underline g_a(x)\le0\}.
\]
When the diagonal correction makes \(\underline g_a\) convex, its zero sublevel set is convex. Underestimation, rather than overestimation, is therefore the direction required for an outer relaxation of a less-than-or-equal constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a constraint written as g≤0, imposing a convex underestimator of g≤0 gives a convex outer relaxation.
knowledge_statements.title: Inequality-Constraint Relaxations

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 11. The alphaBB for Box Constrained Twice-Differentiable NLPs: Theory p. 315
9.2 Problems with General Convex Constraints p. 188

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Overestimation Can Cut Off Feasible Points in a Less-Than Constraint
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Demonstrates failure of the wrong approximation direction for a less-than-or-equal constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=[-1,1]\), \(g(x)=x\), and \(\overline g(x)=x+1\ge g(x)\). The original constraint \(g(x)\le0\) has feasible set \([-1,0]\), whereas \(\overline g(x)\le0\) has feasible set \(\{-1\}\). Hence an overestimator need not produce an outer relaxation of a less-than constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Using an overestimator in a less-than constraint can remove originally feasible points.
knowledge_statements.title: Overestimation Can Cut Off Feasible Points in a Less-Than Constraint

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extends the direction-sensitive rule to the opposite written orientation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A constraint \(g(x)\ge0\) is equivalent to \(-g(x)\le0\). If \(\underline{(-g)}\le-g\) is convex, then \[\underline{(-g)}(x)\le0\] is a convex outer relaxation of \(g(x)\ge0\). Equivalently, with the concave overestimator \(\overline g=-\underline{(-g)}\ge g\), the relaxation is \(\overline g(x)\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A greater-than inequality is sign-reversed and underapproximated, equivalently relaxed using a concave overestimator of its original left side.
assumptions_latex: \(\underline{(-g)}\) is a convex underestimator of \(-g\) on \(X\).

notation.meaning: Concave overestimator of the original greater-than constraint function

knowledge_statements.title: Sign-Normalized Rule for Greater-Than Inequalities

children.title: Equality-Constraint Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Paired relaxation treatment for nonlinear equalities.

knowledge_statements.title: Equality-Constraint Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relaxes an equality through separate convex underestimators of its two inequality orientations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The equality \(h(x)=0\) is equivalent to the pair \(h(x)\le0\) and \(-h(x)\le0\). Relax each orientation separately:
\[
\underline h(x)\le0,
\qquad
\underline{(-h)}(x)\le0.
\]
If \(h(x)=0\), then \(\underline h(x)\le h(x)=0\) and \(\underline{(-h)}(x)\le-h(x)=0\). Therefore
\[
\{x\in X:h(x)=0\}
\subseteq
\{x\in X:\underline h(x)\le0,\ \underline{(-h)}(x)\le0\}.
\]
Because both underestimators are convex, the set on the right is convex. Correcting only one orientation does not generally relax the full equality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relax an equality by convexifying both h≤0 and −h≤0; their paired sublevel constraints form a convex outer approximation.
assumptions_latex: \(h\in C^2\) on an open neighborhood of a nonempty box \(X=[\ell,u]\subset\mathbb{R}^n\).

\(\underline h:X\to\mathbb{R}\) and \(\underline{(-h)}:X\to\mathbb{R}\) are convex alphaBB underestimators satisfying \(\underline h(x)\le h(x)\) and \(\underline{(-h)}(x)\le-h(x)\) for every \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The paired convex inequalities \(\underline h(x)\le0\) and \(\underline{(-h)}(x)\le0\) form a convex outer relaxation of \(h(x)=0\).

notation.meaning: Convex underestimator of the positive equality side
Convex underestimator of the negated equality side

source_refs.locator: Chapter 11. The alphaBB for Box Constrained Twice-Differentiable NLPs: Theory p. 315

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 11. The alphaBB for Box Constrained Twice-Differentiable NLPs: Theory p. 315

knowledge_statements.statement_title: One-Sided Treatment Gives an Arbitrarily Loose Equality Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shows why both inequality orientations are needed for the intended two-sided equality relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(X=[-1,1]\), let \(h(x)=x\). Retaining only the exact convex inequality \(h(x)\le0\) gives \([-1,0]\), whereas the equality set is \(\{0\}\). Thus one orientation is still an outer relaxation of the equality set, but it loses the opposite-sign restriction and admits every point with \(h(x)<0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Using only one sign of an equality remains outer-valid but can be drastically weaker than the required paired relaxation.
knowledge_statements.title: One-Sided Treatment Gives an Arbitrarily Loose Equality Relaxation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalent Convex Lower–Upper Bracketing of an Equality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expresses the paired-sign construction as a convex lower bound and concave upper bound on the equality function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\underline h\le h\) be convex and let \(\underline{(-h)}\le-h\) be convex. Define \(\overline h:=-\underline{(-h)}\). Then \(\overline h\ge h\), \(\overline h\) is concave, and \[\underline h(x)\le0,\quad\underline{(-h)}(x)\le0\iff\underline h(x)\le0\le\overline h(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The paired-sign equality relaxation is equivalently a convex lower and concave upper bracket containing zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{\underline h\le0,\underline{(-h)}\le0\}=\{\underline h\le0\le\overline h\}\), where \(\overline h=-\underline{(-h)}\ge h\).

notation.meaning: Concave overestimator induced from the underestimator of the negated equality

knowledge_statements.title: Equivalent Convex Lower–Upper Bracketing of an Equality

children.title: Box-Vertex Contact
children.top_down_role: Contact behavior at the vertices selected by the box-anchored perturbation.

knowledge_statements.title: Box-Vertex Contact
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Contact caused solely by vanishing of the box-anchored quadratic perturbation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B=\prod_{i=1}^n[\ell_i,u_i]\) and define \[L_B(x)=f(x)+\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i(\ell_i-x_i)(u_i-x_i).\] Then \[L_B(v)=f(v)\qquad\text{for every }v\in\operatorname{vert}(B).\] This contact property does not require convexity of \(L_B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The box-anchored alphaBB model agrees with the original function at every box vertex, independently of whether the model is convex.

notation.meaning: The set of vertices of the box.

source_refs.locator: 11.2 Convex Lower Bounding Function p. 318

source_witnesses.locator: 11.2 Convex Lower Bounding Function p. 318

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Vertex Value Contact Does Not Imply Tangency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates interpolation at box vertices from first-order contact.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(L_B(x)=f(x)+\sum_i\alpha_i(\ell_i-x_i)(u_i-x_i)\), \[\nabla L_B(x)-\nabla f(x)=\bigl(\alpha_i(2x_i-\ell_i-u_i)\bigr)_{i=1}^n.\] At a vertex \(v\), component \(i\) equals \(-\alpha_i(u_i-\ell_i)\) if \(v_i=\ell_i\) and \(\alpha_i(u_i-\ell_i)\) if \(v_i=u_i\). Thus, on a nondegenerate box, vertex value contact is tangential in coordinate \(i\) only when \(\alpha_i=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: AlphaBB interpolates function values at box vertices but generally has a different gradient there.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_B(v)=f(v)\) does not generally imply \(\nabla L_B(v)=\nabla f(v)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Vertex Value Contact Does Not Imply Tangency

children.title: Interior Underestimation Gap
children.top_down_role: Separation between the original function and the lower model in the box interior.

knowledge_statements.title: Interior Underestimation Gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact pointwise gap for a diagonal box-anchored alphaBB perturbation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \[L_B(x)=f(x)+\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i(\ell_i-x_i)(u_i-x_i),\] define \[g_B(x):=f(x)-L_B(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i(x_i-\ell_i)(u_i-x_i).\] Then \(g_B(x)\ge0\) for every \(x\in B\). Moreover, \(g_B(x)>0\) exactly when at least one index \(i\) satisfies \(\alpha_i>0\) and \(x_i\in(\ell_i,u_i)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The pointwise gap is a sum of nonnegative coordinatewise quadratic gaps and is positive exactly when a positively weighted coordinate is interior.

notation.meaning: The alphaBB model anchored to the box.
Pointwise separation between the function and its model.

source_refs.locator: 11.2 Convex Lower Bounding Function p. 318

source_witnesses.locator: 11.2 Convex Lower Bounding Function p. 318

children.title: Subbox-Contraction Geometry
children.top_down_role: Tightening behavior induced by contraction of the underestimation domain.

knowledge_statements.title: Subbox-Contraction Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise tightening under nested anchors and nonincreasing diagonal correction coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[L_B(x)=f(x)+\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i(\ell_i-x_i)(u_i-x_i)\] and \[L_{B'}(x)=f(x)+\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i'(\ell_i'-x_i)(u_i'-x_i).\] If \(B'\subseteq B\) and \(0\le\alpha_i'\le\alpha_i\) for every \(i\), then \[0\le f(x)-L_{B'}(x)\le f(x)-L_B(x)\qquad(x\in B').\] Box inclusion alone gives no such comparison when the contracted-box coefficients may increase.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On the retained subbox, contraction cannot enlarge the pointwise gap when every contracted-box correction coefficient is nonnegative and no larger than its parent-box coefficient.

notation.meaning: AlphaBB models anchored to the original box and subbox.
Original and contracted diagonal correction coefficients.

source_refs.locator: 11.2 Convex Lower Bounding Function p. 318

source_witnesses.locator: 11.2 Convex Lower Bounding Function p. 318

assumptions_latex: The parent and child coefficients are respectively \(1\) and \(10\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp counterexample to tightening from box inclusion alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\equiv0\), \(B=[0,1]\), \(B'=[1/4,3/4]\), \(\alpha=1\), and \(\alpha'=10\). At \(x=1/2\), \[f(x)-L_B(x)=\tfrac14,\qquad f(x)-L_{B'}(x)=10\left(\tfrac14\right)^2=\tfrac58.\] Thus \(B'\subset B\) but the contracted-box gap is larger.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smaller box can have a worse pointwise AlphaBB gap when its recomputed coefficient increases sufficiently.
knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient Increase Can Defeat Contraction

notation.meaning: Coordinatewise nonnegative AlphaBB gap factors on the parent and child boxes.
Pointwise gaps between the objective and the corresponding AlphaBB models.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact decomposition of the improvement obtained from nested box anchors and nonincreasing AlphaBB coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(q_i^B(x)=(x_i-\ell_i)(u_i-x_i)\) and \(q_i^{B'}(x)=(x_i-\ell_i')(u_i'-x_i)\), let \(g_B=f-L_B=\sum_i\alpha_iq_i^B\) and \(g_{B'}=f-L_{B'}=\sum_i\alpha_i'q_i^{B'}\). If \(B'\subseteq B\) and \(0\leq\alpha_i'\leq\alpha_i\), then for every \(x\in B'\), \[g_B(x)-g_{B'}(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n\left[\alpha_i\bigl(q_i^B(x)-q_i^{B'}(x)\bigr)+(\alpha_i-\alpha_i')q_i^{B'}(x)\right].\] Every summand is nonnegative. Equality holds exactly when both nonnegative terms vanish for every coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The tightening splits exactly into an anchor-contraction contribution and a coefficient-reduction contribution; this also characterizes equality and strict improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Gap Reduction under Subbox Contraction
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Gap Reduction under Subbox Contraction

children.top_down_role: Criteria used to compare valid alphaBB underestimators independently of convexity certification.

children.title: Maximum-Separation Criteria
children.top_down_role: Quality comparisons based on the largest regional underestimation gap.

knowledge_statements.title: Maximum-Separation Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case pointwise criterion for diagonal alphaBB perturbations on a box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a lower model \(L_B\) of \(f\) on \(B\), define \[Q_{\max}(L_B):=\max_{x\in B}\bigl(f(x)-L_B(x)\bigr).\] For \[L_B(x)=f(x)+\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i(\ell_i-x_i)(u_i-x_i),\] one has \[Q_{\max}(L_B)=\frac14\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i(u_i-\ell_i)^2.\] On a fixed function and box, smaller values are preferred under this criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximum-separation quality is the largest pointwise gap on the box; for a diagonal alphaBB model it is one quarter of the weighted sum of squared box widths.

notation.meaning: Worst-case separation criterion on the box.

source_refs.locator: 11.2 Convex Lower Bounding Function p. 318

source_witnesses.locator: 11.2 Convex Lower Bounding Function p. 318

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies every point at which the diagonal alphaBB perturbation attains its worst separation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[G(x)=f(x)-L_B(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i(x_i-\ell_i)(u_i-x_i),\qquad \alpha_i\ge0.\] Then \(G\) is maximized exactly at the points satisfying \[x_i=\frac{\ell_i+u_i}{2}\quad\text{for every }i\text{ with }\alpha_i>0.\] Coordinates with \(\alpha_i=0\) are unrestricted in their intervals. Hence the box midpoint is the unique maximizer exactly when every \(\alpha_i>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The maximum alphaBB gap occurs at the midpoint in every positively corrected coordinate; zero-weight coordinates do not affect the gap.
assumptions_latex: \(\alpha_i\ge0\), and \(L_B\) is the diagonal alphaBB lower model.
knowledge_statements.title: Maximum-Gap Attainment Set

children.title: Average-Separation Criteria
children.top_down_role: Quality comparisons based on aggregate separation over the domain.

knowledge_statements.title: Average-Separation Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform-volume average gap for a diagonal alphaBB perturbation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a lower model \(L_B\) of \(f\) on a positive-volume box \(B\), define \[Q_{\mathrm{avg}}(L_B):=\frac{1}{\operatorname{vol}(B)}\int_B\bigl(f(x)-L_B(x)\bigr)\,dx.\] For \[L_B(x)=f(x)+\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i(\ell_i-x_i)(u_i-x_i),\] one has \[Q_{\mathrm{avg}}(L_B)=\frac16\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i(u_i-\ell_i)^2.\] On a fixed function and box, smaller values are preferred under this criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Average-separation quality is the volume-normalized integral gap; for a diagonal alphaBB model it is one sixth of the weighted sum of squared box widths.

children.title: Optimized Lower-Bound Criteria

knowledge_statements.title: Optimized Lower-Bound Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Model comparison by the solved relaxation value rather than pointwise separation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a continuous lower model \(L:B\to\mathbb R\) on a nonempty compact set \(B\), define \[Q_{\mathrm{LB}}(L):=\min_{x\in B}L(x).\] If \(L(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in B\), then \[Q_{\mathrm{LB}}(L)\le\min_{x\in B}f(x).\] The optimized lower-bound criterion ranks \(L_1\) at least as good as \(L_2\) exactly when \[Q_{\mathrm{LB}}(L_1)\ge Q_{\mathrm{LB}}(L_2).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The optimized lower-bound criterion compares solved relaxations by their attained minimum values, preferring the larger valid lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(L_1,L_2:B\to\mathbb R\) are continuous and satisfy \(L_k(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in B\) and \(k\in\{1,2\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q_{\mathrm{LB}}(L_1)\ge Q_{\mathrm{LB}}(L_2)\) means that \(L_1\) is at least as good under the optimized lower-bound criterion.

notation.meaning: Optimal objective value of the lower relaxation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Optimized-Value Ordering Does Not Imply Pointwise Dominance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shows that optimized lower-bound comparison is strictly coarser than pointwise comparison of lower models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(B=[-1,1]\), let \(f(x)=1\), \(L_1(x)=x\), and \(L_2(x)=-x\). Both models satisfy \(L_k(x)\le f(x)\) on \(B\), and \[Q_{\mathrm{LB}}(L_1)=Q_{\mathrm{LB}}(L_2)=-1.\] Nevertheless, \(L_1(x)>L_2(x)\) for \(x>0\) and \(L_1(x)<L_2(x)\) for \(x<0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two crossing valid lower models can have the same optimized lower bound, so solved-value comparison does not imply pointwise dominance.
knowledge_statements.title: Optimized-Value Ordering Does Not Imply Pointwise Dominance

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extends optimized-value comparison to relaxations having different outer feasible sets and objective lower models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(k\in\{1,2\}\), let \(R_k\) be a nonempty relaxation set and let \(L_k:R_k\to\mathbb R\) have a finite infimum \(q_k=\inf_{x\in R_k}L_k(x)\). If \(R_1\subseteq R_2\) and \(L_1(x)\ge L_2(x)\) for every \(x\in R_1\), then \[q_1\ge q_2.\] Thus simultaneous feasible-set tightening and objective-model dominance are sufficient for an optimized lower-bound ordering. The converse need not hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relaxation with a contained feasible set and a pointwise larger objective lower model has an optimized lower bound no smaller than the other relaxation's.
assumptions_latex: \(L_1\ge L_2\) on \(R_1\), and both stated infima are finite.

notation.meaning: Optimized objective value of relaxation k

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An interval-Hessian curvature model for \(f\) on \(B\) is a pair of symmetric matrices \(\underline H,\overline H\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) satisfying \(\underline H_{ij}\le\overline H_{ij}\) and \[\underline H_{ij}\le\frac{\partial^2 f}{\partial x_i\partial x_j}(x)\le\overline H_{ij}\qquad(x\in B,\ 1\le i,j\le n).\] It represents the symmetric interval family \[[\underline H,\overline H]:=\{H=H^{\mathsf T}:\underline H_{ij}\le H_{ij}\le\overline H_{ij}\},\] which contains every regional Hessian \(\nabla^2 f(x)\), although it may also contain matrices not jointly realizable by any \(x\in B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An interval-Hessian model encloses every regional Hessian entrywise, while possibly losing dependencies among entries.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smallest entrywise interval matrix containing all Hessians on a compact box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty compact box and let \(f\in C^2\) on a neighborhood of \(B\). Define \[\underline H_{ij}=\min_{x\in B}\frac{\partial^2f}{\partial x_i\partial x_j}(x),\qquad \overline H_{ij}=\max_{x\in B}\frac{\partial^2f}{\partial x_i\partial x_j}(x).\] Then \([\underline H,\overline H]\) contains every \(\nabla^2f(x)\) and is contained in every entrywise interval matrix containing all such Hessians.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Entrywise Hessian extrema form the unique smallest entrywise interval hull of the regional Hessian image.
assumptions_latex: \(f\in C^2\) on an open neighborhood of \(B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: [\underline H,\overline H]\text{ is the smallest entrywise interval enclosure of }\{\nabla^2f(x):x\in B\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dependency Loss under Entrywise Hull Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A coupled matrix family can have a strictly larger entrywise interval hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(H(t)=\operatorname{diag}(t,-t)\) with \(t\in[-1,1]\), the two diagonal entries are coupled. Its entrywise interval hull permits \(\operatorname{diag}(-1,-1)\), although no common value of \(t\) produces that matrix. Thus independently varying interval entries can introduce curvature matrices absent from the parametric family.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A parametric-Hessian curvature model on \(B\) consists of a parameter set \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^m\), a symmetric matrix-valued map \(H:P\to\mathbb S^n\), and a selection map \(p:B\to P\) such that \[\nabla^2 f(x)=H(p(x))\qquad\text{for every }x\in B.\] An outer model may instead require only \(\nabla^2 f(x)\in\{H(p):p\in P\}\). Shared parameters appearing in multiple entries preserve their stated algebraic dependencies, so curvature certification is performed over the coupled family \(H(P)\), not over the entrywise interval hull unless that relaxation is explicitly chosen.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform spectral condition for alphaBB convexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A scalar Hessian-eigenvalue certificate for convexifying a twice continuously differentiable function on a box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let B=\prod_{i=1}^n[x_i^L,x_i^U] and f\in C^2(B). If \lambda_i^f(x), i=1,\ldots,n, are the eigenvalues of \nabla^2f(x) and \alpha\geq\max\left\{0,\sup_{x\in B,\,1\leq i\leq n}\left(-\tfrac12\lambda_i^f(x)\right)\right\}, then \mathcal L(x)=f(x)+\alpha\sum_{i=1}^n(x_i^L-x_i)(x_i^U-x_i) is convex on B.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a twice continuously differentiable function on a box, adding the standard alphaBB separable quadratic correction produces a convex function whenever the scalar correction parameter dominates zero and one half of the worst negative Hessian eigenvalue throughout the box.

knowledge_statements.title: Minimum-Eigenvalue Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform least-eigenvalue certificate for convexity of the corrected model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[L_B(x)=f(x)+\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i(\ell_i-x_i)(u_i-x_i)\] and \(D=2\operatorname{diag}(\alpha)\). A number \(\underline\lambda\in\mathbb R\) satisfying \[\underline\lambda\le\inf_{x\in B}\lambda_{\min}\bigl(\nabla^2f(x)+D\bigr)\] is a valid minimum-eigenvalue lower certificate. If \(\underline\lambda\ge0\), then \(L_B\) is convex on \(B\). If \(\underline\lambda<0\), this certificate is inconclusive about convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative rigorous lower bound on the smallest corrected-Hessian eigenvalue certifies convexity of the alphaBB model throughout the box; a negative lower bound is inconclusive.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is twice continuously differentiable on an open neighborhood of \(B\).

knowledge_statements.title: Diagonal-Dominance Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scaled rowwise diagonal-dominance certificate applied uniformly to corrected Hessians.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal M\subseteq\mathbb S^n\) and let \(d\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\). If every \(M\in\mathcal M\) satisfies \[M_{ii}\ge\sum_{j\ne i}|M_{ij}|\frac{d_j}{d_i}\qquad(i=1,\ldots,n),\] then \[M\succeq0\qquad\text{for every }M\in\mathcal M.\] In particular, applying the inequalities uniformly to \(M(x)=\nabla^2f(x)+2\operatorname{diag}(\alpha)\) certifies convexity of the corresponding alphaBB model on its box.

children.title: Interval-Matrix Positive-Semidefiniteness Certificates
children.top_down_role: Certificates applying uniformly to a symmetric interval-matrix family.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Vertex Characterization of Uniform Interval-Matrix Semidefiniteness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite characterization for an independently parameterized symmetric interval family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal H\subseteq\mathbb S^n\) be formed by independently choosing every upper-triangular entry \(H_{ij}\in[\underline H_{ij},\overline H_{ij}]\) and imposing \(H_{ji}=H_{ij}\). Let \(\mathcal V\) contain the endpoint vertex matrices obtained by choosing each nondegenerate independent entry at one endpoint. Then every \(H\in\mathcal H\) is positive semidefinite if and only if every \(V\in\mathcal V\) is positive semidefinite. With \(q\) nondegenerate independent intervals, exhaustive testing requires at most \(2^q\) PSD tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An independently parameterized symmetric interval family is uniformly positive semidefinite exactly when all endpoint vertex matrices are positive semidefinite, though exhaustive testing is exponential.
assumptions_latex: Upper-triangular entries vary independently over closed intervals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\forall H\in\mathcal H,\ H\succeq0)\Longleftrightarrow(\forall V\in\mathcal V,\ V\succeq0)\).

notation.meaning: Number of nondegenerate independent entry intervals.

knowledge_statements.title: Vertex Characterization of Uniform Interval-Matrix Semidefiniteness

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal H=[C-R,C+R]\subseteq\mathbb S^n\) is a symmetric interval family.
\(R\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is entrywise nonnegative and symmetric.

notation.meaning: Spectral radius of the radius matrix.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Midpoint-radius sufficient certificate for an entire symmetric interval family.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Write each member as \(H=C+E\), where \(E=E^{\mathsf T}\) and \(|E_{ij}|\le R_{ij}\). For every \(z\in\mathbb R^n\), \[|z^{\mathsf T}Ez|\le |z|^{\mathsf T}R|z|\le\rho(R)\|z\|_2^2.\] Therefore \[z^{\mathsf T}Hz\ge\bigl(\lambda_{\min}(C)-\rho(R)\bigr)\|z\|_2^2.\] The computable inequality \(\lambda_{\min}(C)\ge\rho(R)\) consequently certifies \(H\succeq0\) for every \(H\in\mathcal H\). Failure of this sufficient test does not establish that the interval family contains an indefinite matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An interval family is uniformly positive semidefinite when the midpoint's least eigenvalue dominates the spectral radius of its entrywise radius matrix.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact positive-semidefiniteness reduction through a positive definite pivot block.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the symmetric block matrix \[M=\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\B^{\mathsf T}&C\end{pmatrix}\] with \(A\succ0\), positive semidefiniteness is characterized by \[M\succeq0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad C-B^{\mathsf T}A^{-1}B\succeq0.\] Thus a curvature certificate may first verify a positive definite principal block and then certify the lower-dimensional Schur complement. Repeating this reduction gives a recursive refinement. For a regional Hessian family, the block and Schur-complement conditions must hold rigorously for every admissible matrix; checking only a midpoint matrix does not certify the full family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive definite pivot block reduces positive-semidefiniteness to its Schur complement, enabling recursive and potentially tighter curvature certification.
knowledge_statements.title: Schur-Complement Refinement Certificates

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact positive-semidefiniteness reduction when the pivot block may be singular.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(M=\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\B^{\mathsf T}&C\end{pmatrix}\in\mathbb S^n\), \[M\succeq0\Longleftrightarrow A\succeq0,\ (I-AA^{\dagger})B=0,\ C-B^{\mathsf T}A^{\dagger}B\succeq0.\] Thus a singular positive-semidefinite pivot is admissible only when every column of \(B\) belongs to \(\operatorname{range}(A)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A singular positive-semidefinite pivot requires the coupling block to lie in its range and uses the Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse.

children.title: Perturbation-Sign Validity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sign condition ensuring that the standard alphaBB perturbation lowers the objective throughout a finite box.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 11. The alphaBB for Box Constrained Twice-Differentiable NLPs: Theory p. 315

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\in\mathbb N\), let \(X=\prod_{i=1}^n[\ell_i,u_i]\) with \(-\infty<\ell_i\le u_i<\infty\), let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\), and let \(\alpha_i\ge0\) for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\). Define \(L:X\to\mathbb R\) by \(L(x)=f(x)+\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i(\ell_i-x_i)(u_i-x_i)\). Then \((\ell_i-x_i)(u_i-x_i)\le0\) for every \(x\in X\) and every \(i\), and \(L(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a finite box, each nonnegative alpha coefficient multiplies a nonpositive box factor, and the alphaBB lower model does not exceed the objective anywhere on the box.
knowledge_statements.title: Perturbation-Sign Validity

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 11. The alphaBB for Box Constrained Twice-Differentiable NLPs: Theory p. 315

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessity and sufficiency of nonnegative coefficients for the classical separable perturbation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\prod_{i=1}^n[\ell_i,u_i]\) have finite endpoints and define \(p_\alpha(x)=\sum_i\alpha_i(\ell_i-x_i)(u_i-x_i)\). Then \(p_\alpha(x)\le0\) for every \(x\in X\) if and only if \(\alpha_i\ge0\) for every nondegenerate coordinate \(i\) with \(\ell_i<u_i\). Coefficients on fixed coordinates are immaterial. If \(\alpha_j<0\) and \(\ell_j<u_j\), choosing \(x_j\) strictly between its endpoints and every other coordinate at an endpoint gives \(p_\alpha(x)>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative alpha coefficients are necessary and sufficient for the classical perturbation to be nonpositive throughout a finite box, apart from fixed coordinates.
knowledge_statements.title: Sharp Coefficient-Sign Condition

children.title: Box-Anchoring Validity
children.top_down_role: The dependence of lower-model validity and contact on finite coordinate bounds.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in X\), and \(L(v)=f(v)\) for every \(v\in\prod_{i=1}^n\{\ell_i,u_i\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary contact and underestimation supplied by the finite-box alphaBB perturbation.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 11. The alphaBB for Box Constrained Twice-Differentiable NLPs: Theory p. 315

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\in\mathbb N\), let \(X=\prod_{i=1}^n[\ell_i,u_i]\) with finite coordinate bounds, let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\), and let \(\alpha_i\ge0\) for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\). Define \(L:X\to\mathbb R\) by \(L(x)=f(x)+\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i(\ell_i-x_i)(u_i-x_i)\). Then \(L(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in X\). The \(i\)-th perturbation term is zero whenever \(x_i\in\{\ell_i,u_i\}\), and \(L(v)=f(v)\) for every vertex \(v\in\prod_{i=1}^n\{\ell_i,u_i\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a finite box, the alphaBB perturbation is nonpositive, each coordinate term vanishes on its two coordinate faces, and the lower model equals the objective at every box vertex.
knowledge_statements.title: Box-Anchoring Validity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Domain boundary for the classical endpoint-anchored quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The classical factor \((\ell_i-x_i)(u_i-x_i)\) defines a finite real-valued endpoint-anchored quadratic only when both \(\ell_i\) and \(u_i\) are finite. If either endpoint is infinite, this formula and its two-endpoint contact assertion are undefined; a finite enclosing box or a different perturbation is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The standard box-anchored alphaBB quadratic requires two finite coordinate endpoints and does not directly extend to an unbounded coordinate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \ell_i,u_i\in\mathbb R\text{ are required for the classical endpoint-anchored factor.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Vertex characterization of the minimum interval-Hessian eigenvalue
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An exact reduction of the least eigenvalue over a symmetric interval Hessian family to finitely many endpoint matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \([A]=([\underline a_{ij},\bar a_{ij}])\) be a symmetric interval Hessian family, and let \(S=\{s\in\{-1,1\}^n:s_1=1\}\). For each \(s\in S\), define the symmetric vertex matrix \(A^s=(a_{ij}^s)\in[A]\) by \[a_{ij}^s=\begin{cases}\underline a_{ii},&i=j,\\ \underline a_{ij},&i\ne j\text{ and }s_is_j=1,\\ \bar a_{ij},&i\ne j\text{ and }s_is_j=-1.\end{cases}\] Since \(|S|=2^{n-1}\), these are the sign-pattern vertex matrices, and \[\min_{A\in[A]}\lambda_{\min}(A)=\min_{s\in S}\lambda_{\min}(A^s).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The minimum eigenvalue over a symmetric interval Hessian family equals the smallest eigenvalue among 2^(n−1) endpoint matrices selected by the possible coordinate-sign patterns.
assumptions_latex: [A]=([\underline a_{ij},\bar a_{ij}])\text{ is a symmetric interval Hessian family}
\{A^s:s\in S\}\text{ are the stated sign-pattern vertex matrices}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex underestimation of a twice-differentiable function over a bounded box using one scalar αBB parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B=\prod_{k=1}^{K}[t_k^L,t_k^U]\), let \(V\) be twice differentiable on a neighborhood of \(B\), and define
\[
\mathcal L(t)=V(t)+\alpha\sum_{k=1}^{K}(t_k^L-t_k)(t_k^U-t_k).
\]
If
\[
\alpha\geq\max\left\{0,-\frac12\min_{t\in B}\lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2V(t))\right\},
\]
then \(\mathcal L\) is convex on \(B\) and \(\mathcal L(t)\leq V(t)\) for every \(t\in B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a bounded box, the uniform scalar αBB correction produces a convex underestimator when α is nonnegative and is at least negative one half of the smallest Hessian eigenvalue over the box.
assumptions_latex: V\text{ is twice differentiable on a neighborhood of }B
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal L\text{ is convex on }B\quad\text{and}\quad\mathcal L(t)\leq V(t)\ \forall t\in B.

knowledge_statements.title: Natural Interval Hessian Enclosures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Entrywise interval extension of the symbolic Hessian over a box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\in C^2(U)\) on an open set \(U\supset X\), where \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) is a box. For each Hessian entry, evaluate a chosen symbolic expression for \(\partial_{ij}^2f\) by natural interval arithmetic on \(X\), obtaining \([H_{ij}](X)\). After intersecting paired off-diagonal evaluations when necessary, form the symmetric interval matrix \([H](X)=([H_{ij}](X))\). Inclusion isotonicity gives \(\nabla^2f(x)\in[H](X)\) entrywise for every \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Natural interval evaluation of every second-derivative expression produces an entrywise interval matrix containing every Hessian attained on the box.
assumptions_latex: All interval operations are inclusion-isotone and defined on \(X\).

notation.meaning: natural interval extension of the second derivative

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Repeated-Variable Dependency in a Natural Hessian Extension
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar example showing strict overestimation by natural evaluation of a Hessian expression.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=x^4/12\) on \(X=[-1,1]\). Then \(f''(x)=x^2\) has exact range \([0,1]\). If the algebraically identical expression \(x\cdot x\) is evaluated by ordinary interval multiplication, its natural interval value is \(X\cdot X=[-1,1]\). Hence \[\operatorname{range}(f'',X)=[0,1]\subsetneq[-1,1]=X\cdot X.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluating the Hessian expression x times x on [-1,1] gives [-1,1], although its exact range is [0,1], demonstrating dependency overestimation.
assumptions_latex: The expression is evaluated as \(x\cdot x\) by ordinary interval multiplication.

notation.meaning: ordinary interval product of two occurrences of the same interval

knowledge_statements.title: Centered Hessian Enclosures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mean-value Hessian enclosure expanded about a selected point, commonly the box midpoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\in C^3(U)\), let \(X\subset U\) be a box, and choose \(c\in X\). Suppose interval extensions \([T_{ijk}](X)\) enclose \(\partial_{ijk}^3f(x)\) for all \(x\in X\). The centered enclosure has entries \([H_{ij}]_c(X)=\partial_{ij}^2f(c)+\sum_{k=1}^n[T_{ijk}](X)(X_k-c_k)\). The multivariate mean-value theorem implies \(\partial_{ij}^2f(x)\in[H_{ij}]_c(X)\) for every \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expanding each Hessian entry from a center and enclosing its third derivatives yields a valid regional Hessian enclosure.
assumptions_latex: \(f\in C^3(U)\) on an open neighborhood of \(X\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: First-Order Width Consistency of Centered Hessian Enclosures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diameter-dependent consistency under uniformly bounded third-derivative interval enclosures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \([T_{ijk}](X)\subseteq[-M_{ijk},M_{ijk}]\) and choose \(c\in X\). The radius of the centered enclosure entry \((i,j)\) is at most
\[
\sum_k M_{ijk}\max\{|\ell_k-c_k|,|u_k-c_k|\}.
\]
Consequently, along contracting boxes, every entry width tends to zero at least linearly in the box diameter whenever the \(M_{ijk}\) remain uniformly bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With uniformly bounded third-derivative interval enclosures, centered Hessian enclosure widths vanish linearly as the box contracts.
assumptions_latex: \(f\in C^3\) on neighborhoods of the boxes.

notation.meaning: Uniform magnitude bound for the complete third-derivative interval enclosure.

knowledge_statements.title: First-Order Width Consistency of Centered Hessian Enclosures

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactness of the centered construction when the zero third derivatives are enclosed exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(f\) is quadratic on a neighborhood of \(X\) and each third-derivative enclosure is evaluated as \([T_{ijk}](X)=\{0\}\), then \(\nabla^2f(x)=\nabla^2f(c)\) for every \(x\in X\). Consequently,
\[
[H]_c(X)=\{\nabla^2f(c)\}
\]
for every \(c\in X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a quadratic function, exact zero enclosures of the third derivatives make the centered Hessian enclosure equal to the constant Hessian.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is quadratic on a neighborhood of \(X\).
knowledge_statements.title: Exactness for Quadratic Functions

knowledge_statements.title: Taylor Hessian Enclosures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Second-order Taylor enclosure of Hessian entries with interval remainder.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\in C^4(U)\), let \(X\subset U\) be a box, and choose \(c\in X\). If \([Q_{ijkm}](X)\) encloses \(\partial_{ijkm}^4f\) on \(X\), define \([H_{ij}]_{T,c}(X)=\partial_{ij}^2f(c)+\sum_k\partial_{ijk}^3f(c)(X_k-c_k)+\frac12\sum_{k,m}[Q_{ijkm}](X)(X_k-c_k)(X_m-c_m)\). Taylor's theorem with interval remainder yields \(\partial_{ij}^2f(x)\in[H_{ij}]_{T,c}(X)\) for all \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Taylor expansion of each Hessian entry, with interval-bounded fourth-derivative remainder, encloses every Hessian on the box.
assumptions_latex: \(f\in C^4(U)\) on an open neighborhood of \(X\).

notation.meaning: Taylor Hessian enclosure about the expansion point

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Entrywise magnitude bound for the fourth-derivative remainder in a Taylor Hessian enclosure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r_k=\max_{x_k\in X_k}|x_k-c_k|\) and suppose \(|\partial_{ijkm}^4f(x)|\le M_{ijkm}\) on \(X\). For every \(x\in X\), the remainder \(R_{ij}(x)=\partial_{ij}^2f(x)-\partial_{ij}^2f(c)-\sum_k\partial_{ijk}^3f(c)(x_k-c_k)\) satisfies \[|R_{ij}(x)|\le\frac12\sum_{k,m}M_{ijkm}r_kr_m.\] Consequently, under proportional contraction of all radii with uniformly bounded \(M_{ijkm}\), this remainder bound contracts quadratically.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform fourth-derivative bounds give a quadratic-in-radius error bound for every Taylor-expanded Hessian entry.

notation.meaning: maximum coordinate displacement from the expansion point

knowledge_statements.title: Expansion-Point Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependence of centered enclosure width on the chosen expansion point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the centered enclosure \([H_{ij}]_c(X)=\partial_{ij}^2f(c)+\sum_k[T_{ijk}](X)(X_k-c_k)\), its interval width satisfies \(\operatorname{wid}([H_{ij}]_c(X))\le\sum_k\operatorname{wid}([T_{ijk}](X)(X_k-c_k))\). Thus changing \(c\) changes both the point Hessian and the dependency structure of the interval terms. For a fixed symmetric box and bounds independent of \(c\), choosing the midpoint minimizes every radius \(\max_{x_k\in X_k}|x_k-c_k|\), although it need not minimize the final enclosure after dependency and cancellation effects.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The expansion point changes enclosure widths; the midpoint minimizes coordinate radii, but dependency and cancellation can make another point produce a tighter final enclosure.
assumptions_latex: The centered enclosure is well defined on the box \(X\).
The stated midpoint conclusion uses derivative bounds held fixed as \(c\) varies.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The enclosure depends on \(c\), and the midpoint minimizes all coordinate displacement radii under fixed derivative bounds.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The coordinate-radius statement is plausible and carefully qualified, but the record supplies no citation for the specialized claims about enclosure width, dependency, cancellation, and expansion-point choice. Source support is required before deciding whether this exact formulation is reliable.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Vertex Certification for Affine Parametric Hessian Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite least-eigenvalue reduction for an affine symmetric matrix over a box of independent parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H(p)=H_0+\sum_{k=1}^m p_kH_k\) be symmetric and let \(P=\prod_{k=1}^m[\underline p_k,\overline p_k]\). Then \[\min_{p\in P}\lambda_{\min}(H(p))=\min_{v\in\operatorname{vert}(P)}\lambda_{\min}(H(v)).\] Thus evaluation at the at most \(2^m\) parameter-box vertices gives an exact least-eigenvalue certificate for the full independent affine family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The worst smallest eigenvalue of an affine symmetric matrix over an independent parameter box occurs at a vertex, giving an exact exponentially sized certificate.
assumptions_latex: The parameters range independently over the box \(P\).
knowledge_statements.title: Vertex Certification for Affine Parametric Hessian Families

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Construction from Shared Scalar Hessian Factors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Construction of an affine parametric Hessian enclosure when regional Hessians depend affinely on bounded shared scalar quantities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(\nabla^2 f(x)=H_0+\sum_{k=1}^m\theta_k(x)H_k\) for every \(x\in X\), where the \(H_k\) are symmetric and \(\theta_k(X)\subseteq[\underline p_k,\overline p_k]\). Then \(\mathcal H_P=\{H_0+\sum_{k=1}^m p_kH_k:p_k\in[\underline p_k,\overline p_k]\}\) contains every Hessian on \(X\). Reusing each parameter \(p_k\) in all entries affected by \(H_k\) preserves that within-factor dependence. Independent interval bounds may enlarge the true joint range of \((\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_m)\), so spectral certification for \(\mathcal H_P\) can be conservative for the actual Hessian range.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bound the shared scalar factors in an affine Hessian formula and retain each factor as one common interval parameter; this gives a valid enclosure, though independent factor bounds may retain extra parameter combinations.
knowledge_statements.title: Construction from Shared Scalar Hessian Factors
Linear Parametric Hessian Enclosures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine matrix enclosure retaining parameter dependence shared across Hessian entries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A linear parametric Hessian enclosure on \(X\) is a family \(\mathcal H_P=\{H_0+\sum_{k=1}^m p_kH_k:p_k\in[\underline p_k,\overline p_k]\}\) of symmetric matrices such that, for every \(x\in X\), there exists one common parameter vector \(p(x)\) with \(\nabla^2f(x)=H_0+\sum_kp_k(x)H_k\). Unlike an entrywise interval matrix, the same parameters occur simultaneously in all affected entries, preserving their algebraic dependence. Hence \(\{\nabla^2f(x):x\in X\}\subseteq\mathcal H_P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine family with shared interval parameters encloses all regional Hessians while retaining dependence among entries that entrywise intervals discard.
assumptions_latex: Every regional Hessian admits the stated common-parameter representation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and shared-parameter formulation fit the leaf, but no source is supplied for the asserted regional Hessian representation or its use as an alternative to entrywise interval matrices.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical trace and Frobenius-norm bound for the smallest eigenvalue of a symmetric matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a real symmetric \(n\times n\) matrix \(H\), let \(\mu=\operatorname{tr}(H)/n\) and \(S=\|H\|_F^2-\operatorname{tr}(H)^2/n\). Then \[\lambda_{\min}(H)\ge\mu-\sqrt{\frac{n-1}{n}S}.\] A validated lower bound on the displayed expression over a regional Hessian family is therefore a uniform least-eigenvalue bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The trace and Frobenius norm give a classical lower bound on the smallest eigenvalue that can be evaluated rigorously over a regional family.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real symmetric \(n\times n\) matrix.
Regional use requires a validated lower bound on the displayed scalar expression.

notation.meaning: sum of squared eigenvalue deviations from their mean

knowledge_statements.title: Trace–Frobenius Least-Eigenvalue Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform classical eigenvalue bound obtained from absolute entry bounds and induced matrix norms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal H\) be a family of real symmetric matrices with \(|H_{ij}|\le r_{ij}\) for every \(H\in\mathcal H\). Define \(R_\infty=\max_i\sum_jr_{ij}\) and \(R_1=\max_j\sum_ir_{ij}\). Then \[\lambda_{\min}(H)\ge-\sqrt{R_1R_\infty}\qquad(H\in\mathcal H).\] For symmetric entry bounds, \(R_1=R_\infty\), so \(\lambda_{\min}(H)\ge-R_\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Absolute entry bounds yield a uniform least-eigenvalue bound through standard induced-matrix-norm inequalities.
assumptions_latex: Every matrix in \(\mathcal H\) is real and symmetric.

notation.meaning: uniform column-sum and row-sum absolute bounds

knowledge_statements.title: Induced-Norm Eigenvalue Lower Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pairwise classical eigenvalue bound complementary to dedicated Gershgorin variants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a real symmetric matrix \(H=(h_{ij})\), define \(R_i=\sum_{k\ne i}|h_{ik}|\). Every eigenvalue belongs to a Brauer Cassini oval, and hence \[\lambda_{\min}(H)\ge\min_{i<j}\frac{h_{ii}+h_{jj}-\sqrt{(h_{ii}-h_{jj})^2+4R_iR_j}}2.\] Validated regional bounds on the diagonal entries and row radii therefore yield a uniform lower bound for a regional symmetric matrix family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Brauer's pairwise Cassini-oval inequality supplies a classical least-eigenvalue bound from diagonal entries and off-diagonal row radii.
assumptions_latex: Regional use requires validated bounds on every displayed diagonal and row-radius quantity.

notation.meaning: absolute off-diagonal row sum for row i

Classical Matrix Eigenvalue Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform regional eigenvalue bounds obtained from entrywise matrix inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \([H]=([\underline h_{ij},\overline h_{ij}])\) be a symmetric interval matrix enclosing every Hessian on \(X\), and set \(r_{ij}=\max\{|\underline h_{ij}|,|\overline h_{ij}|\}\) for \(i
e j\). Gershgorin's theorem gives the uniform lower bound \(\lambda_{\min}(
abla^2f(x))\ge\min_i\{\underline h_{ii}-\sum_{j
e i}r_{ij}\}\) for every \(x\in X\). Therefore any uniform alphaBB shift at least the negative part of one half of this bound makes the shifted Hessian positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Applying Gershgorin inequalities to a regional interval Hessian gives a uniform lower eigenvalue bound and therefore a valid uniform alphaBB curvature shift.
assumptions_latex: \([H]\) is symmetric and encloses \(\nabla^2f(x)\) for every \(x\in X\).
The alphaBB perturbation contributes \(2\alpha I\) to the Hessian.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Preconditioned H-matrix certificate for interval positive definiteness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symmetric interval matrices with a positive-definite modified midpoint preconditioner.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \([G]\) be symmetric, let \(\widetilde G_M\) be its modified midpoint matrix, and set \(C=\widetilde G_M^{-1}\). If \(\widetilde G_M\succ0\) and \(C[G]\) is an H-matrix, then \([G]\) is positive definite; equivalently, \(G\succ0\) for every \(G\in[G]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetric interval matrix is positive definite if its modified midpoint is positive definite and preconditioning the interval matrix by the inverse modified midpoint produces an H-matrix.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: The extract asserts this from continuity and symmetry alone. The conclusion requires the smallest eigenvalue of A(x) to be uniformly bounded below, as occurs when X is compact; that condition is not explicit in the extracted lemma.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A:X\to\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be continuous and symmetric. Then there exists \(\alpha_0>0\) such that, for every \(\alpha\geq\alpha_0\), \(B(x)=A(x)+\alpha I\) is positive definite for every \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous symmetric matrix-valued function can be made uniformly positive definite on X by adding a sufficiently large scalar multiple of the identity, subject to a uniform lower bound on its smallest eigenvalue.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Gershgorin lower bound for a symmetric interval matrix
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform lower bound on the minimum eigenvalue of real symmetric matrices represented by an interval matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \([A]=([\underline a_{ij},\overline a_{ij}])\) be a real symmetric interval matrix. For every real symmetric \(A\in[A]\),
\[
\lambda_{\min}(A)\geq
\min_i\left\{\underline a_{ii}-\sum_{j\ne i}\max\bigl(|\underline a_{ij}|,|\overline a_{ij}|\bigr)\right\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every real symmetric matrix in the interval family has minimum eigenvalue at least the smallest lower diagonal endpoint minus the largest possible absolute off-diagonal row sum.
assumptions_latex: [A]=([\underline a_{ij},\overline a_{ij}])\text{ is a real symmetric interval matrix}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Mori–Kokame eigenvalue bound and E-matrix comparison
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A least-eigenvalue lower bound for a symmetric interval-matrix family and the stated comparison with the diagonal E-matrix bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \([A]=[\underline A,\bar A]\) be a symmetric interval-matrix family. For every symmetric \(A\in[A]\), \[\lambda_{\min}(A)\geq \lambda_{\min}(\underline A)-\rho(\bar A-\underline A).\] If \(A_M=(\underline A+\bar A)/2\) and \(\Delta A=(\bar A-\underline A)/2\), the comparison criterion for the E-matrix method with \(E=\operatorname{diag}(\Delta A)\) is \[\lambda_{\min}(\underline A)-\lambda_{\min}(A_M)\leq\rho(\Delta A).\] This inequality holds, so that E-matrix bound is at least as good as the Mori–Kokame bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every symmetric matrix in the interval family has minimum eigenvalue at least the minimum eigenvalue of the lower endpoint matrix minus the spectral radius of the interval width. The stated comparison criterion always holds, making the diagonal E-matrix bound no worse than the Mori–Kokame bound.

knowledge_statements.title: Midpoint–Radius Spectral Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral enclosure based on the midpoint and radius matrices of a symmetric interval Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the symmetric interval matrix \([H]=[H_c-H_\Delta,H_c+H_\Delta]\) enclose all Hessians on \(X\), where \(H_\Delta\ge0\) entrywise. Every \(H\in[H]\) can be written \(H=H_c+E\) with \(|E|\le H_\Delta\). Since \(\|E\|_2\le\rho(H_\Delta)\), Weyl's inequality yields \(\lambda_{\min}(H)\ge\lambda_{\min}(H_c)-\rho(H_\Delta)\). Consequently this expression is a uniform lower bound for \(\lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2f(x))\) on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The midpoint's smallest eigenvalue minus the radius matrix's spectral radius uniformly bounds the smallest eigenvalue of every enclosed Hessian.
assumptions_latex: \([H]\) is a symmetric interval matrix enclosing every regional Hessian.
\(H_c\) and \(H_\Delta\) are its midpoint and nonnegative radius matrices.

notation.meaning: spectral radius of the radius matrix

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dependency Conservatism of the Radius-Matrix Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine one-parameter family showing strict loss after replacement by an entrywise interval hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[H(t)=\begin{pmatrix}t&t\\t&-t\end{pmatrix},\qquad t\in[-1,1].\] The exact family bound is \(\min_t\lambda_{\min}(H(t))=-\sqrt2\). Its entrywise interval hull has midpoint \(H_c=0\) and radius matrix \(H_\Delta=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}\), so the midpoint-radius certificate is \(-\rho(H_\Delta)=-2\). Therefore \[-2< -\sqrt2,\] demonstrating strict conservatism caused by discarded shared-parameter dependence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A correlated one-parameter family has exact worst eigenvalue minus square root of two, whereas its midpoint-radius interval hull gives only minus two.
assumptions_latex: The family is replaced by its entrywise interval hull before applying the midpoint-radius bound.
