knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform minimum-eigenvalue bound for symmetric interval matrices using modified midpoint-radius data and an arbitrary symmetric shift.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \([A]\) be a real symmetric interval matrix with modified midpoint matrix \(\widetilde A_M\) and modified radius matrix \(\widetilde{\Delta A}\). For every real symmetric matrix \(E\) and every symmetric \(A\in[A]\),
\[
\lambda_{\min}(A)\geq\lambda_{\min}(\widetilde A_M+E)-\rho\bigl(\widetilde{\Delta A}+|E|\bigr),
\]
where \(|E|\) is taken componentwise and \(\rho\) denotes spectral radius.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For any symmetric shift, the minimum eigenvalue of every symmetric matrix in the interval is bounded below by the minimum eigenvalue of the shifted modified midpoint minus the spectral radius of the modified radius plus the componentwise absolute shift.
assumptions_latex: [A]\text{ is a real symmetric interval matrix with modified matrices }\widetilde A_M\text{ and }\widetilde{\Delta A}

Characteristic-Polynomial Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certified regional eigenvalue bounds obtained by enclosing characteristic polynomials and all their real zeros.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal H\) be a compact family of real symmetric matrices enclosing \(\nabla^2f(X)\), and let \(p_H(t)=\det(tI-H)\). knowledge_statements.title: Unscaled Gershgorin Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct rowwise lower eigenvalue bound for every matrix in an interval Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \([H]=([\underline h_{ij},\overline h_{ij}])\) be symmetric and contain every \(
abla^2f(x)\) on \(X\). Define \(m_{ij}=\max\{|\underline h_{ij}|,|\overline h_{ij}|\}\) for \(i
e j\). The unscaled Gershgorin bound is \(\underline\lambda_G=\min_i\{\underline h_{ii}-\sum_{j
e i}m_{ij}\}\). Then \(\lambda_{\min}(
abla^2f(x))\ge\underline\lambda_G\) for all \(x\in X\). A uniform alphaBB coefficient \(\alpha\ge\max\{0,-\underline\lambda_G/2\}\) therefore ensures convexity of the shifted model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Taking each diagonal lower endpoint minus its worst-case off-diagonal row sum gives a uniform Hessian eigenvalue lower bound and alphaBB shift.
assumptions_latex: \([H]\) is a symmetric interval enclosure of every Hessian on \(X\).
The uniform perturbation adds \(2\alpha I\) to the Hessian.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2f(x))\ge\underline\lambda_G\) on \(X\), and \(\alpha\ge\max\{0,-\underline\lambda_G/2\}\) gives a positive-semidefinite shifted Hessian.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unscaled Gershgorin Positivity Is Not Necessary for Positive Semidefiniteness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conservatism boundary of the direct unscaled rowwise lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The symmetric matrix
\[
H=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\2&4\end{pmatrix}
\]
has eigenvalues \(0\) and \(5\), so \(H\succeq0\). Its unscaled Gershgorin lower bound is \(\min\{1-2,4-2\}=-1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-semidefinite Hessian can have a negative unscaled Gershgorin lower bound, so the rowwise test is sufficient but not necessary.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaled Gershgorin Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rowwise lower eigenvalue bounds after positive diagonal similarity scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \([H]
=([\underline h_{ij},\overline h_{ij}])\) be a symmetric interval Hessian enclosure, let \(d_i>0\), and put \(m_{ij}=\max\{|\underline h_{ij}|,|\overline h_{ij}|\}\). Applying Gershgorin's theorem to the similar matrix \(D^{-1}HD\), where \(D=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_n)\), gives \(\lambda_{\min}(H)\ge\min_i\{\underline h_{ii}-\sum_{j\ne i}m_{ij}d_j/d_i\}\). This bound holds for every regional Hessian and reduces to the unscaled bound when all \(d_i\) are equal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive diagonal similarity scaling changes Gershgorin row radii without changing eigenvalues, potentially tightening the uniform regional lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \([H]\) is a symmetric interval enclosure of all Hessians on \(X\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: A Fixed Scaling Need Not Improve the Gershgorin Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary on tightening claims for an arbitrarily chosen positive diagonal scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H=\begin{pmatrix}1&0.9\\0.9&1\end{pmatrix}\) and \(D_t=\operatorname{diag}(t,1)\), where \(t>0\). The unscaled Gershgorin lower bound is \(0.1\), while the scaled bound from \(D_t^{-1}HD_t\) is
\[
\underline\lambda_G(D_t)=\min\{1-0.9/t,\,1-0.9t\}.
\]
Thus \(\underline\lambda_G(D_t)\to-\infty\) as \(t\to\infty\), even though diagonal similarity preserves the eigenvalues of \(H\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A poorly chosen positive diagonal scaling can make the Gershgorin lower bound arbitrarily worse, despite preserving eigenvalues.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\underline\lambda_G(D)\geq\underline\lambda_G(I)\) is not guaranteed for an arbitrary positive diagonal \(D\).

notation.meaning: Gershgorin lower bound after similarity scaling by D.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define
\[
\alpha_i=\frac12\max\left\{0,\sum_{j\ne i}\rho_{ij}\frac{d_j}{d_i}-\underline h_{ii}\right\},\qquad i=1,\ldots,n.
\]
Then every scaled row of the corrected Hessian satisfies
\[
H_{ii}(x)+2\alpha_i\geq\sum_{j\ne i}|H_{ij}(x)|\frac{d_j}{d_i}.
\]
Consequently the symmetric matrix \(H(x)+2\operatorname{Diag}(\alpha)\) is positive semidefinite throughout \(X\). Replacing coarse interval magnitudes by smaller certified values \(\rho_{ij}\) preserves validity and can only decrease the resulting corrections.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tightened entrywise Hessian bounds and positive diagonal scaling yield a verifiable row-dominance certificate for convexity of the alphaBB-corrected function.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each coordinate choose
\[
\alpha_i=\frac12\max\left\{0,\sum_{j\ne i}\rho_{ij}-\underline h_{ii}\right\}.

The function
\[
f_{\alpha}(x)=f(x)+\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i(\ell_i-x_i)(u_i-x_i)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Componentwise Minimality Under Unscaled Row Conditions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal correction within the fixed unscaled Gershgorin sufficient system, not among all convexifying corrections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(r_i=\sum_{j\ne i}\rho_{ij}\). The unscaled row certificate imposes \(\underline h_{ii}+2\alpha_i\geq r_i\) and \(\alpha_i\geq0\) independently for each \(i\). Its componentwise least feasible correction is therefore
\[
\alpha_i^*=\frac12\max\{0,r_i-\underline h_{ii}\}.
\]
Every vector satisfying these same row inequalities obeys \(\alpha_i\geq\alpha_i^*\) for all \(i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The standard rowwise formula is the componentwise smallest nonnegative correction satisfying the fixed unscaled Gershgorin inequalities.
assumptions_latex: \(\underline h_{ii}\) and \(\rho_{ij}\) are valid regional bounds.
Feasibility is defined by the unscaled rowwise sufficient inequalities.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinatewise diagonal corrections for symmetric interval matrix enclosures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \([A]=([\underline a_{ij},\bar a_{ij}])\) be symmetric and let \(d\in\mathbb{R}_{++}^n\). Define \(|a|_{ij}=\max\{|\underline a_{ij}|,|\bar a_{ij}|\}\) and \[\alpha_i=\max\left\{0,-\frac12\left(\underline a_{ii}-\sum_{j\ne i}|a|_{ij}\frac{d_j}{d_i}\right)\right\},\qquad \Delta=\operatorname{diag}(\alpha_i).\] Then \(A+2\Delta\succeq0\) for every \(A\in[A]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For every positive scaling vector and symmetric interval matrix, the stated scaled rowwise formula gives nonnegative diagonal AlphaBB corrections such that every enclosed matrix becomes positive semidefinite after twice the correction is added.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinatewise alphaBB curvature correction on a box using interval Hessian bounds and positive scaling parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B=\prod_{i=1}^n[x_i^L,x_i^U]\), and let \(\underline f_{ij}\) and \(\overline f_{ij}\) bound \(\partial^2f/\partial x_i\partial x_j\) on \(B\). For \(d_i>0\), define \(M_{ij}=\max\{|\underline f_{ij}|,|\overline f_{ij}|\}\) and
\[
\alpha_i=\max\left\{0,-\frac12\left(\underline f_{ii}-\sum_{j\ne i}M_{ij}\frac{d_j}{d_i}\right)\right\}.
\]
Then
\[
\mathcal L(x)=f(x)+\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i(x_i-x_i^L)(x_i-x_i^U)
\]
is an alphaBB convex underestimator on \(B\). A width-sensitive choice is \(d_i=x_i^U-x_i^L>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a box, scaled Gershgorin bounds select a nonnegative correction for each Hessian row. Adding the resulting separable quadratic terms, which are nonpositive throughout the box, produces a convex alphaBB underestimator. Positive box widths may be used as the scaling parameters.
assumptions_latex: f\in\mathbb R[x]\text{ is nonconvex and twice differentiable on }B=\prod_{i=1}^n[x_i^L,x_i^U]
\underline f_{ij}\le \frac{\partial^2f}{\partial x_i\partial x_j}(x)\le \overline f_{ij}\quad\forall x\in B
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal L(x)\le f(x)\ \forall x\in B,\qquad \nabla^2\mathcal L(x)\succeq0\ \forall x\in B.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(d\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\), set
\[
\alpha_i(d)=\frac12\max\left\{0,\sum_{j\ne i}\rho_{ij}\frac{d_j}{d_i}-\underline h_{ii}\right\}.
\]
A scaling-optimized selection is any solution of
\[
\min_{d\in\mathbb R_{++}^n}\ \sum_{i=1}^n w_i\alpha_i(d)
\quad\text{subject to}\quad \prod_{i=1}^n d_i=1,
\]
where \(w_i\geq0\). The normalization removes the invariance under common rescaling of \(d\). Every feasible \(d\) yields a scaled Gershgorin certificate and hence a convex alphaBB underestimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimize a normalized positive scaling while deriving each alpha from its scaled Hessian row; every feasible scaling retains the convexity certificate.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex reformulation of normalized positive-scaling optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Set \(d_i=e^{y_i}\). The normalization \(\prod_i d_i=1\) becomes \(\sum_i y_i=0\), and
\[
\alpha_i(y)=\frac12\max\left\{0,\sum_{j\ne i}\rho_{ij}e^{y_j-y_i}-\underline h_{ii}\right\}.
\]
For \(w_i\geq0\), the equivalent problem
\[
\min_{y\in\mathbb R^n}\sum_iw_i\alpha_i(y)\quad\text{subject to}\quad\sum_i y_i=0
\]
has a convex objective and an affine constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Logarithmic scaling converts the normalized scaling search into a convex optimization problem with one affine equality.
knowledge_statements.title: Convex Log-Scaling Formulation

assumptions_latex: \(X=\prod_{i=1}^n[\ell_i,u_i]\) and the feasible set \(\mathcal A\subseteq\mathbb R_+^n\) contains only convexifying alpha vectors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A maximum-error selection minimizes \(\sum_i\alpha_i(u_i-\ell_i)^2/4\) over \(\mathcal A\).

notation.meaning: Set of nonnegative corrections satisfying the selected convexity certificate.
Pointwise separation between the original function and its underestimator.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case vertical separation on a box for nonnegative coordinatewise corrections.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 11. The alphaBB for Box Constrained Twice-Differentiable NLPs: Theory p. 315

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The separation is
\[
E_\alpha(x)=f(x)-f_\alpha(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i(x_i-\ell_i)(u_i-x_i).
\]
For \(\alpha\geq0\), separability gives
\[
\max_{x\in X}E_\alpha(x)=\frac14\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i(u_i-\ell_i)^2,
\]
attained at the box midpoint. Thus maximum-error alpha selection is represented by
\[
\min_{\alpha\in\mathcal A}\ \frac14\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i(u_i-\ell_i)^2.
\]
Membership in \(\mathcal A\), rather than the error objective, guarantees convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Among valid convexifying corrections, minimize the exact worst-case gap, which is attained at the box midpoint and is linear in alpha.
knowledge_statements.title: Maximum-Error Alpha Selection

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 11. The alphaBB for Box Constrained Twice-Differentiable NLPs: Theory p. 315

assumptions_latex: \(X=\prod_{i=1}^n[\ell_i,u_i]\) has positive widths and is equipped with the uniform probability measure.
The feasible set \(\mathcal A\subseteq\mathbb R_+^n\) contains only convexifying alpha vectors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An average-error selection minimizes \(\sum_i\alpha_i(u_i-\ell_i)^2/6\) over \(\mathcal A\).

notation.meaning: Set of corrections satisfying the selected convexity certificate.
Uniform random point on the regional box.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mean vertical separation under the uniform distribution on the regional box.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 11. The alphaBB for Box Constrained Twice-Differentiable NLPs: Theory p. 315

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(U\) be uniformly distributed on \(X\). For the alphaBB separation
\[
E_\alpha(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i(x_i-\ell_i)(u_i-x_i),
\]
one has
\[
\mathbb E[E_\alpha(U)]=\frac16\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i(u_i-\ell_i)^2.
\]
Accordingly, average-error alpha selection is represented by
\[
\min_{\alpha\in\mathcal A}\ \frac16\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i(u_i-\ell_i)^2.
\]
The feasible-set constraints provide convexity; the displayed objective ranks valid corrections by their uniform mean separation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under uniform averaging on the box, the alphaBB gap has a closed linear expression; minimize it over all valid convexifying corrections.
knowledge_statements.title: Average-Error Alpha Selection

children.title: Rowwise Bound Complexity
children.top_down_role: Cost characteristics of Gershgorin-type regional estimates.

assumptions_latex: A dense symmetric interval Hessian is stored by its \(n(n+1)/2\) independent entry intervals.
Each row bound uses constant-time arithmetic per stored entry.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: All rowwise bounds and corrections require \(O(n^2)\) arithmetic and \(O(n^2)\) stored interval data.

notation.meaning: Number of structurally nonzero stored Hessian entries.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arithmetic cost after interval Hessian entries have already been computed.

source_refs.locator: 1.5 Complexity Analysis p. 19

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Computing every Gershgorin radius requires visiting each off-diagonal entry at most twice. Hence an unscaled or fixed-scaling rowwise eigenvalue bound for a dense \(n\times n\) interval Hessian uses \(O(n^2)\) arithmetic operations after the entry intervals are available. Forming all coordinatewise corrections has the same bound. For a sparse representation with \(m\) stored structural nonzeros, the arithmetic cost is \(O(n+m)\). The bound excludes the cost of constructing the interval Hessian and of optimizing a scaling vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Once interval Hessian entries are available, dense rowwise bounds cost quadratic time; sparse bounds cost linear time in rows plus stored nonzeros.
knowledge_statements.title: Rowwise Bound Complexity

source_witnesses.locator: 1.5 Complexity Analysis p. 19

children.title: Spectral-Enclosure Complexity
children.top_down_role: Cost characteristics of tighter interval spectral methods.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cost of evaluating the midpoint–radius interval spectral bound after the interval Hessian is available.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a dense symmetric interval Hessian have midpoint \(M\in\mathbb S^n\) and entrywise radius matrix \(R\in\mathbb S^n_+\). Evaluating \(\lambda_{\min}(M)-\rho(R)\) with standard dense symmetric eigensolvers requires a constant number of dense eigenvalue computations. Its arithmetic cost is therefore \(O(n^3)\) and its matrix storage is \(O(n^2)\), excluding interval-Hessian construction and validated-rounding overhead.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dense midpoint–radius spectral enclosure costs cubic arithmetic and quadratic storage after the interval Hessian has been formed.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) and \(R\) are dense symmetric matrices of order \(n\).
Standard dense eigenvalue algorithms are used.
Interval-Hessian construction and validated-rounding overhead are excluded.

notation.meaning: midpoint matrix of the interval Hessian
spectral radius of the radius matrix

knowledge_statements.title: Dense Midpoint–Radius Spectral-Enclosure Cost

assumptions_latex: A spectral-enclosure procedure performs \(k\) dense symmetric eigenvalue decompositions and \(q\) additional scalar interval operations.
Standard dense arithmetic is used for each eigendecomposition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Its arithmetic cost is \(O(kn^3+q)\), in addition to interval-Hessian construction.

notation.meaning: Number of additional scalar interval operations.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: dense symmetric eigendecomposition has cubic arithmetic cost
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional cost template for enclosure methods based on repeated dense spectral calculations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If a certified spectral-enclosure method evaluates \(k\) dense symmetric point matrices of order \(n\), each by a standard eigensolver, and performs \(q\) further scalar interval operations, then its arithmetic work is
\[
O(kn^3+q).
\]
Its matrix storage is \(O(n^2)\), excluding any method-dependent collection of subproblems. Thus such an enclosure is generally more expensive than a single \(O(n^2)\) rowwise pass. The formula is conditional: subdivision, vertex generation, or iterative refinement can make \(k\) depend exponentially on \(n\) or on the requested enclosure tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A spectral enclosure using k dense eigensolves costs cubic time per solve, with any subdivision or vertex count multiplying that cost.
knowledge_statements.title: Spectral-Enclosure Complexity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional cubic-cost template is plausible, but no citation identifies a certified spectral-enclosure method or supports the claims about method-dependent subdivision and vertex growth.

children.title: Exact Interval-Spectrum Complexity Boundary
children.top_down_role: The combinatorial boundary associated with exact spectral extremization over interval-matrix families.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal H\) is a symmetric interval-matrix family with \(m\) independently varying upper-triangular entries.
Exact real arithmetic and exhaustive vertex evaluation are allowed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact vertex enumeration requires at most \(2^m\) eigenvalue computations, giving \(O(2^m n^3)\) dense arithmetic.

notation.meaning: Number of independently varying interval entries.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: a concave function attains a polytope minimum at some extreme point
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exhaustive exact minimization of the smallest eigenvalue over a symmetric interval box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Because the smallest-eigenvalue map is concave on symmetric matrices,
\[
\min_{H\in\mathcal H}\lambda_{\min}(H)
=
\min_{V\in\operatorname{vert}(\mathcal H)}\lambda_{\min}(V).
\]
With \(m\) independently varying interval entries, the interval box has at most \(2^m\) vertices. Exhaustive exact evaluation therefore uses at most \(2^m\) symmetric eigensolves and \(O(2^m n^3)\) dense arithmetic. For a fully independent symmetric family, \(m=n(n+1)/2\). This establishes a combinatorial boundary for naive exact spectral extremization, without asserting that every structured family requires enumeration of all vertices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact smallest-eigenvalue minimization can be reduced to interval-box vertices, whose count is exponential in the number of independent entries.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Interval-Spectrum Complexity Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The extreme-point identity and arithmetic-model enumeration bound are plausible, but this exact interval-spectrum complexity claim has no cited source and requires authoritative support.

children.title: Special-Structure Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Dedicated lower models for recognized nonlinear forms.

assumptions_latex: A term \(t:X\to\mathbb R\) has a recognized structure with a known convex underestimator \(r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The function \(r\) is a valid structure-specific relaxation of \(t\) on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Use of a dedicated convex envelope or relaxation for an identified nonlinear form.

source_refs.locator: 1.2 Structure of Global Optimization Models p. 3

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A special-structure relaxation of \(t\) on \(X\) is a function \(r:X\to\mathbb R\) satisfying
\[
r(x)\leq t(x)\quad\text{for every }x\in X,
\]
with \(r\) convex on \(X\), where validity follows from the recognized algebraic form of \(t\), such as a bilinear, multilinear, fractional, or univariate-composite form. When several valid structure-specific models are available, their pointwise maximum remains a valid underestimator and is convex whenever all constituent models are convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a recognized nonlinear form, use a dedicated convex lower model valid on the current region; compatible models may be strengthened by taking their maximum.
knowledge_statements.title: Special-Structure Relaxations

source_witnesses.locator: 1.2 Structure of Global Optimization Models p. 3

children.title: Generic AlphaBB Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Curvature-based treatment for residual smooth nonconvex terms.

assumptions_latex: \(X=\prod_i[\ell_i,u_i]\) and \(t\in C^2\) on a neighborhood of \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The alphaBB function \(t_\alpha\) is a convex underestimator of \(t\) on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic boxwise convexification for a twice-differentiable residual term.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 11. The alphaBB for Box Constrained Twice-Differentiable NLPs: Theory p. 315

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The generic alphaBB relaxation of \(t\) on \(X\) associated with \(\alpha\) is
\[
t_\alpha(x)=t(x)+\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i(\ell_i-x_i)(u_i-x_i).
\]
Since \((\ell_i-x_i)(u_i-x_i)\leq0\) on \(X\), one has \(t_\alpha(x)\leq t(x)\). Its Hessian is
\[
\nabla^2t_\alpha(x)=\nabla^2t(x)+2\operatorname{Diag}(\alpha),
\]
which is positive semidefinite by assumption. Thus \(t_\alpha\) is a convex underestimator suitable when no stronger recognized structural relaxation is selected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A generic alphaBB relaxation adds nonpositive separable quadratic terms whose diagonal curvature correction makes a smooth residual term convex.
knowledge_statements.title: Generic AlphaBB Relaxations

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 11. The alphaBB for Box Constrained Twice-Differentiable NLPs: Theory p. 315

children.title: Hybrid Termwise Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Combined models using specialized envelopes and generic alphaBB convexifiers.

assumptions_latex: The function decomposes as \(f=\sum_{k=1}^p t_k\) on a convex region \(X\).
Each selected model \(r_k\) is convex on \(X\) and satisfies \(r_k\leq t_k\) there.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sum \(R=\sum_k r_k\) is a convex underestimator of \(f\) on \(X\).

notation.meaning: Termwise decomposition of the original function.
Selected lower model for term k.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Termwise combination of structural envelopes and generic alphaBB models.

source_refs.locator: 1.2 Structure of Global Optimization Models p. 3
Chapter 11. The alphaBB for Box Constrained Twice-Differentiable NLPs: Theory p. 315

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Partition the term indices into \(S\), treated by special-structure convex underestimators, and \(G\), treated by generic alphaBB convexifiers. Define
\[
R(x)=\sum_{k\in S}r_k^{\mathrm{str}}(x)+\sum_{k\in G}r_k^{\alpha}(x).
\]
If each constituent satisfies \(r_k^{\mathrm{str}}(x)\leq t_k(x)\) or \(r_k^{\alpha}(x)\leq t_k(x)\) on \(X\), then \(R(x)\leq f(x)\) on \(X\). Since a finite sum of convex functions is convex, \(R\) is a valid convex hybrid underestimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relax recognized terms with specialized envelopes, residual smooth terms with alphaBB, and sum the convex lower models to obtain a valid hybrid relaxation.
knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Termwise Relaxations

children.title: Objective Relaxation Assembly
children.top_down_role: Composition of a convex regional objective from heterogeneous lower models.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective Relaxation Assembly
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-sum assembly of heterogeneous convex termwise objective underestimators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the regional relaxed objective by
\[
f^{L}(x)=\sum_{k=1}^p r_k(x),
\]
where each \(r_k\) may be an exact convex term, a special-structure envelope, or a generic alphaBB underestimator. Termwise validity implies
\[
f^{L}(x)=\sum_{k=1}^p r_k(x)\leq\sum_{k=1}^p t_k(x)=f(x)
\quad\text{for every }x\in X.
\]
Because each \(r_k\) is convex on \(X\), the assembled objective \(f^{L}\) is convex on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Summing exact convex terms, structural envelopes, and generic alphaBB models produces a convex objective underestimator on the regional domain.
assumptions_latex: \(p\in\mathbb N\), \(X\) is a convex regional domain, and \(f=\sum_{k=1}^p t_k\) on \(X\).
For every \(k\in\{1,\ldots,p\}\), \(r_k\) is convex on \(X\) and satisfies \(r_k(x)\leq t_k(x)\) for every \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The assembled objective \(f^{L}=\sum_{k=1}^p r_k\) is convex and satisfies \(f^{L}(x)\leq f(x)\) for every \(x\in X\).

notation.meaning: Chosen convex lower model for term k.

source_refs.locator: 10.1 Theoretical Results: GOP to alphaBB p. 309

source_witnesses.locator: 10.1 Theoretical Results: GOP to alphaBB p. 309

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correct bound orientation for scalar-weighted objective components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(f(x)=\sum_{k=1}^p a_kt_k(x)\) and \(r_k(x)\le t_k(x)\) on \(X\). If \(a_k\ge0\), then \(a_kr_k\le a_kt_k\). If \(a_k<0\), the inequality reverses, so a lower model of \(t_k\) cannot generally be used directly; one must use an upper model of \(t_k\) or directly understate the signed term \(a_kt_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lower models can be multiplied directly only by nonnegative coefficients. Negative coefficients require reversing the model orientation or treating the signed component as the term.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a_k\ge0\Rightarrow a_kr_k\le a_kt_k\), while \(a_k<0\) reverses the inequality.

notation.meaning: Scalar coefficient of objective component k.

knowledge_statements.title: Signed-Coefficient Boundary for Termwise Assembly

children.title: Constraint Relaxation Assembly
children.top_down_role: Composition of a convex feasible relaxation from nonlinear constraint models.

assumptions_latex: Each displayed underestimator is convex and valid throughout \(X\).

notation.meaning: Original feasible set restricted to the box.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex outer relaxation of inequality and equality constraints on a fixed box.

source_refs.locator: 11.2 Convex Lower Bounding Function p. 318

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X=[l,u]\subset\mathbb R^n\), let \(g_j:X\to\mathbb R\) for \(j=1,\ldots,m\), and let \(h_k:X\to\mathbb R\) for \(k=1,\ldots,p\). Define \(F_X=\{x\in X:g_j(x)\le0\ \forall j,\ h_k(x)=0\ \forall k\}\). For each \(j\), choose a convex underestimator \(\underline g_j\le g_j\) on \(X\). For each \(k\), choose convex underestimators \(\underline h_k\le h_k\) and \(\underline{(-h_k)}\le-h_k\) on \(X\). Define
\[R_X=\{x\in X:\underline g_j(x)\le0\ \forall j,\ \underline h_k(x)\le0\ \forall k,\ \underline{(-h_k)}(x)\le0\ \forall k\}.\]
Then \(R_X\) is convex and \(F_X\subseteq R_X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For finitely indexed inequality and equality constraints on a box, replace every inequality by a convex underestimating inequality and every equality by convex underestimators of both signs. The intersection of these relaxed constraints with the box is convex and contains the original regional feasible set.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Relaxation Assembly

source_witnesses.locator: 11.2 Convex Lower Bounding Function p. 318

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone strengthening by tighter component underestimators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_X\) be assembled from convex underestimators of inequalities and both signed forms of equalities. Replace a constituent \(r\) by a convex underestimator \(\widehat r\) satisfying \(r(x)\le\widehat r(x)\le t(x)\) on \(X\), where \(t\) is the corresponding signed constraint function. If \(\widehat R_X\) is the new assembly, then \[F_X\subseteq\widehat R_X\subseteq R_X.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pointwise larger valid convex constraint underestimator tightens the assembled outer relaxation without excluding original feasible points.
assumptions_latex: The original and replacement component models are convex on \(X\).
For every replacement, \(r\le\widehat r\le t\) on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.title: Componentwise Dominance in Constraint Assembly

children.title: Regional Convex Lower-Bounding Problems
children.top_down_role: The solver-facing convex models through which alphaBB underestimators produce regional bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Regional Convex Lower-Bounding Problems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solver-facing alphaBB lower-bound model on one search region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
On a box \(X\), let \(\underline f_X\) be a convex underestimator of the objective and let \(R_X\) be a convex constraint relaxation containing the original regional feasible set \(F_X\). The regional problem is
\[L_X=\inf\{\underline f_X(x):x\in R_X\}.\]
If \(R_X\ne\varnothing\), this is a convex optimization problem and \(L_X\le\inf_{x\in F_X}f(x)\). If \(R_X=\varnothing\), then \(F_X=\varnothing\), so the region may be discarded as infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimizing the convex objective underestimator over the assembled convex relaxation gives a valid regional lower bound; an empty relaxation certifies that the original region is infeasible.

notation.meaning: Optimal value of the regional convex relaxation.

source_refs.locator: 11.2 Convex Lower Bounding Function p. 318

source_witnesses.locator: 11.2 Convex Lower Bounding Function p. 318

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Required solver output when the convex relaxation is not solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(L_X=\inf_{x\in R_X}\underline f_X(x)\), any certified scalar \(\beta_X\le L_X\) satisfies \[\beta_X\le L_X\le\inf_{x\in F_X}f(x).\] A relaxation-feasible primal objective instead bounds \(L_X\) from above and is not a regional lower-bound certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inexact convex solve is safe only when it returns a certified value below the relaxation optimum; a primal feasible objective has the wrong orientation.

notation.meaning: Certified lower estimate of the relaxation optimum.

knowledge_statements.title: Certified Inexact Regional Lower Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison of nested valid regional formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_X\subseteq R_2\subseteq R_1\), let \(\phi_1\le\phi_2\) on \(R_2\), and let \(\phi_2\le f\) on \(F_X\). With \(L_j=\inf_{x\in R_j}\phi_j(x)\), \[L_1\le L_2\le\inf_{x\in F_X}f(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shrinking a valid outer feasible region or pointwise raising a valid objective underestimator cannot weaken the regional lower bound.

notation.meaning: Optimal value of regional relaxation j.

knowledge_statements.title: Monotonicity of Regional Convex Bounds

children.title: Preconvexification Domain Reduction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of subbox contraction on an already valid alphaBB curvature correction and its uniform correction bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X'=\prod_i[\ell_i',u_i']\subseteq X\), and suppose \(\alpha\in\mathbb R_+^n\) satisfies \(\nabla^2t(x)+2\operatorname{Diag}(\alpha)\succeq0\) for every \(x\in X\). Then the same \(\alpha\) is valid on \(X'\). For the alphaBB model formed with the endpoints of \(X'\), \[0\le t(x)-t_{\alpha,X'}(x)=\sum_i\alpha_i(x_i-\ell_i')(u_i'-x_i)\le\frac14\sum_i\alpha_i(u_i'-\ell_i')^2.\] Thus contraction cannot increase this bound; it decreases strictly if a contracted coordinate has \(\alpha_i>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A correction valid on a box remains valid on a contracted subbox. Rebuilding the endpoint correction on the subbox cannot increase its width-based uniform gap bound.

notation.meaning: AlphaBB model formed with the contracted endpoints.

knowledge_statements.title: Contraction Monotonicity for AlphaBB Convexification
Preconvexification Domain Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility-preserving box contraction performed before regional curvature estimation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a box \(X^0=[l^0,u^0]\) and a contractor \(C\) satisfying \(F\cap X\subseteq C(X)\subseteq X\) for every processed box \(X\). Set \(X^{t+1}=C(X^t)\), declaring the region infeasible if \(X^{t+1}=\varnothing\). Stop when \(X^{t+1}=X^t\), a prescribed contraction tolerance is met, or an iteration limit is reached. Output the final box \(X'\), and only then enclose the Hessians and estimate alphaBB parameters on \(X'\). The contraction cannot remove a feasible point from the input box.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply a feasibility-preserving contractor until stable or within tolerance, then compute curvature information on the contracted box. Empty contraction safely discards the region.
assumptions_latex: The contractor satisfies \(F\cap X\subseteq C(X)\subseteq X\).

source_refs.locator: 1.4 Deterministic Global Optimization: Approaches and Classes of Problems p. 18

source_witnesses.locator: 1.4 Deterministic Global Optimization: Approaches and Classes of Problems p. 18

A source specifically covering feasibility-preserving contraction and its alphaBB interface is required before the mathematical algorithm can be reviewed reliably.

children.title: Relaxation-Driven Bound Tightening
children.top_down_role: Use of convex alphaBB models to strengthen regional variable bounds.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Certified Inexact Bounds for Relaxation-Driven Tightening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe coordinate updates from inexact auxiliary relaxation solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_X\subseteq R_X\subseteq X=[\ell,u]\), \(m_i=\inf_{x\in R_X}x_i\), and \(M_i=\sup_{x\in R_X}x_i\). Any certified values \(\underline m_i\le m_i\) and \(\overline M_i\ge M_i\) give the safe update \[\ell_i'=\max\{\ell_i,\underline m_i\},\qquad u_i'=\min\{u_i,\overline M_i\}.\] Every point of \(F_X\) remains within these bounds. A feasible value from the minimization generally lies above \(m_i\), and a feasible value from the maximization generally lies below \(M_i\); using either on the tightening side can remove feasible points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inexact tightening is safe only with outward-facing certificates: a lower bound on the coordinate minimum and an upper bound on the coordinate maximum.
assumptions_latex: \(\underline m_i\le\inf_{x\in R_X}x_i\) and \(\overline M_i\ge\sup_{x\in R_X}x_i\) are certified.

notation.meaning: Certified lower bound on the coordinate minimum.
Certified upper bound on the coordinate maximum.

knowledge_statements.title: Certified Inexact Bounds for Relaxation-Driven Tightening
Relaxation-Driven Bound Tightening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimization-based variable contraction using the current convex alphaBB relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(X=[l,u]\) and a convex relaxation \(R_X\supseteq F_X\), solve for each selected coordinate \(i\)
\[m_i=\inf\{x_i:x\in R_X\},\qquad M_i=\sup\{x_i:x\in R_X\}.\]
Update \(l_i\leftarrow\max\{l_i,m_i\}\) and \(u_i\leftarrow\min\{u_i,M_i\}\). If any relaxation is infeasible, discard the region. Otherwise repeat selected solves until no bound improves by more than a prescribed tolerance or a solve limit is reached, and output the tightened box. Because \(F_X\subseteq R_X\), every original feasible point remains inside the updated bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize and maximize selected variables over the convex relaxation, intersect the resulting ranges with the box, and repeat until bounds cease improving.
assumptions_latex: Each auxiliary convex problem is solved to a valid bounding accuracy.

notation.meaning: Relaxation-derived lower and upper bounds for coordinate i.

children.title: Subbox Hessian Re-enclosure
children.top_down_role: Re-evaluation of regional curvature after subdivision.

knowledge_statements.title: Subbox Hessian Re-enclosure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fresh interval-Hessian enclosure after subdivision to exploit the smaller child domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a twice continuously differentiable function \(q\) and child box \(Y\subseteq X\), evaluate interval extensions of all second derivatives on \(Y\) to form \([H_q(Y)]\) satisfying
\[\nabla^2q(y)\in[H_q(Y)]\quad\text{for every }y\in Y.\]
Optionally intersect each entry with its valid parent enclosure: \([H_q(Y)]_{ij}\leftarrow[H_q(Y)]_{ij}\cap[H_q(X)]_{ij}\). If an intersection is empty, flag an enclosure error. Output the resulting child enclosure for alpha re-estimation; repeat independently for the objective and every constraint requiring convexification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After branching, reevaluate each Hessian over the child box and optionally intersect it with the valid parent enclosure, producing curvature data for child-specific alpha values.
assumptions_latex: \(q\in C^2\) on a neighborhood of the parent box \(X\).
The interval second-derivative evaluations are inclusion isotonic and outward rounded.

notation.meaning: Interval enclosure of the Hessian of q on the child box.

source_refs.locator: 10.2 Estimation of the Parameter alpha p. 311

source_witnesses.locator: 10.2 Estimation of the Parameter alpha p. 311

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic sharpness of a convergent interval-Hessian extension on shrinking child boxes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(q\in C^2\) near \(x^*\), and let \(Y_k\ni x^*\) be nested boxes with \(\operatorname{diam}(Y_k)\to0\). Suppose every \([H_q(Y_k)]\) is a valid interval Hessian and every entry width satisfies \(\operatorname{wid}([H_q(Y_k)]_{ij})\to0\). Then
\[\bigcap_{k\ge1}[H_q(Y_k)]_{ij}=\{\partial_{ij}^2q(x^*)\}\]
for every \(i,j\), and the midpoint of each interval entry converges to the corresponding Hessian entry at \(x^*\). Validity or inclusion isotonicity without width convergence does not by itself imply asymptotic sharpening.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A width-convergent interval-Hessian evaluation becomes pointwise exact along nested boxes shrinking to a point; enclosure validity alone does not guarantee this behavior.
assumptions_latex: Every enclosure is valid and every entry width converges to zero.

notation.meaning: Validated interval Hessian on the kth child box.

knowledge_statements.title: Convergence of Child Hessian Enclosures

children.title: Subbox Alpha Re-estimation
children.top_down_role: Recalculation of convexification parameters on a child box.

knowledge_statements.title: Subbox Alpha Re-estimation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Child-specific diagonal convexification parameters obtained from a child Hessian enclosure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a child box \(Y=[a,b]\) and a symmetric interval Hessian enclosure \([H_q(Y)]\), let \(\underline H_{ii}\) be the lower endpoint of its diagonal entry and let \(\rho_{ij}=\max\{|\underline H_{ij}|,|\overline H_{ij}|\}\). Set
\[\alpha_i^Y=\max\left\{0,\frac12\left(\sum_{j\ne i}\rho_{ij}-\underline H_{ii}\right)\right\}.\]
Output \(\underline q_Y(x)=q(x)+\sum_i\alpha_i^Y(a_i-x_i)(b_i-x_i)\). Gershgorin diagonal dominance makes its Hessian positive semidefinite throughout \(Y\), while the correction is nonpositive on \(Y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use the child Hessian enclosure to recompute nonnegative diagonal shifts. The resulting alphaBB function is convex and remains below the original function on the child box.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\underline q_Y(x)\le q(x)\) on \(Y\), and \(\underline q_Y\) is convex on \(Y\).

notation.meaning: Maximum absolute endpoint of an off-diagonal Hessian interval.

source_refs.locator: 10.2 Estimation of the Parameter alpha p. 311

source_witnesses.locator: 10.2 Estimation of the Parameter alpha p. 311

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Monotonicity of Nested Gershgorin Alpha Estimates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise improvement of the standard child alpha formula under nested interval-Hessian data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \([H(Y)]_{ij}\subseteq[H(X)]_{ij}\) entrywise for \(Y\subseteq X\). For each box \(Z\), define \(\underline H_{ii}^Z=\inf[H(Z)]_{ii}\), \(\rho_{ij}^Z=\sup\{|h|:h\in[H(Z)]_{ij}\}\), and
\[\alpha_i^Z=\max\left\{0,\frac12\left(\sum_{j\ne i}\rho_{ij}^Z-\underline H_{ii}^Z\right)\right\}.\]
Then \(\underline H_{ii}^Y\ge\underline H_{ii}^X\), \(\rho_{ij}^Y\le\rho_{ij}^X\), and hence \(0\le\alpha_i^Y\le\alpha_i^X\) for every \(i\). Independently computed valid but nonnested enclosures need not yield componentwise monotone coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If every child Hessian interval is contained in its parent counterpart, the standard Gershgorin alpha coefficients cannot increase; validity without nesting does not imply this monotonicity.
assumptions_latex: Both alpha vectors use the displayed unscaled Gershgorin rule.

notation.meaning: Interval Hessian enclosure on box Z.
Largest absolute magnitude in an off-diagonal interval.
Gershgorin alpha coefficient on box Z.

knowledge_statements.title: Monotonicity of Nested Gershgorin Alpha Estimates

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nested-box monotonicity of the αBB underestimator
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison of coordinatewise αBB underestimators when the parameter is re-estimated on a nested subbox.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let [x_i^{L1},x_i^{U1}]\subseteq[x_i^{L2},x_i^{U2}] and x_i\in[x_i^{L1},x_i^{U1}]. Suppose \alpha^2\geq\alpha^1 and, for j=1,2, \alpha^j\geq\max\left\{0,\max_{x_i^{Lj}\leq x_i\leq x_i^{Uj}}\left(-\tfrac12\lambda_i^f(\mathbf{x})\right)\right\}. Then \mathcal L(x_i,\alpha^1,x_i^{L1},x_i^{U1})\geq\mathcal L(x_i,\alpha^2,x_i^{L2},x_i^{U2}).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a subinterval contained in a larger interval, the subinterval αBB underestimator is at least as large as the larger-interval underestimator when both parameters satisfy their stated curvature bounds and the larger-interval parameter is no smaller.

children.title: Inherited Curvature Information
children.top_down_role: Safe inheritance or refinement of parent-region enclosure information.

knowledge_statements.title: Inherited Curvature Information
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity conditions for reusing or refining parent curvature information on a child box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y\subseteq X\), and suppose \([H_q(X)]\) encloses \(\nabla^2q(x)\) for every \(x\in X\). Then the same interval matrix is a valid, though possibly loose, enclosure on \(Y\). Any parent parameter \(\alpha^X\) satisfying \(\nabla^2q(x)+2\operatorname{Diag}(\alpha^X)\succeq0\) on \(X\) remains convexifying on \(Y\). Moreover, if \([K(Y)]\) is another valid child enclosure, the entrywise intersection \([H_q(X)]\cap[K(Y)]\), when nonempty, is also valid on \(Y\). Thus inheritance is safe, while refinement can strengthen the relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A parent Hessian enclosure and its convexifying alpha remain valid on every child. Intersecting the parent data with another valid child enclosure safely sharpens it.
assumptions_latex: Both intersected interval matrices, when used, contain every child Hessian.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \([H_q(X)]\) and \(\alpha^X\) remain valid on \(Y\); valid nonempty enclosure intersections remain valid.

source_refs.locator: 10.2 Estimation of the Parameter alpha p. 311

source_witnesses.locator: 10.2 Estimation of the Parameter alpha p. 311

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Child Curvature Data Are Not Upward-Inheritable
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of applying a child-valid curvature correction to its parent or a sibling region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q(x)=-x^4\), \(X=[-1,1]\), and \(Y=[-\delta,\delta]\) with \(0<\delta<1\). Since \(q''(x)=-12x^2\), the coefficient \(\alpha^Y=6\delta^2\) makes the alphaBB-corrected function convex on \(Y\), because its second derivative is \(-12x^2+12\delta^2\ge0\). The same coefficient is insufficient on \(X\), where the corrected second derivative at \(x=1\) is \(-12+12\delta^2<0\). Thus curvature validity descends from parent to child, but child-specific data cannot generally be inherited upward or sideways.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A correction certified on a small child can be too small for its parent or a sibling, so curvature inheritance is valid only from a containing region to a subset.
assumptions_latex: A one-dimensional alphaBB coefficient \(\alpha\) adds \(2\alpha\) to the second derivative.
knowledge_statements.title: Child Curvature Data Are Not Upward-Inheritable

children.title: Regional Lower-Bound Validity
children.top_down_role: The role of valid convex underestimation at every active region.

assumptions_latex: \(F\ne\varnothing\), \(f^*=\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\), and \(\widehat x\in F\) has value \(U=f(\widehat x)\).
The active boxes cover every \(x\in F\) satisfying \(f(x)<U\).
For every active box \(X\), \(F\cap X\subseteq R_X\), \(\underline f_X\le f\) on \(X\), and \(L_X\le\inf_{x\in R_X}\underline f_X(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L\le f^*\le U\), and \(L_X\ge U\) permits safe pruning of \(X\).

notation.meaning: Certified lower bound for active box X.
Objective value of a feasible incumbent.
Certified global lower bound including the incumbent value.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate supplied by valid convex underestimation on every active search region.

source_refs.locator: 1.4 Deterministic Global Optimization: Approaches and Classes of Problems p. 18

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\ne\varnothing\) be the global feasible set, let \(f^*=\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\), and let a feasible incumbent \(\widehat x\in F\) have value \(U=f(\widehat x)\). Let the active boxes \(\mathcal A\) cover every \(x\in F\) with \(f(x)<U\). For each \(X\in\mathcal A\), suppose \(F\cap X\subseteq R_X\), \(\underline f_X(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in X\), and \(L_X\le\inf_{x\in R_X}\underline f_X(x)\). Define
\[L=\min\bigl(\{U\}\cup\{L_X:X\in\mathcal A\}\bigr).\]
Then \(L\le f^*\le U\). Moreover, if \(L_X\ge U\), box \(X\) cannot contain a feasible point with objective value strictly below \(U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Combine the incumbent value with all valid active-box lower bounds by taking their minimum. The result bounds the global optimum from below, and an active box whose lower bound reaches the incumbent cannot contain a strictly better feasible point.
knowledge_statements.title: Regional Lower-Bound Validity

source_witnesses.locator: 1.4 Deterministic Global Optimization: Approaches and Classes of Problems p. 18

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure when a lower-bounding subproblem omits original regional feasible points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(X=[0,1]\), let \(F=X\), \(f(x)=x\), and \(\underline f=f\), but minimize over \(R_X=\{1\}\). The returned value is \(1\), whereas \(\inf_{x\in F\cap X}f(x)=0\). Thus pointwise objective underestimation alone is insufficient: the relaxation domain must contain the original regional feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even an exact objective model returns an invalid lower bound when optimized over an inner approximation that omits feasible points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\cap X\subseteq R_X\text{ is essential for the stated regional lower-bound construction.}
knowledge_statements.title: Invalid Inner-Relaxation Bound

children.title: Underestimator Consistency
children.top_down_role: Limiting agreement between the original and relaxed regional models under box contraction.

knowledge_statements.title: Underestimator Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform alphaBB approximation error vanishes as nested boxes contract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(X=[l,u]\), define
\[\underline q_X(x)=q(x)+\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i^X(l_i-x_i)(u_i-x_i),\qquad \alpha_i^X\ge0.\]
Then every \(x\in X\) satisfies
\[0\le q(x)-\underline q_X(x)\le\frac14\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i^X(u_i-l_i)^2.\]
Consequently, for any sequence of boxes \(X_k\) with maximum side length tending to zero, if the vectors \(\alpha^{X_k}\) remain uniformly bounded, then \(\sup_{x\in X_k}|q(x)-\underline q_{X_k}(x)|\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The alphaBB error is bounded by one quarter of the weighted squared side lengths. Bounded alpha values therefore give uniform agreement as boxes shrink.

notation.meaning: AlphaBB underestimator of q on X.

source_refs.locator: 11.2 Convex Lower Bounding Function p. 318

source_witnesses.locator: 11.2 Convex Lower Bounding Function p. 318

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp weighted-width condition for uniform agreement on a sequence of boxes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(X=[\ell,u]\) and nonnegative \(\alpha_i^X\), \[\sup_{x\in X}\bigl(q(x)-\underline q_X(x)\bigr)=\frac14\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i^X(u_i-\ell_i)^2.\] Hence, along any sequence \(X_k\), uniform alphaBB consistency holds if and only if \[\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i^{X_k}(u_i^k-\ell_i^k)^2\longrightarrow0.\] Uniform boundedness of \(\alpha^{X_k}\) together with shrinking widths is sufficient but not necessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The exact uniform alphaBB error is one quarter of the weighted sum of squared side lengths, so convergence of that sum is the sharp consistency condition.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact AlphaBB Consistency Criterion

children.title: Epsilon-Global Certification
children.top_down_role: Global termination and certification through upper and lower bound convergence.

assumptions_latex: \(F\ne\varnothing\), \(\varepsilon\ge0\), and \(\widehat x\in F\) has value \(U=f(\widehat x)\).
The active boxes cover every feasible point with objective value strictly below \(U\).
Every \(L_X\) is a certified lower bound for feasible objective values in its active box.

notation.meaning: Global lower bound formed from the incumbent and active-region bounds.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute-gap certificate for branch-and-bound termination with alphaBB regional bounds.

source_refs.locator: 3.6 Finite epsilon-Convergence and epsilon-Global Optimality p. 87
2.5 Local, Global, epsilon-Global Minima p. 57

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\ne\varnothing\) be the feasible set, let \(f^*=\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\), and let \(\widehat x\in F\) have incumbent value \(U=f(\widehat x)\). Let the active boxes \(\mathcal A\) cover every \(x\in F\) satisfying \(f(x)<U\), and assign each \(X\in\mathcal A\) a certified lower bound \(L_X\) for feasible objective values in that box. Define
\[L=\min\bigl(\{U\}\cup\{L_X:X\in\mathcal A\}\bigr),\]
with this definition giving \(L=U\) when \(\mathcal A=\varnothing\). Then \(L\le f^*\le U\). If \(U-L\le\varepsilon\) for \(\varepsilon\ge0\), then
\[f(\widehat x)-f^*\le\varepsilon.\]
Thus the incumbent, active-box cover, and certified regional bounds form an absolute \(\varepsilon\)-global optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Include the feasible incumbent value when combining the active-region lower bounds. If the resulting certified global lower bound lies within epsilon of the incumbent, the incumbent is absolutely epsilon-globally optimal; the definition also covers an empty active set.
knowledge_statements.title: Epsilon-Global Certification

source_witnesses.locator: 3.6 Finite epsilon-Convergence and epsilon-Global Optimality p. 87
2.5 Local, Global, epsilon-Global Minima p. 57

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of an apparent bound gap when improving feasible points are omitted from the active cover.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Minimize \(f(x)=x\) on \([0,1]\), take incumbent \(\widehat x=1\) with \(U=1\), and incorrectly use an empty active set despite the uncovered feasible points. The convention \(L=U\) then reports a zero gap although \(f^*=0\). Thus an incumbent and active-node bounds do not certify an \(\varepsilon\)-global gap unless every potentially improving feasible point is represented or safely discarded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A small computed gap is invalid if the active search structure has lost coverage of a potentially improving feasible point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: U-L\le\varepsilon\text{ is not a certificate without preserved coverage of all potentially improving feasible points.}
knowledge_statements.title: Lost-Coverage False Gap Certificate

children.title: Curvature-Estimation Cost
children.top_down_role: Cost arising from Hessian enclosure and alpha calculation at search nodes.

knowledge_statements.title: Curvature-Estimation Cost
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Per-node arithmetic accounting for dense interval-Hessian enclosure and diagonal alpha estimation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(m+1\) twice differentiable functions are convexified in dimension \(n\). Let \(C_H(n)\) denote the cost of producing one dense interval-Hessian enclosure. Computing all enclosures costs \((m+1)C_H(n)\). Given those enclosures, endpoint magnitudes and Gershgorin row sums require \(O((m+1)n^2)\) arithmetic operations and \(O(n^2)\) reusable storage when functions are processed sequentially. Hence the per-node curvature-estimation cost is
\[O\bigl((m+1)(C_H(n)+n^2)\bigr).\]
This bound excludes subsequent convex-relaxation solves and may decrease under sparsity or inherited enclosures.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a dense model, enclosing Hessians dominates function-dependent work, while Gershgorin alpha calculations add quadratic arithmetic per convexified function.
assumptions_latex: Dense \(n\times n\) interval Hessians are used.
Arithmetic operations after interval-Hessian evaluation have unit cost.

notation.meaning: Cost of one dense interval-Hessian enclosure.

children.title: Convex Lower-Bound Solve Cost
children.top_down_role: Cost arising from repeated solution of regional convex relaxations.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex Lower-Bound Solve Cost
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Search-wide cost accounting for repeated regional convex-relaxation solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal N\) be the set of processed search nodes, and let \(T_{\mathrm{cvx}}(X,\eta_X)\) denote the work required by the chosen convex solver to certify the regional lower bound on box \(X\) to tolerance \(\eta_X\). Excluding curvature construction and domain reduction, total lower-bound solution work is
\[T_{\mathrm{LB}}=\sum_{X\in\mathcal N}T_{\mathrm{cvx}}(X,\eta_X).\]
If every relaxation belongs to a fixed class with uniform bound \(T_{\mathrm{cvx}}(X,\eta_X)\le T_{\max}\), then \(T_{\mathrm{LB}}\le|\mathcal N|T_{\max}\). Any bound-tightening auxiliary solves must be added separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Total convex-solve work is the sum of regional solver costs. With a uniform per-node bound, it is at most the node count times that bound.
assumptions_latex: Each processed node requires one certified regional lower-bound solve.
Solver work is measured under a fixed computational and accuracy model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_{\mathrm{LB}}=\sum_{X\in\mathcal N}T_{\mathrm{cvx}}(X,\eta_X)\le|\mathcal N|T_{\max}\) under a uniform per-node bound.

notation.meaning: Cost of certifying one regional convex bound.

children.title: Subdivision–Relaxation Tradeoff
children.top_down_role: The balance between stronger node relaxations and the number of required subregions.

knowledge_statements.title: Subdivision–Relaxation Tradeoff
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform box subdivision with classical diagonal alphaBB corrections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\prod_{i=1}^n[\ell_i,u_i]\), let \(d_i=u_i-\ell_i\), and suppose the diagonal alphaBB underestimator is \(g(x)=f(x)-\sum_i\alpha_i(x_i-\ell_i)(u_i-x_i)\), with \(\alpha_i\ge0\). Its pointwise relaxation gap satisfies \[0\le f(x)-g(x)\le \frac14\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i d_i^2.\] After dividing coordinate \(i\) into \(m_i\) equal intervals and recomputing valid local parameters \(\alpha_{i,k}\le\bar\alpha_i\), every child-box gap is at most \(\frac14\sum_i\bar\alpha_i(d_i/m_i)^2\), while the partition contains \(\prod_i m_i\) boxes. Thus halving every width quarters this bound but can multiply the node count by \(2^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subdivision quadratically reduces the alphaBB gap in box widths, but uniform halving can increase the number of regions by a factor of 2^n.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is twice differentiable on a neighborhood of \(X\).
The displayed parent and child alphaBB parameters certify convex underestimators.

notation.meaning: number of equal subdivisions in coordinate i

source_refs.locator: Chapter 11. The alphaBB for Box Constrained Twice-Differentiable NLPs: Theory p. 315

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 11. The alphaBB for Box Constrained Twice-Differentiable NLPs: Theory p. 315

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous and conservatively rounded coordinatewise allocation for a prescribed classical alphaBB gap bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(c_i=\alpha_i d_i^2/4>0\), and use \(m_i\ge1\) equal subdivisions in coordinate \(i\), giving the child-gap bound \(\sum_{i=1}^n c_i/m_i^2\). When the lower bounds \(m_i\ge1\) are inactive, the continuous minimizer of \(\prod_i m_i\) subject to \(\sum_i c_i/m_i^2\le\varepsilon\) is
\[m_i^*=\sqrt{\frac{n c_i}{\varepsilon}},\qquad \prod_i m_i^*=\left(\frac n\varepsilon\right)^{n/2}\sqrt{\prod_i c_i}.\]
For nonnegative coefficients, the integer choice
\[m_i=\max\left\{1,\left\lceil\sqrt{\frac{n c_i}{\varepsilon}}\right\rceil\right\}\]
guarantees \(\sum_i c_i/m_i^2\le\varepsilon\); coordinates with \(c_i=0\) need no subdivision for this criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the separable alphaBB gap bound, continuous coordinate allocations scale with the square root of each coordinate's gap contribution; ceiling these allocations gives a sufficient integer subdivision rule.
assumptions_latex: \(c_i=\alpha_i d_i^2/4\ge0\) are valid uniform coordinatewise gap coefficients.
Child alpha values do not exceed the coefficients used to define \(c_i\).
The continuous closed form applies only where the constraints \(m_i\ge1\) are inactive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m_i=\max\{1,\lceil\sqrt{n c_i/\varepsilon}\rceil\}\) guarantees a child-gap bound no greater than \(\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: Coordinate contribution to the classical alphaBB gap bound.
