knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Vertex Contact Set of Pairwise Box Factors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correct boundary-contact behavior of the proposed sign-preserving off-diagonal factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d_i=u_i-\ell_i>0\) and define \[p_{ij}(x)=(x_i-\ell_i)(u_j-x_j)+(x_j-\ell_j)(u_i-x_i).\] At a box vertex \(v\), \(p_{ij}(v)=d_id_j\) when coordinates \(i,j\) choose opposite endpoint orientations and \(p_{ij}(v)=0\) when they choose the same orientation. Hence, for \(q_\beta=-\tfrac12\sum_{i<j}\beta_{ij}p_{ij}\) with \(\beta_{ij}\ge0\), \[q_\beta(v)=-\frac12\sum_{\{i,j\}\in\delta(S_v)}\beta_{ij}d_id_j.\] The pairwise perturbation generally does not vanish at mixed vertices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pairwise factor is positive at oppositely oriented vertices and zero at equally oriented endpoints; vertex contact is governed by cuts in the positive-coupling graph.

notation.meaning: coordinates placed at upper endpoints at vertex v
coupling edges crossing the endpoint-orientation cut

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Vertex Contact Set of Pairwise Box Factors

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted-cut representation of off-diagonal underestimation gaps at box vertices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Associate an undirected graph with weights \(w_{ij}=\beta_{ij}d_id_j/2\). For each box vertex \(v\), the pairwise perturbation gap is \[-q_\beta(v)=\sum_{\{i,j\}\in\delta(S_v)}w_{ij}.\] Consequently, all box vertices retain contact if and only if \(\beta_{ij}=0\) for every pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The off-diagonal vertex gap is a weighted graph-cut value, and universal vertex contact is possible only in the diagonal subfamily.
assumptions_latex: The perturbation uses the pairwise factors \(p_{ij}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Coupling-Graph Representation of Vertex Gaps

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Universal Vertex Contact Forces a Diagonal Quadratic
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Impossibility of genuine cross-coordinate curvature for quadratic perturbations vanishing at every box vertex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\prod_{i=1}^n[\ell_i,u_i]\) be full-dimensional and let \(q:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be quadratic. If \(q(v)=0\) at every vertex \(v\) of \(X\), then every mixed quadratic coefficient of \(q\) is zero and there are scalars \(\gamma_i\) such that \[q(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n\gamma_i(x_i-\ell_i)(u_i-x_i).\] Thus a quadratic box perturbation with a genuinely nondiagonal Hessian cannot retain contact at every box vertex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every quadratic perturbation vanishing at all vertices of a full-dimensional box is separable, so genuine cross curvature sacrifices universal vertex contact.
knowledge_statements.title: Universal Vertex Contact Forces a Diagonal Quadratic
Off-Diagonal Perturbation Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sign-preserving quadratic representation on a box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(X=\prod_{i=1}^n[\ell_i,u_i]\), define \[q_{\alpha,\beta}(x)=-\sum_i\alpha_i(x_i-\ell_i)(u_i-x_i)-\frac12\sum_{i<j}\beta_{ij}\bigl((x_i-\ell_i)(u_j-x_j)+(x_j-\ell_j)(u_i-x_i)\bigr).\] If \(\alpha_i\ge0\) and \(\beta_{ij}\ge0\), then \(q_{\alpha,\beta}(x)\le0\) throughout \(X\) and vanishes at every vertex. Moreover, \(\nabla^2q_{\alpha,\beta}=Q\), where \(Q_{ii}=2\alpha_i\) and \(Q_{ij}=\beta_{ij}\) for \(i\ne j\). Hence \(g=f+q_{\alpha,\beta}\) is an underestimator whose curvature correction may contain cross-coordinate entries.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative diagonal and pairwise box factors give a nonpositive quadratic perturbation with a prescribed nondiagonal constant Hessian.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: An authoritative source for this nondiagonal alphaBB family is required. The displayed perturbation is nonpositive for nonnegative coefficients and has the stated Hessian, but it does not vanish at every box vertex: a mixed vertex such as x_i=u_i and x_j=ell_j generally makes the pairwise factor positive. Differentiability of f is also needed for the Hessian conclusion.

children.title: Nondiagonal Parameter Selection
children.top_down_role: Selection of diagonal and cross-coordinate corrections.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility boundary for parameter programs retaining unrestricted nonnegative diagonal corrections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L\in\mathbb S^n\) be finite. If the admissible family contains arbitrary nonnegative diagonal corrections, then \[L+2\operatorname{diag}(\alpha)\succeq0,\qquad\alpha\ge0\] is feasible. In particular, \(\alpha_i=t\) is sufficient for every \(i\) when \(t\ge\max\{0,-\lambda_{\min}(L)/2\}\). Thus infeasibility can arise only from additional parameter bounds, structural restrictions, or an invalid or nonfinite curvature enclosure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any finite symmetric curvature lower bound can be made PSD by sufficiently large nonnegative diagonal loading; intrinsic infeasibility requires extra restrictions.
assumptions_latex: The admissible family includes arbitrary nonnegative diagonal corrections.
knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded Diagonal Loading Guarantees Feasibility

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convexity of the Feasible Parameter Region
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conic structure supporting optimization of affine correction parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(Q(\theta)=Q_0+\sum_k\theta_kQ_k\) is affine and all side restrictions form a closed convex set \(C\). For fixed \(L\in\mathbb S^n\), \[\Theta=\{\theta\in C:L+Q(\theta)\succeq0\}\] is closed and convex. A linear correction-cost objective therefore gives a semidefinite program. If \(\Theta\ne\varnothing\) and a nonempty feasible objective level set is bounded, the optimum is attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Affine correction Hessians and convex side restrictions yield a closed convex feasible region and an SDP for every linear selection criterion.
assumptions_latex: For the attainment conclusion, the problem is feasible and has a bounded nonempty feasible level set.

notation.meaning: combined diagonal and cross-coordinate parameter vector

knowledge_statements.title: Convexity of the Feasible Parameter Region
Nondiagonal Parameter Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semidefinite selection under a regional Hessian lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a box \(X\), a symmetric matrix \(L\) satisfying \(\nabla^2f(x)\succeq L\) for all \(x\in X\), and nonnegative weights \(w_i,w_{ij}\), choose \(\alpha_i,\beta_{ij}\ge0\) by solving \[\min\ \sum_iw_i\alpha_i+\sum_{i<j}w_{ij}\beta_{ij}\quad\text{subject to}\quad L+Q(\alpha,\beta)\succeq0,\] where \(Q_{ii}=2\alpha_i\) and \(Q_{ij}=\beta_{ij}\). Construct \(g=f+q_{\alpha,\beta}\) using the sign-preserving perturbation representation. If the semidefinite problem is infeasible under additional parameter bounds, subdivide \(X\) or strengthen the Hessian enclosure; otherwise output \(g\) and the matrix certificate \(L+Q\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select diagonal and cross corrections by a weighted semidefinite program using a valid regional lower bound on the Hessian.
assumptions_latex: The perturbation is the sign-preserving representation of the preceding record.

notation.meaning: regional Löwner lower bound for the Hessian

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The semidefinite construction is mathematically plausible and the algorithm content kind fits parameter selection, but no source supports this particular weighted nondiagonal selection program, its objective, or the proposed infeasibility response. Source evidence is required before fixing the algorithmic formulation.

children.title: Nondiagonal Convexifier Certificate System
children.top_down_role: Certification and tightness comparisons for coupled quadratic convexifiers.

children.title: Coupled Convexity Certificates
children.top_down_role: Validity certification for quadratic convexifiers containing cross-coordinate coupling.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite positive-semidefiniteness witness supplementing a separately certified regional Hessian lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a convex box, \(f\in C^2\) on a neighborhood of \(X\), and let \(q\) have constant symmetric Hessian \(Q\). Suppose \(\nabla^2f(x)\succeq L\) for every \(x\in X\). If a verified matrix \(R\) satisfies \(L+Q=R^{\mathsf T}R\), then \(g=f+q\) is convex on \(X\). If, independently, \(q\le0\) on \(X\), then \(g\) is a convex underestimator of \(f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certified Hessian lower bound and a verified Gram factorization certify coupled convexity; an independent sign certificate establishes underestimation.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a convex box and \(f\in C^2\) near \(X\).
\(L+Q=R^{\mathsf T}R\) is verified exactly or by validated arithmetic.

notation.meaning: certified uniform Löwner lower bound for the Hessian of f
constant Hessian of the coupled perturbation
Gram-factor witness for the corrected matrix lower bound

knowledge_statements.title: Factorized Coupled Convexity Certificate
Coupled Convexity Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regional certificate combining interval curvature and cross-coordinate corrections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g=f+q_{\alpha, eta}\) on a box \(X\), and let \(Q=
abla^2q_{\alpha, eta}\). A coupled convexity certificate consists of a symmetric matrix \(L\) and parameters \((\alpha, eta)\) satisfying \[
abla^2f(x)\succeq L\quad(x\in X),\qquad L+Q\succeq0.\] These two finitely checkable claims imply \(
abla^2g(x)=
abla^2f(x)+Q\succeq L+Q\succeq0\) throughout \(X\). When the perturbation coefficients also satisfy their sign conditions, the same certificate system establishes both convexity of \(g\) and underestimation \(g\le f\) on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Hessian lower bound plus a positive-semidefinite corrected matrix certifies regional convexity; perturbation sign conditions additionally certify underestimation.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is twice differentiable on a neighborhood of \(X\).
\(L\) is a valid uniform Löwner lower bound.
The perturbation has constant symmetric Hessian \(Q\).

notation.meaning: certified lower bound on the original Hessian

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The matrix implication is correct and certificate is the appropriate content kind, but no citation supports this nondiagonal certificate system. Moreover, the uniform inequality nabla^2 f(x) succeq L is not inherently finitely checkable without specifying a certified enclosure method or finite certificate representation.

children.title: Underestimator Dominance Regimes
children.top_down_role: Problem regions where coupled quadratic correction yields stronger lower models than diagonal correction.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating pointwise dominance from metric-dependent comparison.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g_k=f+q_k\) on the same domain \(X\). If there exist \(x,y\in X\) such that \((q_1-q_2)(x)>0\) and \((q_1-q_2)(y)<0\), then neither \(g_1\) nor \(g_2\) pointwise dominates the other. Their minimized values can nevertheless be ordered, so comparison in this crossing regime requires a declared metric or optimization of both regional models.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the complete perturbation difference changes sign, the underestimators are pointwise incomparable even though their optimized bounds may be ordered.
knowledge_statements.title: Crossing Regime Is Unordered
Underestimator Dominance Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise dominance criterion for two certified perturbation underestimators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g_1=f+q_1\) and \(g_2=f+q_2\) be convex underestimators of the same function on a box \(X\). Then \(g_1\) dominates \(g_2\) on \(X\) exactly when \[q_1(x)-q_2(x)\ge0\qquad\text{for every }x\in X.\] Strict dominance holds when this inequality is strict at some point. Consequently, adding a nonpositive cross perturbation while leaving all diagonal coefficients fixed cannot improve pointwise dominance. Nondiagonal dominance can occur only when the coupled parameter choice permits compensating changes in other correction terms so that the complete perturbation difference is nonnegative throughout the box.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One underestimator dominates another exactly when its full perturbation is everywhere larger; cross terms must be compared jointly with diagonal changes.
assumptions_latex: Both underestimators are feasible for the intended convex relaxation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The equivalence between underestimator dominance and perturbation dominance is algebraically correct, and condition fits the container. A source is nevertheless required for the claimed nondiagonal dominance regime. Strict dominance should also be defined explicitly as nonnegative difference everywhere and positive difference somewhere, rather than merely saying the inequality is strict at some point.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed condition for strict improvement of the minimized regional value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be compact and suppose \(g_1\ge g_2\) on \(X\). Positivity of \(g_1-g_2\) on every minimizer of \(g_2\) implies \(\min_Xg_1>\min_Xg_2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gain on all minimizers of the weaker model yields strict optimized-bound improvement.
knowledge_statements.title: Strict Bound Improvement under Dominance

intermediate_metadata.reason: This leaf owns the pointwise order regimes: weak dominance, strict dominance, and sign-changing incomparability. The proposed optimized-bound criterion was deferred because its canonical home is Cross-Term Tightness Gains. Parameter computation, certificates, and quantitative gap improvement were excluded to sibling scopes.

children.title: Cross-Term Tightness Gains
children.top_down_role: Bound improvements attributable specifically to retained off-diagonal curvature information.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary on uniform additive gain when two underestimators share a contact point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g_N,g_D\) be underestimators on \(X\), and define \(\Delta=g_N-g_D\). If \(g_N(x^c)=g_D(x^c)\) for some \(x^c\in X\), then \(\inf_X\Delta\le0\). If also \(g_N\ge g_D\) on \(X\), then \(\inf_X\Delta=0\). Thus common contact precludes a strictly positive uniform additive gain, although strict pointwise or integrated gains may occur elsewhere.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Underestimators agreeing somewhere cannot have a positive uniform additive gain, even if one is strictly tighter elsewhere.

notation.meaning: pointwise gain of the nondiagonal model over the diagonal model

knowledge_statements.title: Common-Contact Obstruction to Uniform Gain

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Condition converting pointwise improvement into strict improvement of the minimized regional bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be compact and let continuous functions satisfy \(g_N\ge g_D\) on \(X\). If \(g_N(x)>g_D(x)\) for every \(x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_Xg_D\), then \[\min_Xg_N>\min_Xg_D.\] Positivity only at points outside \(\operatorname*{argmin}_Xg_D\) does not imply a strict lower-bound gain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dominance improves the optimized regional bound strictly when the gain is positive at every minimizer of the weaker model.

notation.meaning: minimizer set of the diagonal underestimator

knowledge_statements.title: Strict Regional Lower-Bound Gain Criterion
Cross-Term Tightness Gains
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise and worst-case gain relative to a diagonal underestimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g_N=f+q_N\) be a certified nondiagonal underestimator and \(g_D=f+q_D\) a certified diagonal underestimator on the same box \(X\). Define the pointwise tightness gain by \(\Delta(x)=g_N(x)-g_D(x)=q_N(x)-q_D(x)\). Then \(\Delta(x)>0\) means that the nondiagonal relaxation is strictly tighter at \(x\), and \(\inf_{x\in X}\Delta(x)\ge0\) certifies global dominance. Their worst-case relaxation gaps satisfy \[\sup_X(f-g_N)\le \sup_X(f-g_D)-\inf_X\Delta.\] Thus a positive lower bound on \(\Delta\) yields a quantified reduction in the maximum underestimation error.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The difference between nondiagonal and diagonal perturbations exactly measures pointwise tightness and bounds improvement in the worst relaxation gap.
assumptions_latex: \(g_N\le f\) and \(g_D\le f\) on the same compact box \(X\).
Both underestimators satisfy their convexity certificates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_X\Delta\ge0\) certifies dominance, and \(\inf_X\Delta>0\) reduces the worst-case gap by at least that amount.

notation.meaning: nondiagonal tightness gain over the diagonal model

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The gain identity and worst-case-gap inequality are mathematically consistent, and property fits the tightness-gain container. No source is supplied for this metric or its use in comparing diagonal and nondiagonal alphaBB relaxations.

children.title: Coupling Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Structural or numerical regimes where nondiagonal coupling offers little benefit or complicates certification.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp witness showing that every negative cross coefficient violates underestimation for the concrete family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(q_{a,b}\) above, the mixed vertex \((1,0)\) satisfies \(q_{a,b}(1,0)=-b/2\). Hence every \(b<0\) makes \(q_{a,b}(1,0)>0\), irrespective of \(a\), so \(f+q_{a,b}\) is not an underestimator of \(f\) on \([0,1]^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every negative cross coefficient fails at a mixed vertex; the center-point threshold is not the sharp sign boundary.
assumptions_latex: The perturbation is \(q_{a,b}\) from the preceding record.

notation.meaning: a vertex choosing opposite endpoints in the two coordinates

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Vertex Obstruction for Negative Coupling

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact sign and perturbation-curvature boundaries for the concrete symmetric two-coordinate family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(a\ge0\), define on \([0,1]^2\) \[q_{a,b}(x)=-a\sum_{i=1}^2x_i(1-x_i)-\frac b2\bigl(x_1(1-x_2)+x_2(1-x_1)\bigr).\] Then \(q_{a,b}\le0\) on the box if and only if \(b\ge0\), whereas \[\nabla^2q_{a,b}=\begin{pmatrix}2a&b\\ b&2a\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\] if and only if \(|b|\le2a\). Thus this perturbation is simultaneously nonpositive and convex exactly when \(0\le b\le2a\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For this symmetric two-variable family, sign validity requires nonnegative coupling and convexity of the perturbation requires coupling magnitude at most twice the diagonal coefficient.
knowledge_statements.title: Sharp Two-Variable Joint Validity Region
Coupling Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp two-coordinate failures of sign and curvature conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(X=[0,1]^2\), consider \[q(x)=-a\bigl(x_1(1-x_1)+x_2(1-x_2)\bigr)-\frac b2\bigl(x_1(1-x_2)+x_2(1-x_1)\bigr).\] Its Hessian is \(Q=\begin{pmatrix}2a&b\\b&2a\end{pmatrix}\). For \(a\ge0\) and \(b\ge0\), underestimation by \(f+q\) is sign-valid, but the correction itself is convex exactly when \(2a\ge b\). If \(b>2a\), \(Q\) has a negative eigenvalue. If \(b<0\), then \(q(1/2,1/2)=-a/2-b/4\), which becomes positive whenever \(b<-2a\), directly violating underestimation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In two dimensions, excessive positive coupling destroys convexity, while sufficiently negative coupling makes the perturbation positive and destroys underestimation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b>2a\) violates convexity, whereas \(b<-2a\) violates underestimation at \((1/2,1/2)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The positive-coupling curvature boundary b=2a is correct when a and b are nonnegative, but the advertised sharp sign boundary is wrong or incomplete. For every b<0, the mixed vertex (1,0) gives q(1,0)=-b/2>0, so underestimation already fails; b<-2a is only a sufficient center-point failure condition. A source for the intended coupled family and its failure boundaries is also absent.

children.title: Nonquadratic Separable Underestimators
children.top_down_role: Separable perturbation families extending the classical quadratic functional form.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: A new class of improved convex underestimators for twice continuously differentiable constrained NLPs
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: A new class of improved convex underestimators for twice continuously differentiable constrained NLPs

children.title: Exponential Underestimators
children.top_down_role: Exponential perturbation families for smooth nonconvex functions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed-form location of the deepest exponential chord residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(d>0\) and \(\kappa\ne0\), let \[r(t)=e^{\kappa t}-1-\frac{e^{\kappa d}-1}{d}t.\] This strictly convex residual has the unique minimizer \[t_*=\frac1\kappa\log\!\left(\frac{e^{\kappa d}-1}{\kappa d}\right)\in(0,d).\] For \(\alpha>0\), the maximum perturbation gap \(-\alpha r(t)\) is attained uniquely at \(t_*\), and \(t_*\to d/2\) as \(\kappa\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The exponential correction's maximum gap has an explicit unique interior location approaching the midpoint in the quadratic limit.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Interior Maximum-Gap Location

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quadratic Limit of Normalized Exponential Residuals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous connection between exponential chord residuals and the classical quadratic box factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(d>0\), \(t\in[0,d]\), and \(\kappa\ne0\), define \[h_{\kappa,d}(t)=\frac{e^{\kappa t}-1-\frac{e^{\kappa d}-1}{d}t}{\kappa^2}.\] Then \(h_{\kappa,d}\le0\), \(h_{\kappa,d}(0)=h_{\kappa,d}(d)=0\), and \(h_{\kappa,d}''(t)=e^{\kappa t}>0\). Uniformly on \([0,d]\), \[h_{\kappa,d}(t)\longrightarrow\frac12t(t-d)=-\frac12t(d-t)\qquad(\kappa\to0).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalized exponential chord residuals converge uniformly to one half of the classical quadratic AlphaBB factor.
knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Limit of Normalized Exponential Residuals

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed-form uniform-coordinate average gap of one exponential correction factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d>0\), \(\kappa\ne0\), \(\alpha\ge0\), and \[r_{\kappa,d}(t)=e^{\kappa t}-1-\frac{e^{\kappa d}-1}{d}t,\qquad 0\le t\le d.\] If \(T\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,d]\), then \[\mathbb E[-\alpha r_{\kappa,d}(T)]=\alpha\left[1+\frac{e^{\kappa d}-1}{2}-\frac{e^{\kappa d}-1}{\kappa d}\right].\] For a separable sum under the uniform product distribution, the total mean gap is the sum of these coordinatewise expressions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The uniform average gap of an exponential chord-residual correction has a closed form and adds coordinatewise.
assumptions_latex: The coordinate is uniformly distributed on \([0,d]\).
The multivariate conclusion uses the uniform product distribution.
knowledge_statements.title: Average Exponential Chord-Residual Gap

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Negative-Scale Failure of Exponential Chord Residuals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessity of a nonnegative correction scale for automatic underestimation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(d>0\) and \(\kappa\ne0\), define \[r_{\kappa,d}(t)=e^{\kappa t}-1-\frac{e^{\kappa d}-1}{d}t.\] Then \(r_{\kappa,d}(t)<0\) for every \(t\in(0,d)\). Consequently, if \(\alpha<0\), the perturbation \(g(t)=f(t)+\alpha r_{\kappa,d}(t)\) satisfies \(g(t)>f(t)\) throughout \((0,d)\) and is not an underestimator there.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A negative correction scale reverses the exponential chord-residual lower-model inequality in the interval interior.
knowledge_statements.title: Negative-Scale Failure of Exponential Chord Residuals

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separable exponential chord-residual convexification on a nondegenerate box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X=\prod_i[\ell_i,u_i]\), \(d_i=u_i-\ell_i>0\), \(\alpha_i\ge0\), and \(\kappa_i
e0\). Define \[r_i(x_i)=e^{\kappa_i(x_i-\ell_i)}-1- rac{e^{\kappa_i d_i}-1}{d_i}(x_i-\ell_i),\qquad g(x)=f(x)+\sum_i\alpha_i r_i(x_i).\] Then \(r_i\le0\) on \([\ell_i,u_i]\), with equality at its endpoints, so \(g\le f\) on \(X\). Moreover, \[
abla^2g(x)=
abla^2f(x)+\operatorname{diag}\! igl(\alpha_i\kappa_i^2e^{\kappa_i(x_i-\ell_i)} igr).\] Hence positive semidefiniteness of this matrix throughout \(X\) is equivalent to convexity of \(g\) when \(f\) is twice continuously differentiable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding nonnegative multiples of exponential endpoint-chord residuals preserves underestimation and supplies positive diagonal curvature; a regional Hessian test characterizes convexity.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is twice continuously differentiable on a neighborhood of \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g\le f\) on \(X\), and \(g\) is convex exactly when its displayed Hessian is positive semidefinite throughout \(X\).

notation.meaning: Exponential endpoint-chord residual in coordinate i

knowledge_statements.title: Exponential Endpoint-Chord Underestimator
Exponential Underestimators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separable exponential chord-residual perturbations on a box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\prod_i[\ell_i,u_i]\), with \(d_i=u_i-\ell_i>0\). For \(\alpha_i\ge0\) and \(\kappa_i\ne0\), define \[g(x)=f(x)+\sum_i\alpha_i\left[e^{\kappa_i(x_i-\ell_i)}-1-\frac{e^{\kappa_i d_i}-1}{d_i}(x_i-\ell_i)\right].\] Convexity of the exponential implies that each bracket is nonpositive between its endpoint values, so \(g\le f\) on \(X\). The correction Hessian is diagonal, with entry \(\alpha_i\kappa_i^2e^{\kappa_i(x_i-\ell_i)}\). Hence \(g\) is convex whenever \(\nabla^2f(x)+\operatorname{diag}(\alpha_i\kappa_i^2e^{\kappa_i(x_i-\ell_i)})\succeq0\) throughout \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subtracting each exponential’s endpoint chord produces a separable nonpositive correction whose positive curvature can convexify a smooth function.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is twice differentiable on a neighborhood of \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g\le f\) on \(X\), and the displayed Hessian condition makes \(g\) convex.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exponential chord residual is nonpositive on each interval and its stated second derivative is correct, so representation fits the container. No source establishes this exponential construction as an alphaBB underestimator family or supports the selected parameterization.

children.title: Nonquadratic Parameter Certification
children.top_down_role: Regional verification of convexity and underestimation for nonquadratic perturbations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite workflow for certifying a proposed separable parameter vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(g(x)=f(x)+\sum_i\phi_i(x_i;\theta_i)\), compute validated bounds \[U_i\ge\sup_{t\in[\ell_i,u_i]}\phi_i(t;\theta_i),\qquad m_i\le\inf_{t\in[\ell_i,u_i]}\phi_i''(t;\theta_i).\] If every \(U_i\le0\), combine the \(m_i\) with validated regional Hessian bounds for \(f\) and apply a sufficient PSD test. Accept the parameter vector only when both the sign and PSD tests succeed. If some \(U_i>0\), or the PSD test fails, this procedure is inconclusive rather than a proof of invalidity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Validate each perturbation's sign, then combine its curvature with regional Hessian bounds; accept only after both tests succeed, otherwise report inconclusive.
assumptions_latex: All scalar and Hessian enclosures are exact or outward-rounded.
The selected PSD test is valid for every Hessian in the regional enclosure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U_i\le0\ \forall i\text{ and a successful PSD test}\Longrightarrow g\le f\text{ and }g\text{ is convex on }X.\)

notation.meaning: validated upper bound on the ith perturbation
validated lower bound on the ith perturbation curvature

knowledge_statements.title: Validated Nonquadratic Certification Procedure

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Scaled Row-Dominance Certificate for Separable Perturbations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite interval-Hessian certificate for convexity of a separably perturbed model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g(x)=f(x)+\sum_i\phi_i(x_i)\) on a box \(X\). Suppose validated bounds satisfy \(\partial_{ii}^2f(x)\ge\underline h_{ii}\), \(|\partial_{ij}^2f(x)|\le M_{ij}\) for \(i\ne j\), and \(\phi_i''(t)\ge m_i\). If some \(d\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\) satisfies \[\underline h_{ii}+m_i\ge\sum_{j\ne i}M_{ij}\frac{d_j}{d_i}\qquad(i=1,\ldots,n),\] then \(g\) is convex on \(X\). If also \(\phi_i\le0\) on every coordinate interval, then \(g\le f\) on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Validated Hessian-entry bounds plus scaled row dominance certify convexity; independent scalar sign bounds certify underestimation.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and every \(\phi_i\) are twice differentiable near their domains.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nabla^2g(x)\succeq0\) on \(X\), and the additional sign bounds imply \(g(x)\le f(x)\).

notation.meaning: validated lower bound on a diagonal Hessian entry of f
validated magnitude bound on an off-diagonal Hessian entry
validated lower bound on perturbation curvature

knowledge_statements.title: Scaled Row-Dominance Certificate for Separable Perturbations

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Independence of Sign and Curvature Tests
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal examples showing that neither certificate component implies the other.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \([-1,1]\), \(\phi_+(t)=t^2\) has \(\phi_+''=2>0\) but is positive away from zero, so convexifying curvature does not certify underestimation. Conversely, \(\phi_-(t)=-t^2\le0\) has \(\phi_-''=-2\); for example, with \(f=0\), the corrected function \(f+\phi_-\) is not convex. Thus sign validity and sufficient corrected curvature must be checked independently.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive curvature need not preserve underestimation, and a nonpositive perturbation need not convexify the corrected model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\phi\le0\) and sufficient corrected curvature are logically independent certificate requirements.
knowledge_statements.title: Independence of Sign and Curvature Tests
Nonquadratic Parameter Certification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regional certificate for separable nonquadratic perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g(x)=f(x)+\sum_i\phi_i(x_i;\theta_i)\) on \(X=\prod_i[\ell_i,u_i]\). A valid parameter certificate consists of enclosures establishing \[\sup_{t\in[\ell_i,u_i]}\phi_i(t;\theta_i)\le0\quad\text{for every }i\] and a symmetric matrix \(L\) satisfying \(\nabla^2f(x)\succeq L\) on \(X\), together with \[L+\operatorname{diag}(m_1,\ldots,m_n)\succeq0,\qquad m_i\le\inf_{t\in[\ell_i,u_i]}\phi_i''(t;\theta_i).\] The first inequalities certify underestimation; the matrix inequality certifies convexity. Interval arithmetic or exact univariate optimization may supply the required bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certify nonquadratic parameters by bounding each perturbation above by zero and its curvature below strongly enough to make the corrected Hessian positive semidefinite.
assumptions_latex: All scalar and matrix bounds are valid throughout the stated box.

notation.meaning: regional Hessian lower bound for f
certified lower bound on perturbation curvature

knowledge_statements.title: Partition-Local Alpha Parameters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent diagonal alphaBB certification on prescribed subboxes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be partitioned into boxes \(X_k=\prod_i[\ell_{ik},u_{ik}]\). For each \(k\), compute a certified Hessian enclosure for \(f\) on \(X_k\), then select \(\alpha_{ik}\ge0\) such that \[\nabla^2f(x)+2\operatorname{diag}(\alpha_{1k},\ldots,\alpha_{nk})\succeq0\qquad(x\in X_k).\] Define \[g_k(x)=f(x)-\sum_i\alpha_{ik}(x_i-\ell_{ik})(u_{ik}-x_i).\] Each \(g_k\) is a convex underestimator on its own cell. The piecewise relaxation returns \(g_k(x)\) for the unique cell containing \(x\), with a fixed ownership convention on shared boundaries.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute alpha parameters independently on each partition box, producing locally convex underestimators adapted to the curvature of each region.
assumptions_latex: The boxes cover \(X\) with disjoint interiors.
\(f\) is twice differentiable on every cell neighborhood.
Each local Hessian enclosure is valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_k(x)\le f(x)\) and \(g_k\text{ is convex on }X_k\) for every \(k\).

notation.meaning: coordinate-i alpha parameter on cell k

children.title: Spline AlphaBB Underestimators

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Independent Local Convexity Does Not Ensure Spline Continuity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of continuity when valid alphaBB pieces use incompatible corrections on a common facet.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_1=[0,1]\times[0,1]\), \(X_2=[1,2]\times[0,1]\), and \(f(x,y)=0\). Define \(g_1(x,y)=0\) on \(X_1\) and \(g_2(x,y)=-y(1-y)\) on \(X_2\). Both are convex alphaBB underestimators of \(f\) on their cells, but on \(F=\{1\}\times[0,1]\), \(g_1(1,y)\ne g_2(1,y)\) for \(0<y<1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independently valid convex alphaBB pieces may disagree on a shared facet and therefore fail to form a continuous spline.
assumptions_latex: The two boxes share the facet \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The piecewise assembly of \(g_1\) and \(g_2\) is discontinuous on \(F\).
knowledge_statements.title: Independent Local Convexity Does Not Ensure Spline Continuity
Spline AlphaBB Underestimators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility conditions for a continuous convex piecewise assembly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a polyhedral partition of a convex set \(X\) carry differentiable convex underestimators \(g_k\le f\). The piecewise function \(g(x)=g_k(x)\) on each cell is a continuous convex underestimator if adjacent pieces agree on every common facet \(F_{kj}\) and satisfy \[(\nabla g_j(x)-\nabla g_k(x))^{\mathsf T}n_{kj}\ge0\qquad(x\in F_{kj}),\] where \(n_{kj}\) points from cell \(k\) into cell \(j\). Equality of values supplies spline continuity, while the nonnegative normal derivative jump prevents a downward slope break. Higher-order spline smoothness additionally requires matching tangential derivatives to the desired order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local alphaBB pieces form a continuous convex spline when values match across facets and normal directional derivatives do not jump downward.
assumptions_latex: The cells form a finite polyhedral partition of convex \(X\).
Each \(g_k\) is differentiable, convex, and no greater than \(f\) on its cell.
The stated facet orientation is used consistently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g\le f\) on \(X\), and the matching and slope-jump conditions make \(g\) continuous and convex.

notation.meaning: common facet of adjacent cells k and j
unit normal directed from cell k to cell j

children.top_down_role: Strengthening through selected lower-dimensional curvature projections.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary directional coverage condition for convexification by selected rank-one projection corrections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For fixed directions \(a_1,\ldots,a_p\) and \(\gamma_r\ge0\), set \(C=2\sum_{r=1}^p\gamma_ra_ra_r^{\mathsf T}\). If \(v
e0\) satisfies \(a_r^{\mathsf T}v=0\) for every \(r\), then \(v^{\mathsf T}Cv=0\). If, additionally, \(v^{\mathsf T}
abla^2f(x)v<0\) at some \(x\in X\), then \(
abla^2f(x)+C
ot\succeq0\) for every choice of the coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Selected projection corrections cannot remove negative curvature in a direction orthogonal to every selected projection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A negative-curvature direction in \(\operatorname{span}\{a_r\}^{\perp}\) prevents convexification by the selected family.

notation.meaning: direction orthogonal to all selected projections

knowledge_statements.title: Uncorrected Orthogonal-Direction Obstruction
Low-Dimensional Projection Underestimators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank-one convexification along selected linear projections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a box and choose vectors \(a_r\in\mathbb R^n\). Set \(L_r=\min_{x\in X}a_r^{\mathsf T}x\) and \(U_r=\max_{x\in X}a_r^{\mathsf T}x\). For \(\gamma_r\ge0\), define \[g(x)=f(x)-\sum_{r=1}^p\gamma_r(a_r^{\mathsf T}x-L_r)(U_r-a_r^{\mathsf T}x).\] Every product is nonnegative on \(X\), so \(g\le f\). Its curvature correction is \(2\sum_r\gamma_ra_ra_r^{\mathsf T}\). Consequently, selected low-dimensional directions yield a convex underestimator whenever \[\nabla^2f(x)+2\sum_r\gamma_ra_ra_r^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\qquad(x\in X).\] Coordinate vectors recover diagonal alphaBB corrections.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Applying alphaBB factors to selected linear projections gives rank-one curvature corrections and includes classical coordinate-wise alphaBB as a special case.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is twice differentiable on a neighborhood of \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g\le f\) on \(X\), with correction Hessian \(2\sum_r\gamma_ra_ra_r^{\mathsf T}\).

notation.meaning: minimum and maximum projected coordinates on X

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The projection-factor representation is algebraically correct, yields the stated rank-one Hessian corrections, and specializes to diagonal alphaBB for coordinate directions. No source supports this construction as a recognized projection-strengthened alphaBB underestimator family.

children.title: Orthonormal-Transformation Strengthening
children.top_down_role: Coordinate transformations used to expose stronger projected lower models.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Rotation Invariance of Exact Isotropic Curvature
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary showing when orthogonal transformation cannot strengthen an exact scalar spectral correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q^{\mathsf T}Q=I\), \(y=Q^{\mathsf T}(x-c)\), and \(\phi(y)=f(c+Qy)\). Then \(
abla^2\phi(y)=Q^{\mathsf T}
abla^2f(c+Qy)Q\), hence \(\lambda_{\min}(
abla^2\phi(y))=\lambda_{\min}(
abla^2f(c+Qy))\). Therefore the exact uniform minimum-eigenvalue bound over \(Q^{\mathsf T}(X-c)\) is independent of \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Orthogonal rotation preserves exact Hessian eigenvalues and cannot by itself improve an exact isotropic spectral alphaBB shift.
assumptions_latex: Curvature is compared over the exact transformed image.
knowledge_statements.title: Rotation Invariance of Exact Isotropic Curvature
Orthonormal-Transformation Strengthening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rotated-coordinate AlphaBB underestimation on a box enclosing the transformed region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a box, let \(Q^TQ=I\), and choose \(c\in\mathbb R^n\). Suppose the box \(Y=[\underline y,\overline y]\) contains \(Q^T(X-c)\). If \(\alpha_i\ge0\) are chosen so that \(g(y)=f(c+Qy)+\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i(\underline y_i-y_i)(\overline y_i-y_i)\) is convex on \(Y\), then \(\underline f_Q(x)=g(Q^T(x-c))\) is convex and satisfies \(\underline f_Q(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in X\). Selecting \(Q\) by maximizing the relaxation optimum over an admissible family cannot weaken the best bound relative to any included transformation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid AlphaBB model built in rotated coordinates pulls back to a convex underestimator; optimizing over transformations gives at least the bound of every included transformation.
assumptions_latex: The selected correction makes \(g\) convex on \(Y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\underline f_Q\) is convex on \(X\), \(\underline f_Q\le f\) on \(X\), and \(\sup_Q\min_{x\in X}\underline f_Q(x)\ge\min_{x\in X}\underline f_{Q_0}(x)\) for every included \(Q_0\).

notation.meaning: box enclosure of the transformed region

children.title: Projection-Derived Linear Cuts
children.top_down_role: Additional relaxation cuts obtained from projection-based underestimation.

assumptions_latex: \(h\) is convex on \(P(X)\) and \(h(Px)\le f(x)\) on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(t\ge h(Px^0)+s^TP(x-x^0)\) is valid whenever \(t\ge f(x)\) and \(s\in\partial h(Px^0)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) be convex, let \(P:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^k\) be linear, and suppose a convex function \(h\) satisfies \(h(Px)\le f(x)\) for all \(x\in X\). For any \(x^0\in X\) and any \(s\in\partial h(Px^0)\), the affine function \(\ell_{x^0,s}(x)=h(Px^0)+s^TP(x-x^0)\) obeys \(\ell_{x^0,s}(x)\le h(Px)\le f(x)\) on \(X\). Hence an epigraph relaxation with variable \(t\) may validly include the linear cut \(t\ge\ell_{x^0,s}(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every supporting hyperplane of a convex projected underestimator lifts to a valid linear cut for the original function's epigraph relaxation.
knowledge_statements.title: Projection-Derived Linear Cuts

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Support Representation and Monotone Finite Cut Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact and finite supporting-hyperplane representations of a projected convex underestimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z\subset\mathbb R^k\) be open and convex and let \(h:Z\to\mathbb R\) be convex. For \(z^j\in Z\) and \(s^j\in\partial h(z^j)\), define \(\ell_j(z)=h(z^j)+(s^j)^{\mathsf T}(z-z^j)\). Then \[h(z)=\sup_{z^0\in Z,\,s\in\partial h(z^0)}\bigl(h(z^0)+s^{\mathsf T}(z-z^0)\bigr).\] For every finite \(J\), \(h_J(z)=\max_{j\in J}\ell_j(z)\le h(z)\), and \(J\subseteq J'\) implies \(h_J\le h_{J'}\le h\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: All supporting hyperplanes recover the projected convex function, while finite subsets remain valid and strengthen monotonically when cuts are added.
assumptions_latex: Every cut uses a valid subgradient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: h_J(Px)\le h(Px),\qquad J\subseteq J'\Longrightarrow h_J(Px)\le h_{J'}(Px)\le h(Px).

children.title: Symbolic Reformulation Pipelines
children.top_down_role: Expression reformulation and simplification before curvature enclosure.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Reformulation Dependence of Interval Hessian Enclosures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of domain-equivalent symbolic expressions on natural interval curvature bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(e_1\) and \(e_2\) represent the same \(C^2\) function with identical domains on a box \(X\). Natural interval evaluation of their symbolically differentiated Hessian expressions need not return the same interval matrix. Cancellation, factorization, and repeated-variable occurrences may change enclosure width while both matrices remain valid. Thus domain-preserving equivalence alone implies neither equality nor an ordering of the resulting enclosures.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equivalent symbolic expressions can yield different valid interval Hessian widths, so reformulation quality must be assessed after rigorous evaluation.
assumptions_latex: \(e_1(x)=e_2(x)\) for every \(x\in X\), with identical domains on \(X\).
Both expressions admit the required second derivatives and use valid interval extensions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(e_1=e_2\text{ on }X\not\Longrightarrow H(e_1,X)=H(e_2,X)\), and no enclosure ordering follows in general.

notation.meaning: Natural interval enclosure of the Hessian expressions derived from e.

knowledge_statements.title: Reformulation Dependence of Interval Hessian Enclosures
Symbolic Reformulation Pipelines
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantics-preserving expression normalization before rigorous Hessian enclosure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an expression \(e\) representing \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) and a box \(X\). Construct a domain-guarded expression \(\widetilde e\) by constant folding, canonicalizing sums and products, eliminating common subexpressions, and applying identities only where their domains agree on \(X\). Symbolically differentiate \(\widetilde e\) twice to obtain entries \(d_{ij}\). Simplify each \(d_{ij}\) without enlarging its domain, then pass \((d_{ij},X)\) to an outward-rounded interval evaluator. Output \(\widetilde e\) and the resulting interval Hessian matrix; reject any rewrite whose equivalence cannot be certified throughout \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalize an expression with domain-safe identities, differentiate it symbolically twice, and rigorously evaluate the simplified Hessian entries over the regional box.
assumptions_latex: The original expression is defined on the box \(X\).
Every rewrite is certified value- and domain-preserving on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output expression represents \(f\) on \(X\), and each returned interval encloses the corresponding entry of \(\nabla^2 f(x)\) for every \(x\in X\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the symbolic-reformulation pipeline leaf, but its guarantees depend on certified domain-preserving rewriting, symbolic differentiation, and outward interval evaluation. No source or inspectable specification supports those guarantees.

children.title: Automatic-Differentiation Pipelines
children.top_down_role: Programmatic generation of first- and second-order information.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Structural-Sparsity Propagation in Second-Order Automatic Differentiation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe omission of structurally zero Hessian entries during graph differentiation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every node \(v\) of a finite acyclic scalar computational graph, propagate a dependency set \(D_v\) and a conservative second-order sparsity set \(S_v\subseteq D_v\times D_v\) through the elementary-operation chain rules. If the propagation includes every pair that can have a nonzero second derivative, then \((i,j)\notin S_f\) implies \(\partial_{ij}^2f\equiv0\) throughout the graph's regular domain. Such entries may be stored as \([0,0]\), while only pairs in \(S_f\) require numerical enclosure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conservative graph-dependency propagation identifies exact structural Hessian zeros and permits sparse second-order automatic differentiation.
assumptions_latex: The computational graph is finite and acyclic.
Every elementary operation is twice differentiable on the reachable domain.
The sparsity propagation rules conservatively include every potentially nonzero second derivative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((i,j)\notin S_f\Longrightarrow\partial_{ij}^2f\equiv0\), so omitted entries may be represented by \([0,0]\).

notation.meaning: Variables on which node v may depend.
Conservative structural Hessian pattern at node v.

knowledge_statements.title: Structural-Sparsity Propagation in Second-Order Automatic Differentiation
Automatic-Differentiation Pipelines
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Second-order automatic differentiation followed by rigorous regional evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a twice differentiable computational graph for \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and a box \(X\). Propagate values and first- and second-order derivative objects through each elementary operation using its chain rules; exploit symmetry by storing only one of each pair \((i,j)\) and \((j,i)\). Evaluate the resulting derivative graph over \(X\) with outward-rounded interval arithmetic. Output interval vectors \(G\) and an interval matrix \(H\) such that \(\nabla f(x)\in G\) and \(\nabla^2f(x)\in H\) entrywise for every \(x\in X\), or report a domain failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Differentiate the computational graph automatically to second order, then evaluate it outwardly to enclose every regional gradient and Hessian value.
assumptions_latex: Every elementary graph operation is twice differentiable on all values reachable from \(X\).
Interval evaluation uses directed outward rounding.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nabla f(X)\subseteq G\) and \(\nabla^2 f(X)\subseteq H\) entrywise.

notation.meaning: interval enclosure of the gradient range
interval enclosure of the Hessian range

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm is locally appropriate and internally coherent, but no source supports the second-order graph propagation and verified interval-enclosure guarantees. An authoritative automatic-differentiation source and an interval-arithmetic source with specific locators are required.

children.title: Verified Interval-Evaluation Pipelines
children.top_down_role: Outward-enclosing evaluation of regional derivative information.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Subdivision Convergence of Verified Hessian Evaluation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tightening of natural interval Hessian evaluations with shrinking boxes and vanishing rounding error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d_{ij}\) be a finite expression for a continuous Hessian entry near \(x^*\). Suppose its interval primitives are inclusion isotonic and width convergent at the encountered regular arguments. For nested boxes \(X_k\ni x^*\) with \(\operatorname{diam}(X_k)\to0\), evaluate with outward rounding whose maximum endpoint error also tends to zero. Then \(d_{ij}(x^*)\in D_{ij}(X_k)\) and \(\operatorname{wid}(D_{ij}(X_k))\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Away from singularities, shrinking boxes and vanishing outward-rounding error make verified Hessian-entry enclosures converge to the point value.
assumptions_latex: All encountered interval primitives are inclusion isotonic and width convergent.
Outward-rounding endpoint error tends to zero, for example through increasing precision.

notation.meaning: Verified interval evaluation of Hessian-entry expression d_ij on X.

review_flags: Revised to require vanishing rounding error; fixed finite precision can leave a nonzero ulp-width enclosure even as the input box collapses.
knowledge_statements.title: Subdivision Convergence of Verified Hessian Evaluation
Verified Interval-Evaluation Pipelines
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Machine-checkable outward enclosures of regional Hessian entries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d_{ij}\) be an expression for \(\partial^2f/\partial x_i\partial x_j\) on a box \(X\). Evaluate every elementary operation with inclusion-isotonic interval extensions and directed outward rounding, obtaining \(H_{ij}\). Record the expression graph, input intervals, rounding mode, and every intermediate interval. If no operation encounters an uncertified domain violation, this trace certifies \(d_{ij}(x)\in H_{ij}\) for all \(x\in X\). Symmetrizing by \(\widehat H_{ij}=\widehat H_{ji}=H_{ij}\cap H_{ji}\) is valid whenever the intersections are nonempty and equality of mixed partials holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An outward-rounded interval trace certifies regional Hessian enclosures; compatible transposed entries may be intersected when mixed partials are equal.
assumptions_latex: All interval primitives are inclusion-isotonic and outward rounded.
The evaluation trace contains no unresolved domain exception.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nabla^2f(x)_{ij}\in H_{ij}\) for every \(x\in X\), with valid symmetric tightening under the stated condition.

notation.meaning: certified interval for one Hessian entry

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role fits the exact leaf, and the symmetric intersection is valid under equality of mixed partials when both intervals enclose the same derivative. However, the trace semantics, primitive requirements, and certification claim have no cited source or formal checker specification.

knowledge_statements.title: Expression-Syntax Recognition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bottom-up recognition of relaxation-relevant operators and canonical expression patterns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a domain-annotated expression directed acyclic graph \(E\) over a box \(X\). Traverse \(E\) in topological order. At each node, record its operator, children, constants, variable support, and certified domain; canonicalize commutative children and scalar factors. Match the canonical subtree against a finite rule library for affine, quadratic, bilinear, fractional, power, exponential, logarithmic, and composition patterns. Output every match together with its substitution, support, and domain obligations. A match is accepted only if syntactic unification succeeds and every obligation is certified on \(X\); otherwise label the node unresolved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Canonicalize an expression graph and match subtrees against relaxation templates, accepting a classification only when syntax and regional domain obligations both succeed.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) is acyclic and its primitive operators have declared domains.
The rule library supplies explicit patterns and domain obligations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted label has a syntactic witness and certified validity on \(X\); unmatched or domain-uncertain nodes are unresolved.

children.title: Generic Nonconvex Component Classification
children.top_down_role: Recognition of components requiring generic regional curvature treatment.

knowledge_statements.title: Generic Nonconvex Component Classification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conservative fallback class for certified nonconvex terms lacking recognized exploitable structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an expression component \(e:X	o\mathbb R\), assign the label generic nonconvex precisely when: a valid regional test certifies that \(e\) is not convex on \(X\), or convexity cannot be certified; no special-structure rule is both syntactically matched and domain-certified on \(X\); and a general curvature-enclosure underestimator is applicable. The label authorizes only structure-independent procedures, such as an AlphaBB correction derived from a rigorous Hessian enclosure. Failure to prove convexity alone must not be recorded as proof that \(e\) is nonconvex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use the generic class when convexity is absent or unresolved, no special template is certified, and a structure-independent curvature relaxation remains applicable.
assumptions_latex: \(e\) is twice differentiable on a neighborhood of \(X\).
Classification rules distinguish certified nonconvexity from unknown curvature.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The generic label permits a rigorous curvature-based underestimator but asserts nonconvexity only when a separate certificate establishes it.

children.title: Special-Structure Component Classification

knowledge_statements.title: Special-Structure Component Classification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certified assignment to a structure-specific relaxation class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An expression component \(e:X	o\mathbb R\) belongs to a special-structure class \(Ciguration\,\) only if there exist a template \(\tau_C\), a substitution \(\sigma\), and certified regional predicates \(D_C\) such that \(e=\sigma(\tau_C)\) on \(X\) and \(D_C(\sigma,X)\) holds. The class record must include the matched variables, parameters, domain certificate, and the relaxation rule whose validity follows from \(D_C\). Examples of admissible classes include bilinear, univariate-concave, sign-stable fractional, and separable quadratic components; a syntactic resemblance without its predicates is insufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A term receives a special-structure label only through a template substitution and certified regional predicates that justify a corresponding relaxation rule.
assumptions_latex: Each class has a formal template and complete validity predicates.
Expression equality and predicates are certified throughout \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A class assignment is valid exactly when \(e=\sigma(\tau_C)\) on \(X\) and \(D_C(\sigma,X)\) is certified.

notation.meaning: regional validity predicates for the class

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement contains the malformed and undefined text \(Ciguration\,\), so the quantified class is not well defined. More importantly, no source specifies the proposed classes, templates, predicates, or their associated relaxation rules; source uncertainty prevents a reliable replacement.

children.title: Classification Ambiguity Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cases where expression form, metadata, or competing structural interpretations prevent a unique classification.

knowledge_statements.title: Classification Ambiguity Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cases where syntax or interval curvature cannot determine a unique safe relaxation class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Classification is ambiguous on a box \(X\) when two certified templates prescribe incomparable treatments, or when a required predicate is undecidable from available enclosures. For example, if a factor \(u(x)\) has interval range containing zero, then syntax alone cannot certify a fixed-sign fractional or product rule; if an interval Hessian admits both positive and negative Rayleigh quotients, it cannot certify either convexity or concavity. At such a boundary, the pipeline must refine \(X\), strengthen analysis, or dispatch to a valid generic underestimator. It must not select a structure-specific rule whose predicates remain unproved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When competing templates or inconclusive sign and curvature enclosures prevent certification, refine the region or use a valid generic relaxation.
assumptions_latex: Classification decisions must preserve relaxation validity over all of \(X\).
Structure-specific rules have explicit sign, domain, or curvature predicates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Unproved predicates prohibit structure-specific dispatch; refinement, stronger certification, or generic fallback is required.

notation.meaning: certified interval range of a subexpression

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the leaf, but the decision policy and examples are unsupported. In particular, the phrase that an interval Hessian admits positive and negative Rayleigh quotients needs a precise quantification over its matrix enclosure before it can support the stated certification failure.

children.title: Underestimator-Strategy Dispatch

knowledge_statements.title: Underestimator-Strategy Dispatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity-preserving selection among convex, structural, and generic regional relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a classified component \(e:X	o\mathbb R\), its certificates, and an ordered library of underestimator generators. If convexity is certified, retain \(e\). Otherwise enumerate generators whose applicability predicates are certified, construct their convex underestimators \(u_r\), and verify \(u_r(x)\le e(x)\) on \(X\). Select one generator by a declared criterion, such as the largest certified reference-point value or smallest estimated construction cost. If no structural generator is certified, invoke a generic AlphaBB generator from a rigorous curvature enclosure. Output the chosen model and all certificates; report failure if no valid generator exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose only certified underestimator generators, retain already convex terms, and fall back to rigorous AlphaBB when no special treatment applies.
assumptions_latex: Every generator declares checkable applicability and validity predicates.
The selection criterion is evaluated only among certified valid candidates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned \(u\) is convex on \(X\) and satisfies \(u(x)\le e(x)\) for every \(x\in X\).

knowledge_statements.title: Convex Model Generation

knowledge_statements.title: Alpha-Calculation Benchmarks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reproducible comparison of rigorous AlphaBB parameter-estimation methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For benchmark boxes \(X_b\) and Alpha-calculation methods \(m\), record a rigorously valid parameter vector \(\alpha^{m,b}\), construction time \(T_{m,b}\), and relaxation value \(L_{m,b}=\min_{x\in X_b}\underline f_{m,b}(x)\), where \(\underline f_{m,b}(x)=f(x)+\sum_i\alpha_i^{m,b}(\underline x_i-x_i)(\overline x_i-x_i)\) is certified convex. Relative strength against reference method \(r\) is \(S_{m,b}=L_{m,b}-L_{r,b}\) for minimization. Aggregate time by geometric means and strength by paired distributions; methods failing validity checks receive no bound score rather than a substituted value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compare rigorous Alpha calculations using parameter size, construction time, and paired lower-bound improvement, excluding any method that fails convexity certification.
assumptions_latex: All methods use identical functions, boxes, scaling, tolerances, and hardware conditions.
Every scored parameter vector is certified to make its underestimator convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The benchmark reports paired \((T_{m,b},L_{m,b},S_{m,b})\) values that separate computational cost from relaxation strength.

paired bound improvement over the reference method

children.title: Underestimator-Strength Benchmarks
children.top_down_role: Comparisons of regional separation and lower-bound effectiveness.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Well-defined extended-value metrics for comparing valid underestimators without assuming attained extrema.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\ne\varnothing\), and let real-valued functions \(f,L_1,L_2\) satisfy \(L_j(x)\le f(x)\) on \(X\). Define \(b_j=\inf_{x\in X}L_j(x)\) and \(G_j=\sup_{x\in X}(f(x)-L_j(x))\), allowing extended values. If \(L_1(x)\ge L_2(x)\) for every \(x\in X\), then \(b_1\ge b_2\) and \(G_1\le G_2\). Without pointwise dominance, neither metric alone orders the underestimators.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a common domain, pointwise dominance improves both the infimum lower bound and worst underestimation gap; absent dominance, the metrics need not agree.
assumptions_latex: \(L_1\) and \(L_2\) are valid underestimators of \(f\) on the same domain \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_1\ge L_2\text{ on }X\Longrightarrow b_1\ge b_2\text{ and }G_1\le G_2\).

notation.meaning: Infimum of underestimator j on the comparison domain.

review_flags: Uses infimum and supremum because compactness alone does not ensure that arbitrary underestimators attain extrema.
knowledge_statements.title: Common-Domain Underestimator Strength Metrics
Underestimator-Strength Benchmarks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise and optimization-based criteria for comparing alphaBB underestimators on a common box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=[l,u]\subset\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\), and let \(L_1,L_2:X\to\mathbb{R}\) satisfy \(L_j(x)\le f(x)\) on \(X\). Underestimator \(L_1\) is at least as strong as \(L_2\) when \(L_1(x)\ge L_2(x)\) for every \(x\in X\). A regional benchmark may report \(b_j=\min_{x\in X}L_j(x)\) and \(G_j=\sup_{x\in X}(f(x)-L_j(x))\). Pointwise dominance implies \(b_1\ge b_2\) and \(G_1\le G_2\). Comparisons lacking dominance must report both bound and gap metrics on identical boxes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stronger underestimator is pointwise higher. Fair regional benchmarks use identical boxes and report both the resulting lower bound and worst underestimation gap.
assumptions_latex: Each \(L_j\) is a valid lower estimator of \(f\) on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_1\ge L_2\text{ on }X\Longrightarrow b_1\ge b_2\text{ and }G_1\le G_2\).

notation.meaning: regional lower bound furnished by underestimator j

children.title: End-to-End Search Benchmarks
children.top_down_role: Comparisons of complete alphaBB configurations on global-optimization test sets.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Aggregate comparison of complete alphaBB configurations under a common certified-success convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal P\) and \(\mathcal K\) be finite nonempty sets. Assign each run an extended resource value \(m_{p,k}\in(0,+\infty]\), with \(+\infty\) for a run that fails the common certified-success test. Set \(b_p=\min_{j\in\mathcal K}m_{p,j}\) and define \(r_{p,k}=m_{p,k}/b_p\) when \(b_p<+\infty\), and \(r_{p,k}=+\infty\) when \(b_p=+\infty\). Then \(\rho_k(\tau)=|\{p\in\mathcal P:r_{p,k}\le\tau\}|/|\mathcal P|\) for \(\tau\ge1\) is the performance profile of configuration \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A performance profile measures the fraction of instances completed within each factor of the best successful run; failed runs and instances solved by no configuration receive infinite ratios.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal P\) and \(\mathcal K\) are finite and nonempty.
Every run uses the same resource metric and certified-success convention.
Finite resource measurements are strictly positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_k(1)\) is the best-observed fraction and \(\lim_{\tau\to\infty}\rho_k(\tau)=|\{p:m_{p,k}<+\infty\}|/|\mathcal P|\).

notation.meaning: Performance ratio for instance p and configuration k.

review_flags: Revised to define instances on which every configuration fails and avoid the undefined ratio infinity divided by infinity.

End-to-End Search Benchmarks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fair paired evaluation of complete alphaBB branch-and-bound configurations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite test set \(\mathcal P\), compare complete configurations \(A\) and \(B\) using the same instances, initial boxes, feasibility and optimality tolerances, stopping limits, hardware, and implementation environment. For each \(p\in\mathcal P\), record termination status, certified final gap \(g_{p,k}=U_{p,k}-L_{p,k}\), elapsed time \(t_{p,k}\), processed nodes \(N_{p,k}\), and derivative or relaxation evaluations \(E_{p,k}\), where \(k\in\{A,B\}\). A configuration solves \(p\) only if it returns a feasible incumbent and certifies \(g_{p,k}\le\varepsilon_{\rm abs}+\varepsilon_{\rm rel}|U_{p,k}|\). Unsolved instances must remain censored at the common resource limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: End-to-end comparisons must pair instances and tolerances, record certified gaps and resource counts, and treat runs exceeding the common limit as unsolved.
assumptions_latex: Both configurations use identical stopping tolerances and resource limits.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p\text{ is solved by }k\Longleftrightarrow g_{p,k}\le\varepsilon_{\rm abs}+\varepsilon_{\rm rel}|U_{p,k}|\text{ and a feasible incumbent exists}.\)

children.title: Dependency Overestimation
children.top_down_role: Loss of shared-variable dependence across repeated expressions and Hessian entries.

knowledge_statements.title: Dependency Overestimation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical repeated-variable failure of natural interval evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=[-1,1]\) and consider the identically zero expression \(h(x)=x-x\). Treating the two occurrences independently under natural interval arithmetic gives \([h](X)=X-X=[-2,2]\), although the exact range is \(h(X)=\{0\}\). Thus repeated occurrences of a shared variable can enlarge interval enclosures. The same loss occurs when algebraically dependent occurrences appear across formulas for Hessian entries, so an interval Hessian assembled entrywise may contain matrices or curvature values unattainable at any common \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent interval treatment of repeated occurrences loses shared-variable dependence; even the zero expression x−x is enclosed by a nonzero interval.
assumptions_latex: Natural interval operations treat repeated operand occurrences independently.

notation.meaning: natural interval evaluation of expression h over X

children.title: Coordinate-Wrapping Enclosure Pathologies

children.title: Coordinate-System Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Changes in Hessian enclosure quality caused by variable scaling, orientation, or coordinate representation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Demonstrates coordinate dependence of an entrywise curvature estimate under an exact box-preserving scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx\), where \(H=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\2&1\end{pmatrix}\), and set \(x=Sy\) with \(S=\operatorname{Diag}(t,1)\), \(t>0\). Then \(\nabla_y^2(f\circ S)=S^{\mathsf T}HS=\begin{pmatrix}t^2&2t\\2t&1\end{pmatrix}\). Its ordinary Gershgorin lower estimate is \(\min\{t^2-2t,1-2t\}\), whereas the estimate for \(H\) is \(-1\). Thus an exact box-preserving diagonal scaling can change coordinatewise curvature estimates and alphaBB parameters derived from them, without any transformed-domain wrapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even diagonal scaling, which maps boxes exactly to boxes, can change coordinatewise Gershgorin curvature estimates and derived alphaBB coefficients.
assumptions_latex: The regional curvature estimate is the ordinary coordinatewise Gershgorin lower bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\underline\lambda_G(S^{\mathsf T}HS)=\min\{t^2-2t,1-2t\}\), so the estimate depends on \(t\).
knowledge_statements.title: Scaling Sensitivity Without Wrapping
Coordinate-System Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of a general coordinate-invariance guarantee when transformed domains are replaced by axis-aligned hulls.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=[l,u]\subset\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(x=Qy+c\) with \(Q^{\mathsf T}Q=I\), and set \(Y=Q^{\mathsf T}(X-c)\). Let \(f\) be twice continuously differentiable on a neighborhood containing \(Q(\square Y)+c\), and define \(\widetilde f(y)=f(Qy+c)\). The set \(Y\) is generally not an axis-aligned box, so replacing it by its coordinate hull \(\square Y\) enlarges the derivative-evaluation domain whenever \(Y\subsetneq\square Y\). Consequently, natural interval Hessian enclosures, derived lower eigenvalue bounds, and alphaBB parameters computed after reboxing need not coincide with coordinate-transformed quantities computed on \(X\). Preserving the transformed domain exactly eliminates this wrapping mechanism, whereas reboxing removes any general guarantee of coordinate invariance; equality may still occur in special cases.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rotation usually turns a coordinate box into a non-box. Replacing that set by its axis-aligned hull can change interval Hessian bounds and alphaBB parameters, although special functions may still give identical results.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is twice continuously differentiable on a neighborhood containing \(Q(\square Y)+c\).
Transformed domains are represented by axis-aligned interval hulls.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Y\subsetneq\square Y\) removes the general guarantee that interval Hessian enclosures and derived alphaBB parameters are coordinate invariant.

notation.meaning: representation of f in the transformed coordinates

children.title: Axis-Aligned Box Wrapping
children.top_down_role: Enclosure degradation caused by representing transformed regional information with axis-aligned interval boxes.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact axis-aligned hull and volume inflation for an orthogonally transformed centered box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:|x_j|\le r_j\}\), where \(r_j>0\), and let \(Q\) be orthogonal. The smallest axis-aligned box containing \(QX\) is \[B_Q=\{y:|y_i|\le s_i\},\qquad s_i=\sum_{j=1}^n|Q_{ij}|r_j.\] Hence \[\frac{\operatorname{vol}(B_Q)}{\operatorname{vol}(QX)}=\frac{\prod_i\sum_j|Q_{ij}|r_j}{\prod_jr_j}\ge1.\] For a two-dimensional square and a rotation through angle \(\theta\), this ratio is \((|\cos\theta|+|\sin\theta|)^2\), which is strictly greater than one away from axis-preserving angles and equals two at \(\theta=\pi/4\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rotating a box and replacing it by its axis-aligned hull has exact absolute-row-sum half-widths and can strictly inflate volume.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a full-dimensional centered axis-aligned box.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{hull}_{\Box}(QX)=B_Q\) with the stated exact volume ratio.

notation.meaning: Half-width of the transformed axis-aligned hull
Smallest axis-aligned box containing the transformed set

knowledge_statements.title: Orthogonal-Image Box-Hull Formula
Axis-Aligned Box Wrapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit area inflation caused by enclosing a rotated box in an axis-aligned box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=[-1,1]^2\) and rotate it through \(\pi/4\) using \(Q=2^{-1/2}\begin{pmatrix}1&-1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}\). The set \(QX\) is a diamond with vertices \((\pm\sqrt2,0)\) and \((0,\pm\sqrt2)\), while its smallest axis-aligned enclosure is \(B=[-\sqrt2,\sqrt2]^2\). Hence \(\operatorname{area}(QX)=4\) but \(\operatorname{area}(B)=8\). Evaluating interval functions or Hessians over \(B\) therefore admits points outside the transformed feasible region and can strictly weaken the resulting enclosure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A 45-degree rotation of the unit square has area 4, but its axis-aligned hull has area 8, introducing infeasible enclosure points.
assumptions_latex: Interval evaluation uses the smallest axis-aligned hull of the transformed set.

notation.meaning: axis-aligned hull of the rotated square

knowledge_statements.title: Rotation-Induced Enclosure Variation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantified variation of coordinate interval widths under an orthogonal rotation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(X=[-1,1]^2\), the coordinate widths are \(w(X)=(2,2)\). Under the rotation \(Q=2^{-1/2}\begin{pmatrix}1&-1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}\), the axis-aligned hull of \(QX\) is \([ -\sqrt2,\sqrt2]^2\), whose width vector is \((2\sqrt2,2\sqrt2)\). Thus an orthogonal transformation preserving Euclidean distances and area changes coordinate interval widths by a factor \(\sqrt2\). Since interval derivative bounds and the alphaBB perturbation depend on coordinate boxes and their widths, their numerical enclosures can vary under rotation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Although rotation preserves Euclidean geometry, reboxing a rotated square enlarges both coordinate widths by a factor of square root two.
assumptions_latex: Transformed domains are replaced by axis-aligned interval hulls.

children.title: Coordinate Preconditioning Limits
children.top_down_role: Regimes where scaling or coordinate transformation cannot adequately recover lost enclosure strength.

knowledge_statements.title: Coordinate Preconditioning Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear transformations cannot generally remove wrapping while retaining axis-aligned box domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be invertible. The image \(AX\) is an axis-aligned box for every axis-aligned box \(X\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) if and only if \(A=DP\), where \(D\) is nonsingular diagonal and \(P\) is a permutation matrix. Therefore a dense rotation or general linear preconditioner necessarily maps some box to a non-axis-aligned parallelotope. Any interval implementation that replaces this image by an axis-aligned hull then introduces wrapping. Coordinate preconditioning can reduce a particular enclosure, but no fixed general linear mixing preserves exact box representation for all branch-and-bound boxes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Only coordinate scalings and permutations preserve every axis-aligned box. General mixing inevitably causes wrapping for some search boxes.
assumptions_latex: Domains are represented exclusively by axis-aligned boxes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(AX\text{ is axis-aligned for every axis-aligned }X\Longleftrightarrow A=DP.\)

children.title: Expression-Form Sensitivity

knowledge_statements.title: Expression-Form Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraically equivalent expressions can have unequal natural interval extensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(X=[0,1]\), the expressions \(p(x)=x(1-x)\) and \(q(x)=x-x^2\) define the same function. Natural interval evaluation gives \([p](X)=[0,1][0,1]=[0,1]\), whereas \([q](X)=[0,1]-[0,1]=[-1,1]\). The exact range is \([0,1/4]\). Hence algebraic rewriting alone changes enclosure width from \(1\) to \(2\), despite leaving the function unchanged. Applied to derivative and Hessian formulas, this sensitivity can alter interval curvature bounds and the alphaBB parameters inferred from them.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equivalent formulas can yield different interval bounds: x(1−x) encloses more tightly than x−x² on the unit interval.
assumptions_latex: Natural interval arithmetic is applied syntactically without symbolic dependency recovery.

notation.meaning: natural interval extension of the displayed expression for p

knowledge_statements.title: Wide-Box Gap Inflation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic growth of the classical alphaBB underestimation gap with box width.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=[l,u]\subset\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(\alpha_i\ge0\), and define the classical alphaBB underestimator by \(L_\alpha(x)=f(x)-\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i(x_i-l_i)(u_i-x_i)\). For every \(x\in X\), its pointwise gap is nonnegative and satisfies \[0\le f(x)-L_\alpha(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i(x_i-l_i)(u_i-x_i)\le\frac14\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i(u_i-l_i)^2.\] The upper bound is attained at the box midpoint. Thus, with fixed alpha parameters, doubling every box width multiplies the maximum perturbation gap by four.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The largest classical alphaBB perturbation gap equals one quarter of the weighted sum of squared box widths, so wide boxes weaken the lower model quadratically.

notation.meaning: lower and upper endpoints of the box
