children.title: Overconservative Alpha Values
children.top_down_role: Excess curvature correction caused by weak regional eigenvalue bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Overconservative Alpha Values
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone weakening caused by alpha parameters larger than necessary for convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(X=[l,u]\), let \(L_\alpha(x)=f(x)-\sum_i\alpha_i(x_i-l_i)(u_i-x_i)\). If \(\beta_i\ge\alpha_i\ge0\) for all \(i\), then \[L_\beta(x)=L_\alpha(x)-\sum_i(\beta_i-\alpha_i)(x_i-l_i)(u_i-x_i)\le L_\alpha(x)\le f(x)\] for every \(x\in X\). The additional maximum gap is \(\frac14\sum_i(\beta_i-\alpha_i)(u_i-l_i)^2\). Hence an unnecessarily pessimistic regional eigenvalue bound, producing excessive alpha values, preserves validity but can strictly lower the relaxation throughout the box interior.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Increasing valid alpha parameters preserves underestimation but lowers the model, with a midpoint penalty proportional to squared box widths.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_\beta\le L_\alpha\le f\text{ on }X\), with maximum added gap \(\frac14\sum_i(\beta_i-\alpha_i)(u_i-l_i)^2\).

notation.meaning: alphaBB underestimators using two componentwise ordered parameter vectors

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Arbitrarily Weak Bounds from Excess Correction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unbounded deterioration of a valid alphaBB lower model as an unnecessary correction coefficient grows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=[l,u]\) have \(u_k>l_k\), and suppose \(L_\alpha\) is a finite valid convex alphaBB underestimator. For \(t\ge0\), set \(\beta(t)=\alpha+t e_k\). Then \(L_{\beta(t)}\) remains a valid convex underestimator. For any fixed \(\bar x\in X\) with \(\bar x_k=(l_k+u_k)/2\), \(L_{\beta(t)}(\bar x)=L_\alpha(\bar x)-\frac{t}{4}(u_k-l_k)^2\). Hence \(\inf_{x\in X}L_{\beta(t)}(x)\to-\infty\) as \(t\to\infty\), although validity and convexity are preserved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Excessive alpha values can drive a valid regional lower bound arbitrarily far downward while preserving convexity and underestimation.
assumptions_latex: \(L_\alpha\) is finite and is a valid convex underestimator on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.title: Arbitrarily Weak Bounds from Excess Correction

knowledge_statements.statement_title: AlphaBB global optimization workflow for nonlinear error-in-variables estimation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A bounded nonlinear error-in-variables problem with parameter bounds, fitted-data bounds, convex AlphaBB relaxations, local feasible searches, and prescribed absolute or relative gap tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize bounds on \(\theta\) and fitted data \(\widehat z_\mu\); enlarge fitted-data bounds until a local solve has an interior feasible solution; iteratively tighten parameter bounds until \(\Delta_B=\sum_{i=1}^p\left(1-\frac{\theta_i^{\mathrm{new},u}-\theta_i^{\mathrm{new},l}}{\theta_i^{\mathrm{old},u}-\theta_i^{\mathrm{old},l}}\right)\le 0.10\). Then run AlphaBB spatial branch-and-bound: obtain an upper bound from a feasible local solution, a lower bound from the convex relaxation, terminate when \(UB-LB\le\epsilon^{abs}\) or \((UB-LB)/UB\le\epsilon^{rel}\), and otherwise tighten selected bounds, bisect a selected variable, discard regions whose lower bound is not below \(UB\), and continue from the retained region of smallest lower bound. After each AlphaBB solve, enlarge the fitted-data domain and repeat unless two successive outer solutions agree. If the outer expansions eventually enclose the full statistical region, the resulting solutions converge in the limit to the global minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method first enlarges fitted-data bounds until local feasibility is interior and repeatedly tightens parameter bounds. It then applies AlphaBB spatial branch-and-bound, using feasible local solutions as upper bounds, convex relaxations as lower bounds, optional bound tightening, variable bisection, pruning, and an absolute or relative optimality-gap test. An outer loop expands the fitted-data domain when successive global solutions differ. Global convergence is guaranteed in the limit if those expansions eventually enclose the full statistical region.
assumptions_latex: \widehat z_\mu\ \text{has finite initial bounds that may be expanded}
\text{AlphaBB convex relaxations provide valid regional lower bounds}
\text{feasible local solutions provide valid upper bounds}
\text{outer domain expansions eventually enclose the full statistical region}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: UB-LB\le\epsilon^{abs}\ \lor\ \frac{UB-LB}{UB}\le\epsilon^{rel}\quad\text{terminates an AlphaBB search, and exhaustive outer expansion yields convergence in the limit to the global minimum.}

children.title: Interior Exactness Limits
children.top_down_role: Restrictions on attaining exact regional bounds when relevant solutions lie away from box vertices.

knowledge_statements.title: Interior Exactness Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality set of the classical separable alphaBB perturbation on a box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(L_\alpha(x)=f(x)-\sum_i\alpha_i(x_i-l_i)(u_i-x_i)\) on a box \(X=[l,u]\), equality \(L_\alpha(x)=f(x)\) holds exactly when \(x_i\in\{l_i,u_i\}\) for every coordinate with \(\alpha_i>0\). In particular, if \(l_i<x_i<u_i\) and \(\alpha_i>0\) for at least one coordinate, then \(L_\alpha(x)<f(x)\). If all alpha parameters are positive, the underestimator is exact only on box vertices and cannot be exact at any relative-interior point, even when such a point is a relevant minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With positive alpha values, the classical correction vanishes only at box vertices; it is strictly positive at every interior point.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strict Regional Bound Gap at an Interior Minimizer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimal-value consequence when a true regional minimizer lies outside the alphaBB equality set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=[l,u]\), let \(x^*\in X\) minimize \(f\) on \(X\), and let \(L_\alpha(x)=f(x)-\sum_i\alpha_i(x_i-l_i)(u_i-x_i)\). If some index \(i\) satisfies \(\alpha_i>0\) and \(l_i<x_i^*<u_i\), then \(L_\alpha(x^*)<f(x^*)\), and consequently \(\inf_{x\in X}L_\alpha(x)<\min_{x\in X}f(x)\). Thus this underestimator cannot furnish an exact regional optimal value on that box.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a true box minimizer is interior in any positively corrected coordinate, the alphaBB regional lower bound is strictly below the true regional minimum.
assumptions_latex: \(x^*\) is a global minimizer of \(f\) on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.title: Strict Regional Bound Gap at an Interior Minimizer

children.title: High-Dimensional Gap Accumulation
children.top_down_role: Accumulation of separable perturbation gaps across many coordinates.

knowledge_statements.title: High-Dimensional Gap Accumulation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive accumulation of separable alphaBB perturbation gaps across coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the classical alphaBB model on \(X=[l,u]\subset\mathbb{R}^n\), the maximum perturbation gap is \[G_X=\max_{x\in X}(f(x)-L_\alpha(x))=\frac14\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i(u_i-l_i)^2.\] Therefore gap contributions accumulate additively across coordinates. If \(\alpha_i\ge\underline\alpha>0\) and \(u_i-l_i\ge\underline w>0\) for every \(i\), then \(G_X\ge n\underline\alpha\underline w^2/4\). Thus, unless alpha values or coordinate widths decrease with dimension, the worst separable perturbation gap can grow at least linearly in \(n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each coordinate adds a nonnegative midpoint penalty; uniformly positive alpha values and widths force the worst gap to grow at least linearly with dimension.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G_X=\frac14\sum_i\alpha_i(u_i-l_i)^2\), and uniform lower bounds imply \(G_X\ge n\underline\alpha\underline w^2/4\).

notation.meaning: maximum alphaBB perturbation gap on X
uniform lower bounds on alpha values and coordinate widths

children.title: Nonsmooth Function Boundary
children.top_down_role: Models lacking the regional second-order structure used by classical alphaBB.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonsmooth Function Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of the classical Hessian-based alphaBB construction on a bounded box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B=[l,u]\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) and let \(f:B\to\mathbb{R}\). Classical alphaBB selects curvature parameters from a regional enclosure of \(\nabla^2 f(x)\) and forms \(f_\alpha(x)=f(x)-\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i(x_i-l_i)(u_i-x_i)\). If \(f\) is not twice differentiable throughout \(B\), this Hessian enclosure is undefined at some points, so the classical curvature-selection certificate does not establish convexity of \(f_\alpha\). This failure concerns the classical certificate; it does not preclude nonsmooth convex underestimators obtained by other methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without second derivatives throughout the box, classical Hessian-based alphaBB curvature selection cannot certify convexity, although other nonsmooth relaxations may remain available.
assumptions_latex: \(f:B\to\mathbb{R}\) fails to be twice differentiable at some point of \(B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nabla^2 f(B)\) is unavailable as a classical regional Hessian enclosure, so the standard alphaBB convexity certificate does not apply.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 11. The alphaBB for Box Constrained Twice-Differentiable NLPs: Theory p. 315

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 11. The alphaBB for Box Constrained Twice-Differentiable NLPs: Theory p. 315

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery of classical alphaBB certification on finitely many smooth pieces of a nonsmooth model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B=\bigcup_{k=1}^K D_k\), with \(D_k\subseteq B_k\) and each \(B_k\) a finite box. Suppose that for every \(k\), there is a \(C^2\) function \(f_k\) on a neighborhood of \(B_k\) satisfying \(f_k=f\) on \(D_k\), and let \(a_k\le f_k\) be a certified convex alphaBB underestimator on \(B_k\). For any \(D_k\subseteq R_k\subseteq B_k\), define \(\beta_k=\inf_{x\in R_k}a_k(x)\). Then
\[\min_k\beta_k\le\inf_{x\in B}f(x).\]
Hence nonsmoothness confined to finitely many known switching pieces can be handled regionally when every point is covered and each local smooth extension agrees with the original function on its piece.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finitely piecewise-smooth function can be bounded by covering its pieces with boxes, constructing a certified alphaBB model from a smooth extension on each box, and taking the smallest regional bound.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_k\) is \(C^2\) near \(B_k\) and agrees with \(f\) on \(D_k\).
Each regional alphaBB model is certified and \(D_k\subseteq R_k\subseteq B_k\).

notation.meaning: Piece on which the original function agrees with a smooth extension.
Box supporting the smooth regional extension.

knowledge_statements.title: Piecewise-Smooth Box Partition Workaround

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity of an alphaBB-form perturbation when convexity is certified without a classical Hessian enclosure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B=[l,u]\) and let \(f:B\to\mathbb R\) be finite but not necessarily differentiable. For \(\alpha\in\mathbb R_+^n\), define
\[f_\alpha(x)=f(x)-\sum_i\alpha_i(x_i-l_i)(u_i-x_i).\]
Then \(f_\alpha\le f\) on \(B\), and
\[f_\alpha(x)=f(x)+\sum_i\alpha_i x_i^2-\sum_i\alpha_i(l_i+u_i)x_i+\sum_i\alpha_i l_i u_i.\]
Consequently, \(f_\alpha\) is convex on \(B\) if and only if \(f(x)+\sum_i\alpha_i x_i^2\) is convex there. Twice differentiability is therefore sufficient for the classical Hessian certificate but is not logically necessary for an alphaBB-form nonsmooth underestimator when this weak-convexity condition is certified by another method.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonsmooth function, the usual box perturbation remains an underestimator and is convex exactly when adding the corresponding separable quadratic makes the function convex; what fails without second derivatives is the classical Hessian certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f_\alpha\le f\) on \(B\), and \(f_\alpha\) is convex if and only if \(f+\sum_i\alpha_i x_i^2\) is convex.
knowledge_statements.title: Direct Nonsmooth Convexification Condition

children.title: Singular or Unbounded Curvature
children.top_down_role: Domains on which the required regional curvature enclosure is unavailable.

knowledge_statements.title: Singular or Unbounded Curvature
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of finite diagonal curvature correction when negative curvature has no uniform regional lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be a box and suppose \(f\) is twice differentiable wherever defined on \(B\). For finite \(\alpha\in\mathbb{R}_+^n\), the alphaBB Hessian is \(
abla^2 f_\alpha(x)=
abla^2 f(x)+2\operatorname{Diag}(\alpha)\). If \(\inf_{x\in B}\lambda_{\min}(
abla^2 f(x))=-\infty\), then no finite diagonal correction can make this matrix positive semidefinite throughout \(B\). Consequently, the classical alphaBB construction has no finite box-wide curvature certificate unless the domain is restricted or a different relaxation is used.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If negative curvature is unbounded on the region, no finite alphaBB diagonal correction can certify convexity over the entire box.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nexists\alpha\in\mathbb{R}_+^n\) finite such that \(\nabla^2 f(x)+2\operatorname{Diag}(\alpha)\succeq0\) for every \(x\in B\).

source_refs.locator: 11.2 Convex Lower Bounding Function p. 318

source_witnesses.locator: 11.2 Convex Lower Bounding Function p. 318

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact curvature-boundedness criterion for a finite diagonal convexifier on a fixed region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), and suppose \(f\) is twice differentiable on \(B\) with finite symmetric Hessian at every point. There exists a finite \(\alpha\in\mathbb R_+^n\) such that \(\nabla^2f(x)+2\operatorname{Diag}(\alpha)\succeq0\) for every \(x\in B\) if and only if \(m:=\inf_{x\in B}\lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2f(x))> -\infty\). When \(m> -\infty\), the isotropic choice \(\alpha_i=\max\{0,-m/2\}\) is sufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite diagonal alphaBB convexifier exists exactly when the Hessian has a uniform finite lower eigenvalue bound on the region.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is twice differentiable at every point of \(B\).

notation.meaning: regional infimum of the smallest Hessian eigenvalue

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Correction Characterization

children.title: Nonbox Domain Geometry
children.top_down_role: Feasible geometries requiring box embeddings, transformations, or other partition families.

assumptions_latex: \(D\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty and is not an axis-aligned box.
\(B=[l,u]\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is a finite axis-aligned box with \(D\subseteq B\).
\(f:D\to\mathbb{R}\) has an extension \(\widetilde f:B\to\mathbb{R}\), and \(a_B\) is a valid alphaBB underestimator of \(\widetilde f\) on \(B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a_B|_D\le f\) on \(D\), but the nonbox set \(D\) alone does not determine the endpoint-based alphaBB perturbation.

notation.meaning: finite axis-aligned box containing the feasible region
extension of the original function to the containing box
box-valid alphaBB underestimator of the extension

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependence of the classical separable perturbation on a chosen finite axis-aligned box containing a nonbox feasible region.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 11. The alphaBB for Box Constrained Twice-Differentiable NLPs: Theory p. 315

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be a nonempty nonbox feasible region, let \(B=[l,u]\) be a finite axis-aligned box containing \(D\), and let \(f:D\to\mathbb{R}\) have an extension \(\widetilde f:B\to\mathbb{R}\). If \(a_B\) is a valid alphaBB underestimator of \(\widetilde f\) on \(B\), then \(a_B|_D\le f\) on \(D\). Thus a box-valid alphaBB relaxation remains valid after restriction, but its construction depends on the chosen box, the extension, and a curvature enclosure on that box. Without a box embedding, coordinate transformation, or alternative finite partition, the classical endpoint perturbation is not intrinsically determined by \(D\); using a larger containing box may also produce a weaker relaxation than a geometry-specific construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonbox region requires a chosen finite box embedding and a compatible extension of the function. A valid box alphaBB underestimator remains valid when restricted to the original region, although it may be weaker than a geometry-specific relaxation.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonbox Domain Geometry

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 11. The alphaBB for Box Constrained Twice-Differentiable NLPs: Theory p. 315

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Box-Cover Relaxation of a Nonbox Domain
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduction of a bounded nonbox feasible region to finitely many boxwise alphaBB models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D\subseteq\bigcup_{k=1}^K B_k\), where every \(B_k\) is a finite axis-aligned box. Let \(a_k\le\widetilde f_k\) on \(B_k\), where \(\widetilde f_k=f\) on \(D\cap B_k\), and let \(D\cap B_k\subseteq R_k\subseteq B_k\). Define \(\beta_k=\inf_{x\in R_k}a_k(x)\). Then
\[\min_{1\le k\le K}\beta_k\le\inf_{x\in D}f(x).\]
Thus a complete finite box cover yields a valid lower bound and permits geometry-adapted local boxes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Covering a nonbox feasible set by finitely many bounded boxes and solving a valid alphaBB relaxation on each yields a global lower bound by taking the smallest regional bound.
assumptions_latex: \(a_k\) underestimates an extension agreeing with \(f\) on \(D\cap B_k\).
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Box-Cover Relaxation of a Nonbox Domain

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Affine Coordinate Transformation to Box Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pullback of a boxwise alphaBB underestimator through an invertible affine coordinate change.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x=Tz+c\) with nonsingular \(T\), suppose \(Z=[p,q]\) is a finite box containing \(T^{-1}(D-c)\), and let a compatible extension define \(F(z)=f(Tz+c)\) on the transformed feasible set. If \(a_Z\) is convex on \(Z\) and underestimates the extension of \(F\), then
\[a_D(x)=a_Z(T^{-1}(x-c))\]
is convex on the parallelotope \(TZ+c\) and satisfies \(a_D(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in D\). Curvature and perturbation parameters must be computed in the transformed coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An invertible affine transformation can align rotated or parallelotopic geometry with a box; pulling back a valid transformed alphaBB model preserves convexity and underestimation.
assumptions_latex: \(a_Z\) is a valid convex underestimator of a compatible transformed extension on \(Z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a_D=a_Z\circ T^{-1}(\cdot-c)\) is convex on \(TZ+c\) and underestimates \(f\) on \(D\).
knowledge_statements.title: Affine Coordinate Transformation to Box Geometry

children.title: Unbounded Domains
children.top_down_role: Models without finite box endpoints for the classical anchored perturbation.

assumptions_latex: \(D\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty and unbounded in coordinate \(i\).
The classical coordinate correction is required to have \(\alpha_i>0\) and to use both finite endpoints \(l_i\) and \(u_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No finite real-valued correction of the form \(-\alpha_i(x_i-l_i)(u_i-x_i)\) is defined on all of \(D\) when \(\alpha_i>0\) and one required endpoint is infinite.

notation.meaning: endpoints required by the classical coordinate correction
positive curvature-correction parameter for coordinate i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Undefined nonzero classical endpoint correction in a coordinate lacking two finite bounds.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 11. The alphaBB for Box Constrained Twice-Differentiable NLPs: Theory p. 315

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be unbounded in coordinate \(i\). A nonzero classical alphaBB correction in that coordinate has the form \(-\alpha_i(x_i-l_i)(u_i-x_i)\), where \(\alpha_i>0\) and both endpoints must be finite. If \(l_i=-\infty\) or \(u_i=+\infty\), this expression is not a finite real-valued anchored correction on \(D\). Consequently, classical alphaBB cannot directly apply a nonzero endpoint correction in that coordinate until finite domain bounds are established; domain reduction, branching bounds, a coercivity argument, or a different relaxation may be required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonzero classical alphaBB correction requires finite lower and upper bounds for its coordinate. On an unbounded coordinate, that endpoint-based correction is not directly defined until finite bounds are established.
knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded Domains

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 11. The alphaBB for Box Constrained Twice-Differentiable NLPs: Theory p. 315

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exception to the finite-endpoint requirement when no correction is needed in an unbounded coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be convex, let \(J\) index coordinates having finite bounds \(l_j\le x_j\le u_j\) on \(D\), and define \(L(x)=f(x)-\sum_{j\in J}\alpha_j(x_j-l_j)(u_j-x_j)\), where \(\alpha_j\ge0\). Set the correction coefficient to zero outside \(J\). If \(f\in C^2(D)\) and \(\nabla^2f(x)+2\operatorname{Diag}(\widetilde\alpha)\succeq0\) throughout \(D\), where \(\widetilde\alpha_j=\alpha_j\) on \(J\) and \(0\) otherwise, then \(L\) is a convex underestimator on \(D\). Thus an unbounded coordinate obstructs the endpoint-anchored construction only when a nonzero correction is required there.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unbounded coordinate is harmless when its alpha parameter can be zero and corrections in finitely bounded coordinates already certify convexity.
assumptions_latex: Every coordinate in \(J\) has finite bounds on \(D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L\le f\text{ on }D\) and \(L\text{ is convex on }D\), even if coordinates outside \(J\) are unbounded.

notation.meaning: coordinates with finite endpoints and possibly nonzero corrections
full correction vector extended by zeros outside J

knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Correction Exception on Unbounded Coordinates

children.title: Verified-Computation Failure Modes
children.top_down_role: Implementation failures capable of invalidating an otherwise correct convexification design.

children.title: Non-Outward Interval Evaluation
children.top_down_role: Loss of enclosure guarantees during numerical interval evaluation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Containment Loss Invalidates the Curvature Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates loss of the convexity certificate from alphaBB pointwise underestimation that may follow independently from the correction formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathbb H\) be a floating-point interval matrix used as an enclosure of \(
abla^2f(B)\). If non-outward evaluation leaves some \(
abla^2f(x)
otin\mathbb H\), then positive semidefiniteness of \(M+2\operatorname{Diag}(\alpha)\) for all \(M\in\mathbb H\) does not imply positive semidefiniteness of the true corrected Hessian. For example, if \(f(x)=-	frac{\varepsilon}{2}x^2\), \(\varepsilon>0\), but a non-enclosing computation supplies \(\mathbb H=\{0\}\), then \(\alpha=0\) passes the computed test although \(f''=-\varepsilon<0\). This failure invalidates the curvature-based convexity certificate; it does not by itself negate a separately established pointwise-underestimation property of a nonnegative alphaBB box correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A non-enclosing Hessian interval can falsely certify convexity. Pointwise underestimation may nevertheless remain valid if it follows independently from the nonnegative box correction.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is twice differentiable on the bounded box \(B\).
At least one attainable Hessian is not contained in the computed interval-matrix family.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\(( orall M\in\mathbb H)\ M+2\operatorname{Diag}(\alpha)\succeq0\) does not imply \(( orall x\in B)\ 
abla^2f(x)+2\operatorname{Diag}(\alpha)\succeq0\) when \(
abla^2f(B)
subseteq\mathbb H\).
knowledge_statements.title: Containment Loss Invalidates the Curvature Certificate
Non-Outward Interval Evaluation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of a rigorous alphaBB curvature certificate through non-enclosing floating-point interval calculations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H_{ij}\) be claimed interval bounds for \(\partial^2 f/\partial x_i\partial x_j\) on a box \(B\), and let \(\alpha\) be computed from those bounds to certify \(\nabla^2 f(x)+2\operatorname{Diag}(\alpha)\succeq0\). If interval endpoints are evaluated without directed outward rounding, a true derivative value may lie outside \(H_{ij}\). The ensuing eigenvalue or diagonal-dominance bound can then overestimate the regional minimum curvature. Hence neither convexity of the computed alphaBB function nor its status as a certified relaxation follows from that interval calculation alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Intervals computed without outward rounding may miss true Hessian values, invalidating the resulting alphaBB convexity and lower-bound certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is twice differentiable on a bounded box \(B\).
At least one computed interval \(H_{ij}\) is not guaranteed to enclose all corresponding derivative values on \(B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The computed condition \(\nabla^2 f(x)+2\operatorname{Diag}(\alpha)\succeq0\) is not rigorously certified for every \(x\in B\).

notation.meaning: computed interval for a Hessian entry

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary role and mathematical distinction are plausible, but no source is cited for the verified interval-arithmetic requirement or for the asserted loss of certification under non-outward evaluation. An authoritative interval-arithmetic source with a section, theorem, or page locator is required.

children.title: Incorrect Derivative Structure
children.top_down_role: Invalid curvature certificates caused by derivative-generation or sparsity errors.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Corrects the distinction between conservative derivative enclosures and erroneous non-enclosing derivative structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H(x)=\nabla^2f(x)\) on a box \(B\), and let \(\mathcal H\) be a matrix family with \(H(x)\in\mathcal H\) for every \(x\in B\). If \(M+2\operatorname{Diag}(\alpha)\succeq0\) for every \(M\in\mathcal H\), then \(H(x)+2\operatorname{Diag}(\alpha)\succeq0\) throughout \(B\); exact equality between stored and true Hessians is unnecessary. Without containment this inference can fail: for \(f(x_1,x_2)=x_1x_2\), incorrectly omitting the mixed derivatives gives \(\widehat H=0\succeq0\), while \(H=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}\) has eigenvalues \(-1\) and \(1\), so \(\alpha=0\) does not certify convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conservative Hessian enclosures may be inexact, but derivative data that omit an attainable Hessian can falsely certify convexity, as the bilinear example shows.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: H(B)\subseteq\mathcal H\ \land\ (\forall M\in\mathcal H)\ M+2\operatorname{Diag}(\alpha)\succeq0\Rightarrow(\forall x\in B)\ H(x)+2\operatorname{Diag}(\alpha)\succeq0; without containment no such implication holds in general.

notation.meaning: conservative family containing every regional Hessian
incorrect generated Hessian in the counterexample

knowledge_statements.title: Hessian Containment Boundary
Incorrect Derivative Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invalidation of curvature bounds by erroneous symbolic, automatic, or sparse derivative generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\widehat H(x)\) be the Hessian representation used to choose \(\alpha\), while the true Hessian is \(H(x)=\nabla^2 f(x)\). A certificate derived from \(\widehat H(x)+2\operatorname{Diag}(\alpha)\succeq0\) is valid for the intended function only if \(\widehat H(x)=H(x)\) throughout the box, including all structurally nonzero off-diagonal entries. If derivative generation omits, mis-signs, or incorrectly declares an entry structurally zero, positive semidefiniteness of the represented matrix does not imply positive semidefiniteness of the true corrected Hessian, so convexity may fail.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A missing or incorrect Hessian entry can make the represented corrected Hessian positive semidefinite while the true alphaBB Hessian remains nonconvex.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is twice differentiable on a box \(B\).

notation.meaning: true Hessian of the modeled function

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is provided, and the statement that validity requires exact equality of the represented and true Hessians is too strong: a conservative enclosure or an inexact representation can still yield a valid certificate. A sourced correction must distinguish erroneous non-enclosing derivative data from conservative derivative bounds.

children.title: Uncertified Relaxation Optima
children.top_down_role: The gap between a valid convex model and a numerically certified regional lower bound.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Certified Dual Lower Bound for a Convex Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formalizes a standard route from a valid convex relaxation to a certified numerical regional lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(v_g=\inf\{g(x):h_i(x)\le0,\ Ax=b\}\) and define \(L(x,\lambda,
u)=g(x)+\sum_i\lambda_i h_i(x)+
u^{\mathsf T}(Ax-b)\) and \(q(\lambda,
u)=\inf_xL(x,\lambda,
u)\). For every rigorously validated \(\lambda\ge0\), weak duality gives \(q(\lambda,nu)\le v_g\). If this convex problem is a valid relaxation of an original regional problem with optimum \(v_f\), then \(q(\lambda,
u)\le v_g\le v_f\). A computed dual value is usable as a certificate only when multiplier feasibility and evaluation error are validated so that the reported value does not exceed the exact dual value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rigorously evaluated dual-feasible value lower-bounds the convex relaxation and the original regional optimum; an unchecked floating-point dual value does not.
assumptions_latex: \(g\) and the \(h_i\) define the stated convex relaxation, and the equality constraints are affine.
The relaxation is valid for the original regional minimization problem.
Multiplier feasibility and the reported dual value are rigorously validated on the lower-bound-preserving side.

notation.meaning: Lagrangian dual function of the convex relaxation

knowledge_statements.title: Certified Dual Lower Bound for a Convex Relaxation
Uncertified Relaxation Optima
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes validity of a convex relaxation from certification of its computed optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g\) be a valid convex underestimator of \(f\) on a feasible region \(D\), and define \(v_g=\inf_{x\in D}g(x)\) and \(v_f=\inf_{x\in D}f(x)\). Then \(v_g\le v_f\). If a numerical solver returns a feasible point \(\widehat x\), however, \(g(\widehat x)\ge v_g\); therefore its objective value is generally an upper bound on the relaxation optimum, not a certified lower bound for \(v_f\). A rigorous regional lower bound requires an independently valid dual bound, verified optimality certificate, or certified optimization error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid convex underestimator does not make an approximate primal solver value a lower bound; the relaxation optimum itself must be certified.
assumptions_latex: The solver supplies only a feasible approximate point \(\widehat x\in D\), without a certified dual or error bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_g\le v_f\le f(\widehat x)\), while \(g(\widehat x)\) need not satisfy \(g(\widehat x)\le v_f\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary role and inequalities are mathematically sound, including the distinction between a feasible primal value and a certified lower bound. However, the record has no source for the certification claim. A convex-optimization or verified-optimization reference with a specific locator is required.

children.title: AlphaBB-Envelope Relaxation Interface

children.title: AlphaBB Curvature Correction
children.top_down_role: Whole-function lower bounding through regional curvature compensation.

knowledge_statements.title: AlphaBB Curvature Correction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical separable quadratic convexification of a twice-differentiable function on a finite box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B=[l,u]\subset\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(f\in C^2(B)\), and choose \(\alpha\in\mathbb{R}_+^n\). The alphaBB correction is
\[f_\alpha(x)=f(x)-\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i(x_i-l_i)(u_i-x_i).\]
Because every product is nonnegative on \(B\), \(f_\alpha(x)\le f(x)\). Moreover,
\[\nabla^2 f_\alpha(x)=\nabla^2 f(x)+2\operatorname{Diag}(\alpha).\]
Thus any choice satisfying \(\nabla^2 f(x)+2\operatorname{Diag}(\alpha)\succeq0\) for all \(x\in B\) yields a convex underestimator that agrees with \(f\) at every vertex of \(B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: AlphaBB subtracts a separable endpoint-vanishing quadratic; sufficient diagonal curvature makes the result convex while preserving a lower bound and box-vertex values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f_\alpha\) is convex on \(B\), \(f_\alpha\le f\) on \(B\), and \(f_\alpha(v)=f(v)\) at every box vertex \(v\).

children.title: Structure-Specific Convex Envelopes
children.top_down_role: Tight convexification based on recognized term structure over a prescribed domain.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{vex}_R w(x,y)=\max\{l_x y+l_y x-l_xl_y,\;u_x y+u_y x-u_xu_y\}\) for every \((x,y)\in R\).

notation.meaning: convex envelope of the factor on the rectangle

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact convex-envelope representation for a bilinear factor over a rectangle.

source_refs.locator: 2.4 Convex Envelopes p. 45

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(w:R\to\mathbb{R}\) be given by \(w(x,y)=xy\) on \(R=[l_x,u_x]\times[l_y,u_y]\), where \(l_x<u_x\) and \(l_y<u_y\). Its convex envelope on \(R\) is
\[\operatorname{vex}_R w(x,y)=\max\{l_x y+l_y x-l_xl_y,\;u_x y+u_y x-u_xu_y\}.\]
Each affine term underestimates \(xy\) on \(R\), their maximum is convex, and no other convex underestimator of \(xy\) on the same rectangle is pointwise larger. This structure-specific envelope may therefore replace a generic whole-function curvature correction for the bilinear factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a rectangle, the bilinear convex envelope is the maximum of the two McCormick affine underestimators and is the strongest convex underestimator there.
knowledge_statements.title: Structure-Specific Convex Envelopes

source_witnesses.locator: 2.4 Convex Envelopes p. 45

children.title: Envelope Dominance Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structures and domains where convex envelopes materially strengthen generic alphaBB bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Envelope Dominance Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise dominance of an exact convex envelope over every valid alphaBB underestimator on the same domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be convex, let \(f:D\to\mathbb{R}\), and suppose the convex envelope \(e=\operatorname{vex}_D f\) exists. For any convex alphaBB underestimator \(a:D\to\mathbb{R}\) satisfying \(a(x)\le f(x)\) on \(D\), the defining maximality of the convex envelope gives \(a(x)\le e(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in D\). Hence the envelope relaxation has an objective lower bound at least as large as the alphaBB relaxation over every common feasible subset; equality occurs only where the chosen alphaBB underestimator attains the envelope.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Whenever an exact convex envelope is available on the same domain, it pointwise dominates every valid convex alphaBB underestimator.
assumptions_latex: \(a\) is convex on \(D\) and \(a\le f\) on \(D\).

notation.meaning: convex envelope of the function on the domain

source_refs.locator: 2.4 Convex Envelopes p. 45

source_witnesses.locator: 2.4 Convex Envelopes p. 45

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pointwise Dominance Need Not Improve the Optimal Value
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of strict pointwise strengthening away from the optimizer to imply a strictly stronger optimized relaxation value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(D=[0,1]\), let \(f(x)=x\), whose convex envelope is \(e(x)=x\). For \(0<\alpha\le1\), the alphaBB underestimator \(a_\alpha(x)=x-\alpha x(1-x)=\alpha x^2+(1-\alpha)x\) is convex and satisfies \(a_\alpha(x)<e(x)\) for every \(x\in(0,1)\). Nevertheless, \(\min_{x\in D}a_\alpha(x)=a_\alpha(0)=0=e(0)=\min_{x\in D}e(x)\). Hence strict envelope dominance throughout the interior need not strictly improve the optimized lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An envelope may strictly dominate alphaBB throughout the interior yet yield the same optimized lower bound because both models attain their minimum at a shared endpoint.

notation.meaning: a convex alphaBB underestimator of the affine function

knowledge_statements.title: Pointwise Dominance Need Not Improve the Optimal Value

children.title: Hybrid Envelope Integration
children.top_down_role: Model partitions combining envelope-based treatment for recognized terms with alphaBB treatment elsewhere.

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Envelope Integration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combination of alphaBB and envelope-based underestimators by pointwise maximum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be convex, and let \(a,e_1,\ldots,e_m:D\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex functions satisfying \(a(x)\le f(x)\) and \(e_j(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in D\). Define
\[h(x)=\max\{a(x),e_1(x),\ldots,e_m(x)\}.\]
Then \(h\) is convex, remains an underestimator of \(f\), and pointwise dominates every constituent relaxation. Here \(a\) may be a whole-function alphaBB correction while each \(e_j\) is a structure-specific envelope relaxation expressed in compatible variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The pointwise maximum of compatible alphaBB and envelope underestimators is convex, valid, and at least as strong as each constituent.
assumptions_latex: \(a\le f\) and \(e_j\le f\) on \(D\) for every \(j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(h=\max\{a,e_1,\ldots,e_m\}\) is convex and satisfies \(a,e_j\le h\le f\) on \(D\).

source_refs.locator: 2.4 Convex Envelopes p. 45

source_witnesses.locator: 2.4 Convex Envelopes p. 45

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Epigraph Form of a Hybrid Maximum
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact optimization formulation of the seed's pointwise-maximum hybrid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(h(x)=\max\{a(x),e_1(x),\ldots,e_m(x)\}\) on a nonempty convex set \(D\), \[\inf_{x\in D}h(x)=\inf\{t:x\in D,\ t\ge a(x),\ t\ge e_j(x)\ (j=1,\ldots,m)\}.\] If the infimum is attained, the same identity holds with minima.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hybrid maximum is optimized exactly by introducing one epigraph variable constrained above every constituent model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed epigraph problem has the same infimum as \(\inf_{x\in D}h(x)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Epigraph Form of a Hybrid Maximum

children.title: Whole-Function AlphaBB Treatment
children.top_down_role: Curvature correction applied to a nonlinear function without recursive factor decomposition.

knowledge_statements.title: Whole-Function AlphaBB Treatment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct alphaBB convexification applied to a complete factorable expression rather than its computational factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:B\to\mathbb{R}\) be the complete twice-differentiable objective or constraint function on a finite box \(B=[l,u]\). Whole-function alphaBB constructs
\[a(x)=f(x)-\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i(x_i-l_i)(u_i-x_i),\]
where \(\alpha\in\mathbb{R}_+^n\) is chosen so that \(\nabla^2 f(x)+2\operatorname{Diag}(\alpha)\succeq0\) throughout \(B\). The resulting \(a\) is a convex underestimator of the entire expression without introducing auxiliary variables for intermediate factors. Its strength depends on curvature bounds for the assembled function and can differ from a recursive factorable relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Whole-function alphaBB applies one curvature correction to the assembled expression, avoiding factor auxiliaries but relying on curvature bounds for the full function.
assumptions_latex: \(\alpha\in\mathbb{R}_+^n\) satisfies the displayed box-wide curvature condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a\) is convex on \(B\) and \(a(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in B\).

source_refs.locator: 11.2 Convex Lower Bounding Function p. 318

source_witnesses.locator: 11.2 Convex Lower Bounding Function p. 318

children.title: Recursive Factorable Relaxation
children.top_down_role: Expression-based relaxation built from recursively composed factor representations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Topological propagation of interval bounds and convex/concave estimators through a factorable expression graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent \(f\) on a box \(B\) by a finite directed acyclic graph whose leaves are constants or variables and whose operation nodes use supported primitives. Process the nodes topologically. At every node, propagate a valid range and valid convex lower and concave upper estimators from its parents using an atomic relaxation or a composition rule valid on the propagated ranges. The convex estimator \(f_B^{\mathrm{fac}}\) at the root then satisfies \(f_B^{\mathrm{fac}}(x)\le f(x)\) for all \(x\in B\); consequently, \(\inf_B f_B^{\mathrm{fac}}\le\inf_B f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Valid interval and convex/concave estimators propagated through an acyclic factorization graph yield a valid convex root underestimator.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) has a finite factorable directed acyclic graph on \(B\).
Every intermediate expression is defined on its propagated range.
Every atomic relaxation and composition rule used is valid on the corresponding propagated ranges.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f_B^{\mathrm{fac}}\le f\) on \(B\), so minimizing the root estimator supplies a valid lower bound.

notation.meaning: Convex estimator propagated to the graph root.

knowledge_statements.title: Recursive Factorable Relaxation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Construction cost of one recursive relaxation for a fixed expression graph and fixed regional bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a factorization DAG with node set \(V\), let \(C_v\) and \(S_v\) denote the work and stored data required by the selected atomic rule at node \(v\). Once a topological order is available, one complete forward propagation requires \(O(|V|+|E|+\sum_{v\in V}C_v)\) work and \(O(|V|+|E|+\sum_{v\in V}S_v)\) storage. The cost of subsequently optimizing the resulting convex relaxation is separate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One recursive construction is a single graph sweep plus the costs of its atomic relaxation rules; solving the finished relaxation is a separate cost.
assumptions_latex: The factorization graph is finite and acyclic.
Each node's atomic relaxation has finite construction cost \(C_v\) and storage \(S_v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Forward construction has the displayed graph-sweep work and storage bounds.

notation.meaning: Node and edge sets of the factorization DAG.
Atomic construction work and stored data at node \(v\).

knowledge_statements.title: Single-Sweep Propagation Cost

children.title: Factorization Advantage Regimes
children.top_down_role: Expression structures and domains where recursive factor treatment provides stronger or cheaper bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Factorization Advantage Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise criterion for a factorable relaxation to dominate whole-function AlphaBB.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f_B^{\mathrm{fac}}\) and \(f_B^{\alpha}\) be convex underestimators of \(f\) on the same nonempty compact box \(B\). A factorization-advantage regime is certified by \[f_B^{\mathrm{fac}}(x)\ge f_B^{\alpha}(x)\quad\text{for every }x\in B.\] Then the associated lower bounds satisfy \(L_B^{\mathrm{fac}}\ge L_B^{\alpha}\), where each bound is the minimum of its underestimator over \(B\). If there is a constant \(\delta>0\) such that \(f_B^{\mathrm{fac}}(x)\ge f_B^{\alpha}(x)+\delta\) throughout \(B\), then \(L_B^{\mathrm{fac}}\ge L_B^{\alpha}+\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A factorable relaxation is at least as strong when its underestimator dominates AlphaBB pointwise; uniform strict dominance yields a strictly improved lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(f_B^{\mathrm{fac}}\) and \(f_B^{\alpha}\) are finite convex underestimators on \(B\).

source_refs.locator: 1.2.5 Relaxation (Successive Outer Approximation) Strategies p. 31

source_witnesses.locator: 1.2.5 Relaxation (Successive Outer Approximation) Strategies p. 31

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shows that pointwise dominance is sufficient but not necessary for a better relaxation optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B=[-1,1]\), \(f(x)=10\), and use the valid AlphaBB model \(f_B^{\alpha}(x)=10+10(-1-x)(1-x)=10x^2\). Let \(f_B^{\mathrm{fac}}(x)=1\). Both are finite convex underestimators of \(f\) on \(B\), and \[L_B^{\alpha}=0<1=L_B^{\mathrm{fac}}.\] Nevertheless, \(f_B^{\mathrm{fac}}(1)=1<10=f_B^{\alpha}(1)\), so pointwise dominance fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A factorable underestimator may give a strictly better minimum without dominating the AlphaBB model everywhere.
knowledge_statements.title: Bound Improvement Without Pointwise Dominance

children.title: Mixed Decomposition Strategies
children.top_down_role: Partitioned models using factorable relaxations for selected subexpressions with alphaBB correction for residual terms.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed Decomposition Strategies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive combination of factorable and AlphaBB component underestimators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(f(x)=r(x)+\sum_{j=1}^m f_j(x)\) on a convex box \(B\). Let \(r_B^{\alpha}\) be a convex AlphaBB underestimator of \(r\), and let \(f_{j,B}^{\mathrm{fac}}\) be convex factorable underestimators of \(f_j\). Define \[f_B^{\mathrm{mix}}(x)=r_B^{\alpha}(x)+\sum_{j=1}^m f_{j,B}^{\mathrm{fac}}(x).\] Then \(f_B^{\mathrm{mix}}\) is convex and satisfies \(f_B^{\mathrm{mix}}(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in B\). Components may be assigned to either construction independently, provided their sum reproduces \(f\) and every component estimator is valid on the same box.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Decompose the objective, relax selected components recursively and the residual by AlphaBB, then sum the component underestimators.
assumptions_latex: \(B\subset\mathbb R^n\) is a nonempty convex box.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f_B^{\mathrm{mix}}\) is convex on \(B\) and \(\min_{x\in B}f_B^{\mathrm{mix}}(x)\le\min_{x\in B}f(x)\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strength comparison between two additive mixed decompositions of the same function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f=\sum_{j=0}^m f_j\) on \(B\). If \(p_j\) and \(q_j\) are convex underestimators of \(f_j\) and \(p_j\ge q_j\) on \(B\) for every \(j\), then \(P=\sum_jp_j\) and \(Q=\sum_jq_j\) are convex underestimators of \(f\), \(P\ge Q\) on \(B\), and \[\inf_{x\in B}P(x)\ge\inf_{x\in B}Q(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replacing any component of an additive mixed relaxation by a pointwise stronger valid convex underestimator cannot weaken the regional lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(p_j\) and \(q_j\) are convex underestimators of \(f_j\) on \(B\).

children.title: AlphaBB Polynomial Curvature Correction
children.top_down_role: Regional alphaBB underestimation applied to polynomial objectives or constraint functions.

knowledge_statements.title: AlphaBB Polynomial Curvature Correction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagonal AlphaBB underestimator specialized to a polynomial on a box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(p\in\mathbb R[x]\) and \(B=[\ell,u]\subset\mathbb R^n\). For \(\alpha\in\mathbb R_+^n\), define \[p_B^{\alpha}(x)=p(x)+\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i(x_i-\ell_i)(x_i-u_i).\] The correction is nonpositive on \(B\), so \(p_B^{\alpha}\le p\) there. Moreover, \(
abla^2p_B^{\alpha}(x)=
abla^2p(x)+2\operatorname{Diag}(\alpha)\). Consequently, any \(\alpha\ge0\) satisfying \(
abla^2p(x)+2\operatorname{Diag}(\alpha)\succeq0\) for every \(x\in B\) produces a convex polynomial underestimator and a valid lower-bounding problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Add a nonpositive separable quadratic to the polynomial, choosing nonnegative coefficients large enough to make the corrected Hessian positive semidefinite.
assumptions_latex: \(p\) is a real polynomial on \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_B^{\alpha}\le p\) on \(B\), and the displayed Hessian condition makes \(p_B^{\alpha}\) convex on \(B\).

source_refs.locator: 11.2 Convex Lower Bounding Function p. 318

children.title: Algebraic Polynomial Lower Models
children.top_down_role: Lower models exploiting monomial, sparsity, degree, or coefficient structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Algebraic Polynomial Lower Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Truncated quadratic-module certificate for a polynomial lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\) and let \(p,g_j\in\mathbb R[x]\). Fix an order \(d\). If a scalar \(\gamma\) and sum-of-squares polynomials \(\sigma_0,\ldots,\sigma_m\) satisfy \[p-\gamma=\sigma_0+\sum_{j=1}^m\sigma_jg_j,\qquad \deg(\sigma_0)\le2d,\qquad \deg(\sigma_jg_j)\le2d,\] then \(p(x)\ge\gamma\) for every \(x\in K\). Searching for the largest such \(\gamma\) is a semidefinite relaxation because each sum-of-squares constraint admits a positive-semidefinite Gram-matrix representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SOS identity expressing the objective minus a scalar through the constraints certifies that scalar as a global lower bound.

source_refs.source_title: Moments, Positive Polynomials and Their Applications
source_refs.locator: 5.3 Constrained Polynomial Optimization: Semidefinite Relaxations p. 117

source_witnesses.source_title: Moments, Positive Polynomials and Their Applications
source_witnesses.locator: 5.3 Constrained Polynomial Optimization: Semidefinite Relaxations p. 117

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonnegative polynomial lacking an SOS certificate at its natural degree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The Motzkin polynomial
\[
M(x,y)=x^4y^2+x^2y^4-3x^2y^2+1
\]
is nonnegative on \(\mathbb R^2\) but is not a sum of squares of polynomials. Consequently, for the unconstrained quadratic module and relaxation order \(d=3\), the valid lower bound \(\gamma=0\) does not admit the certificate \(M-\gamma=\sigma_0\) with \(\sigma_0\) sum-of-squares and \(\deg\sigma_0\le6\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid polynomial lower bound need not possess a fixed-order SOS certificate; the Motzkin polynomial is nonnegative but not SOS.
assumptions_latex: \(K=\mathbb R^2\) has no polynomial inequality generators.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\ge0\) on \(\mathbb R^2\), but \(M\notin\Sigma[x,y]\), so \(\gamma=0\) is not certified by the order-3 unconstrained SOS relaxation.

notation.meaning: Cone of sum-of-squares polynomials in x and y

knowledge_statements.title: Polynomial Structure Advantage Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bound-value criterion identifying when an algebraic polynomial relaxation improves AlphaBB.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq B\) be a nonempty compact semialgebraic set, let \(p_B^{\alpha}\) be an AlphaBB underestimator of a polynomial \(p\) on \(K\), and define \(L^{\alpha}=\inf_{x\in K}p_B^{\alpha}(x)\). Suppose an order-\(d\) sum-of-squares certificate establishes \(p(x)\ge\gamma_d\) for every \(x\in K\). The order-\(d\) algebraic relaxation is at least as strong as the AlphaBB relaxation whenever \(\gamma_d\ge L^{\alpha}\). If \(\gamma_d\ge L^{\alpha}+\delta\) for some \(\delta>0\), its certified lower bound improves on the AlphaBB value by at least \(\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polynomial structure is advantageous when the lower bound certified by the order-d algebraic relaxation is at least the AlphaBB relaxation value; a positive gap gives the same improvement in the bound.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq B\) is nonempty, compact, and semialgebraic.
An order-\(d\) sum-of-squares certificate proves \(p(x)\ge\gamma_d\) on \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma_d\ge L^{\alpha}\) implies that the order-\(d\) algebraic lower bound is no weaker than the AlphaBB lower bound.

notation.meaning: Lower bound certified by the order-d algebraic relaxation
Minimum value of the AlphaBB underestimator over K

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient exactness regime in which a truncated quadratic-module certificate reaches the polynomial optimum and dominates any inexact AlphaBB bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K=\{x:g_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\) be nonempty, let \(p^*=\inf_{x\in K}p(x)\) be finite, and fix an order \(d\). If
\[
p-p^*=\sigma_0+\sum_{j=1}^m\sigma_jg_j,
\qquad \deg(\sigma_0)\le2d,
\qquad \deg(\sigma_jg_j)\le2d,
\]
for sum-of-squares polynomials \(\sigma_j\), then the order-\(d\) algebraic lower bound equals \(p^*\). Consequently it is no weaker than every valid AlphaBB lower bound \(L^\alpha\le p^*\), and it is strictly stronger whenever \(L^\alpha<p^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite-order quadratic-module membership of the optimality gap makes the algebraic relaxation exact and therefore dominates every inexact AlphaBB lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(p-p^*\) has a quadratic-module certificate satisfying the order-\(d\) degree limits.
\(L^\alpha\le p^*\) is a valid AlphaBB lower bound.

notation.meaning: Global infimum of p on K

children.title: Hybrid Polynomial Convexification

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Polynomial Convexification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex hybrid formed from an AlphaBB underestimator and an SOS-certified constant polynomial lower model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq B\) be a nonempty convex semialgebraic set, let \(p_B^{\alpha}\) be a convex underestimator of a polynomial \(p\) on \(K\), and suppose an order-\(d\) algebraic certificate establishes \(p(x)\ge\gamma_d\) for every \(x\in K\). Define \[p_B^{\mathrm{hyb}}(x)=\max\{p_B^{\alpha}(x),\gamma_d\}.\] Then \(p_B^{\mathrm{hyb}}\) is convex, satisfies \(p_B^{\mathrm{hyb}}(x)\le p(x)\) on \(K\), and dominates both constituent lower models. Its epigraph formulation minimizes \(t\) subject to \(t\ge p_B^{\alpha}(x)\), \(t\ge\gamma_d\), and \(x\in K\). Consequently, \(\inf_{x\in K}p_B^{\mathrm{hyb}}(x)\ge\max\{\inf_{x\in K}p_B^{\alpha}(x),\gamma_d\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Take the pointwise maximum of the convex AlphaBB underestimator and an SOS-certified constant lower bound to obtain a valid convex hybrid no weaker than either constituent model.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq B\) is nonempty, convex, and semialgebraic.
\(p_B^{\alpha}\) is convex and satisfies \(p_B^{\alpha}(x)\le p(x)\) for every \(x\in K\).
An order-\(d\) algebraic certificate proves \(\gamma_d\le p(x)\) for every \(x\in K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_B^{\mathrm{hyb}}\) is a convex underestimator and \(\inf_K p_B^{\mathrm{hyb}}\ge\max\{\inf_K p_B^{\alpha},\gamma_d\}\).

notation.meaning: Constant lower bound certified by the order-d algebraic relaxation

knowledge_statements.title: Diagonal AlphaBB Curvature Correction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: AlphaBB as a diagonal positive-semidefinite curvature shift.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f\in C^2(B)\) on \(B=[\ell,u]\subset\mathbb R^n\), and let \(D=\operatorname{Diag}(\alpha)\) with \(\alpha\ge0\). The diagonal AlphaBB model is \[f_D(x)=f(x)+(x-\ell)^{\mathsf T}D(x-u).\] Because each product \((x_i-\ell_i)(x_i-u_i)\) is nonpositive on \(B\), \(f_D\le f\). Its Hessian is \(
abla^2f_D(x)=
abla^2f(x)+2D\). Hence the semi-infinite matrix condition \(
abla^2f(x)+2D\succeq0\) for all \(x\in B\) makes \(f_D\) a convex underestimator; the restriction that \(D\) be diagonal is the defining curvature limitation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: AlphaBB shifts curvature only through a nonnegative diagonal matrix while its separable quadratic correction remains nonpositive on the box.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nabla^2f+2D\succeq0\) on \(B\) implies that \(f_D\) is convex and \(f_D\le f\) on \(B\).

knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Lifted Semidefinite Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order semidefinite lifting for box-constrained quadratic optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(q(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+c_0\) on \(B=[\ell,u]\), introduce \(X\) to represent \(xx^{\mathsf T}\) and impose \[\begin{pmatrix}1&x^{\mathsf T}\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\succeq0.\] Together with valid linearized box-product inequalities, including \(X_{ii}-(\ell_i+u_i)x_i+\ell_i u_i\le0\), minimize \(\langle Q,X\rangle+c^{\mathsf T}x+c_0\). Every feasible \(x\in B\) lifts to \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\), while the semidefinite constraint relaxes the rank-one equality. Therefore the lifted optimum is a valid lower bound for \(\min_{x\in B}q(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace the quadratic matrix product by a lifted matrix, retain positive-semidefinite and box-product constraints, and drop rank one to obtain a lower bound.

notation.meaning: Lifted surrogate for the matrix product of x with itself

knowledge_statements.title: Semidefinite Strength Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible-set containment criterion for semidefinite dominance over AlphaBB.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_{\alpha}\) and \(R_{\mathrm{SDP}}\) be minimization relaxations of the same problem, expressed in a common lifted space and with the same linear objective \(F\). If \[R_{\mathrm{SDP}}\subseteq R_{\alpha},\] then \(L^{\mathrm{SDP}}=\inf_{z\in R_{\mathrm{SDP}}}F(z)\ge\inf_{z\in R_{\alpha}}F(z)=L^{\alpha}\). Thus semidefinite strengthening is guaranteed when its positive-semidefinite and product-consistency constraints cut off only points admitted by the AlphaBB relaxation. If additionally \(F(z)\ge L^{\alpha}+\delta\) throughout \(R_{\mathrm{SDP}}\) for some \(\delta>0\), the improvement is at least \(\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SDP relaxation is stronger whenever, in a common lifting, its feasible set is contained in the AlphaBB relaxation’s feasible set.
assumptions_latex: \(R_{\alpha}\) and \(R_{\mathrm{SDP}}\) contain every lifted feasible point of the original problem.
\(F\) is the same minimization objective on both relaxation sets.

notation.meaning: AlphaBB relaxation feasible set in the common lifting

children.title: Lifted-Model Cost Boundary
children.top_down_role: Problem sizes and structures where semidefinite strength no longer offsets lifted-model expense.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Storage and dense clique-factorization scaling after chordal decomposition of a sparse semidefinite lift.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a partial symmetric lift have a chordal specified-entry graph with maximal cliques \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\). Positive-semidefinite completability is equivalent to positive semidefiniteness of every fully specified clique principal matrix, with shared entries represented consistently. Storing clique matrices uses \[O\!\left(\sum_{j=1}^m|C_j|^2\right)\] scalar locations, and separately factorizing their dense blocks uses \[O\!\left(\sum_{j=1}^m|C_j|^3\right)\] arithmetic operations. If \(|C_j|\le\omega\), these become \(O(m\omega^2)\) storage and \(O(m\omega^3)\) factorization work.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Chordal sparsity replaces one dense matrix burden by costs summed over maximal clique blocks.
assumptions_latex: Clique representations agree on shared entries.
Each clique block uses dense storage and dense factorization.

notation.meaning: Maximal clique of the chordal sparsity graph

knowledge_statements.title: Chordal Sparse-Lift Cost Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation-size reduction and loss of convexity under an explicit low-rank factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent \(X\in\mathbb S_+^n\) as \(X=YY^\top\), where \(Y\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\). Dense storage of \(Y\) uses \(nr\) scalar entries, and explicitly forming \(YY^\top\) costs \(O(n^2r)\) arithmetic operations. For \(r\ll n\), this reduces representation size relative to a dense lifted matrix, but it restricts \(\operatorname{rank}(X)\le r\) and generally converts a convex lifted SDP into a nonconvex factorized formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Low-rank factorization reduces lifted storage but imposes a rank restriction and generally sacrifices convexity.
assumptions_latex: The operation count covers explicit product formation, not end-to-end optimization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{storage}(Y)=\Theta(nr)\) and forming \(YY^\top\) costs \(O(n^2r)\), with a generally nonconvex rank-restricted formulation.
knowledge_statements.title: Low-Rank Factorized-Lift Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation and single-operation costs of an unstructured dense semidefinite lift.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A dense symmetric lift \(X\in\mathbb S^n\) has \(n(n+1)/2\) independent scalar entries and requires \(\Theta(n^2)\) dense storage. A dense eigendecomposition or Cholesky-type factorization of a positive-semidefinite block of order \(n+1\) requires \(\Theta(n^3)\) arithmetic operations. A diagonal AlphaBB correction instead records \(n\) curvature coefficients. These counts concern representation and one dense matrix operation, not end-to-end SDP solution complexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without exploitable structure, semidefinite lifting changes linear-size diagonal curvature data into quadratic storage and cubic-cost dense matrix operations.
assumptions_latex: The lifted symmetric matrix and its principal PSD block are stored densely.
No sparsity, chordal decomposition, or low-rank factorization is exploited.
The operation count is for one dense factorization or eigendecomposition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\#X=n(n+1)/2\), dense storage is \(\Theta(n^2)\), and one dense PSD-block factorization or eigendecomposition costs \(\Theta(n^3)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Dense Symmetric-Lift Cost Boundary
Lifted-Model Cost Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense storage and linear-algebra cost introduced by matrix lifting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A dense symmetric lift \(X\in\mathbb S^n\) introduces \(n(n+1)/2\) scalar variables, compared with the \(n\) original variables used by a diagonal AlphaBB correction. Storing \(X\) therefore requires \(\Theta(n^2)\) numbers. Testing or factorizing the principal positive-semidefinite block of order \(n+1\) by dense eigendecomposition or Cholesky-type linear algebra requires \(\Theta(n^3)\) arithmetic operations per such operation. Consequently, absent exploitable sparsity or low-rank structure, matrix lifting crosses from linear-size curvature data to quadratic storage and cubic dense spectral algebra.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dense SDP lift uses quadratically many scalar entries and cubic-time dense matrix algebra, whereas diagonal AlphaBB stores only linearly many curvature coefficients.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is represented as a dense symmetric matrix.
\(n\) is the number of original variables.
No sparsity, chordal decomposition, or low-rank factorization is exploited.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{storage}(X)=\Theta(n^2)\) and one dense spectral or factorization operation on its PSD block costs \(\Theta(n^3)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Matrix Convexification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intersection of AlphaBB and semidefinite relaxations in a common lifted space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_{\alpha}\) and \(R_{\mathrm{SDP}}\) be valid convex relaxation sets for the same minimization problem in a common lifted space, and let \(F\) be their common convex objective. Define \(R_{\mathrm{hyb}}=R_{\alpha}\cap R_{\mathrm{SDP}}\). Every lifted feasible point of the original problem belongs to \(R_{\mathrm{hyb}}\), so \(L^{\mathrm{hyb}}=\inf_{z\in R_{\mathrm{hyb}}}F(z)\) is a valid lower bound. Since \(R_{\mathrm{hyb}}\) is contained in each constituent relaxation, \[L^{\mathrm{hyb}}\ge\max\{L^{\alpha},L^{\mathrm{SDP}}\}.\] The hybrid remains a convex optimization problem whenever both constituent sets and \(F\) are convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Intersect compatible AlphaBB and SDP relaxation sets; the hybrid stays convex and its lower bound is no weaker than either constituent bound.
assumptions_latex: \(R_{\alpha}\) and \(R_{\mathrm{SDP}}\) are convex and contain all lifted feasible points.
\(F\) is a common convex minimization objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L^{\mathrm{hyb}}\ge\max\{L^{\alpha},L^{\mathrm{SDP}}\}\), while \(L^{\mathrm{hyb}}\) remains a valid lower bound.

knowledge_statements.title: AlphaBB Quadratic Curvature Correction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagonal quadratic alphaBB correction on a fixed box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x\in X\), define
\[
f_{\alpha}(x)=f(x)+\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i(\ell_i-x_i)(u_i-x_i).
\]
Under the stated Hessian condition, \(f_{\alpha}\) is a convex underestimator of \(f\) on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The alphaBB correction adds a nonpositive separable quadratic whose diagonal curvature makes the resulting function convex while preserving a lower bound on the box.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is twice continuously differentiable on an open neighborhood of \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f_{\alpha}\) is convex on \(X\) and \(f_{\alpha}(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in X\).

notation.meaning: Box on which the relaxation is constructed.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact size and sharp boxwise maximum of the separable AlphaBB correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \[f_\alpha(x)=f(x)+\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i(\ell_i-x_i)(u_i-x_i),\qquad \alpha_i\ge0,\] one has \[f(x)-f_\alpha(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i(x_i-\ell_i)(u_i-x_i)\] and therefore \[0\le f(x)-f_\alpha(x)\le\frac14\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i(u_i-\ell_i)^2.\] The upper bound is attained at \(x=(\ell+u)/2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The AlphaBB correction gap has the sharp uniform maximum one quarter of the weighted sum of squared box widths.

children.title: Interval Taylor Lower Models
children.top_down_role: Local polynomial lower models controlled by interval enclosures of higher-order behavior.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Second-order Taylor lower model obtained from a uniform third-derivative bound on one box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a convex box, \(c\in X\), and let \(f\in C^3(U)\) for an open neighborhood \(U\supseteq X\). If \(|D^3f(z)[v,v,v]|\le M\|v\|_2^3\) for every \(z\in X\) and \(v\in\mathbb R^n\), then
\[
m_c(x)=f(c)+\nabla f(c)^{\mathsf T}(x-c)+\tfrac12(x-c)^{\mathsf T}\nabla^2f(c)(x-c)-\tfrac{M}{6}\|x-c\|_2^3
\]
satisfies \(m_c(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subtracting a certified cubic remainder bound from the second-order Taylor polynomial produces a box-valid lower model.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a convex box and \(c\in X\).
\(f\in C^3(U)\) for an open neighborhood \(U\supseteq X\).
\(|D^3f(z)[v,v,v]|\le M\|v\|_2^3\) for all \(z\in X\) and \(v\in\mathbb R^n\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Failure from an Invalid Hessian Lower Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-dimensional failure when the quadratic Taylor model uses an invalid regional Hessian lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(X=[-1,1]\), \(f(x)=-x^2\), and \(c=0\), using \(B=0\) in
\[
m_c(x)=f(c)+f'(c)(x-c)+\tfrac12B(x-c)^2
\]
gives \(m_c(x)=0>f(x)\) for every \(x\ne0\). Here \(B=0\) is not a lower bound for \(f''(x)=-2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the concave quadratic minus x squared, using zero as a purported Hessian lower bound produces a Taylor model lying above the function away from the center.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Monotonicity Under Tighter Hessian Lower Matrices
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise ordering of quadratic Taylor minorants having a common center.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a convex box, \(c\in X\), and \(f\in C^2(U)\) for an open neighborhood \(U\supseteq X\). If \(B_1\preceq B_2\preceq\nabla^2f(z)\) for every \(z\in X\), define \[m_j(x)=f(c)+\nabla f(c)^{\mathsf T}(x-c)+\tfrac12(x-c)^{\mathsf T}B_j(x-c),\quad j=1,2.\] Then \(m_1(x)\le m_2(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in X\).

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: integral Taylor remainder combined with a uniform Hessian lower bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix-bounded second-order Taylor model on one box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define
\[
m_c(x)=f(c)+\nabla f(c)^{\mathsf T}(x-c)+\tfrac12(x-c)^{\mathsf T}B(x-c),\qquad x\in X.
\]
The integral Taylor formula gives
\[
f(x)=f(c)+\nabla f(c)^{\mathsf T}(x-c)+\int_0^1(1-t)(x-c)^{\mathsf T}\nabla^2f(c+t(x-c))(x-c)\,dt.
\]
Because \(B\preceq\nabla^2 f(z)\) throughout \(X\), the integral remainder is at least \(\tfrac12(x-c)^{\mathsf T}B(x-c)\). Consequently, \(m_c\) is a valid lower model of \(f\) on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniform matrix lower bound on the Hessian replaces the second-order Taylor remainder and yields a certified lower model over the box.
knowledge_statements.title: Interval Taylor Lower Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The matrix-Hessian argument is mathematically plausible, but no inspectable source supports this exact formulation as an interval Taylor lower model. A source is also needed to settle the intended regularity convention; \(C^2(X)\) on a closed box should normally be replaced by differentiability on an open neighborhood. The statement additionally contains proof text.

children.title: Expansion-Center Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Influence of the Taylor expansion center on lower-model quality across a region.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative dependence of a second-order Taylor lower model on distance from its expansion center.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) be convex, \(c\in X\), and suppose \(f\) has an \(L\)-Lipschitz Hessian on \(X\). Define \[m_c(x)=f(c)+\nabla f(c)^{\mathsf T}(x-c)+\tfrac12(x-c)^{\mathsf T}\nabla^2f(c)(x-c)-\tfrac{L}{6}\|x-c\|_2^3.\] Then, for every \(x\in X\), \[m_c(x)\le f(x),\qquad 0\le f(x)-m_c(x)\le\tfrac{L}{3}\|x-c\|_2^3.\] Hence its uniform guarantee is controlled by \(\max_{x\in X}\|x-c\|_2^3\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a Lipschitz Hessian, this second-order Taylor lower model has a cubic center-distance error guarantee.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is twice differentiable on \(X\), and \(\|\nabla^2f(x)-\nabla^2f(y)\|_2\le L\|x-y\|_2\) for all \(x,y\in X\).
knowledge_statements.title: Lipschitz-Hessian Center Sensitivity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Minimax Center of a Rectangular Region
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimal center for radial worst-case remainder guarantees on a box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite box \(X=[\ell,u]\), define \(R(c)=\max_{x\in X}\|x-c\|_2\) for \(c\in X\). Then \[\min_{c\in X}R(c)=\tfrac12\|u-\ell\|_2,\] and the unique minimizer is \(c^*=(\ell+u)/2\). Consequently, the midpoint minimizes \(K\max_{x\in X}\|x-c\|_2^p\) for every \(K>0\) and \(p>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The box midpoint uniquely minimizes maximum Euclidean distance and therefore the radial worst-case Taylor remainder guarantee.
assumptions_latex: The center is restricted to \(c\in X\).

notation.meaning: Maximum Euclidean distance from \(c\) to the box.
Box midpoint and Euclidean minimax center.

knowledge_statements.title: Minimax Center of a Rectangular Region

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m_c(x)\le f(x)\) and \(0\le f(x)-m_c(x)\le \frac{L}{3}\|x-c\|_2^3\) for every \(x\in X\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: second-order Taylor remainder under a Lipschitz Hessian
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sensitivity induced by the distance from the expansion center.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x\in X\), set
\[
m_c(x)=f(c)+\nabla f(c)^{\mathsf T}(x-c)+\tfrac12(x-c)^{\mathsf T}\nabla^2f(c)(x-c)-\tfrac{L}{6}\|x-c\|_2^3.
\]
The Lipschitz-Hessian remainder estimate implies
\[
\left|f(x)-f(c)-\nabla f(c)^{\mathsf T}(x-c)-\tfrac12(x-c)^{\mathsf T}\nabla^2f(c)(x-c)\right|
\le\tfrac{L}{6}\|x-c\|_2^3.
\]
Thus \(m_c(x)\le f(x)\) and \(f(x)-m_c(x)\le\tfrac{L}{3}\|x-c\|_2^3\). Its worst-case guarantee is therefore controlled by \(\max_{x\in X}\|x-c\|_2^3\), making center choice quantitatively significant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a Lipschitz Hessian, Taylor-model error grows cubically with distance from the expansion center, so centrally placed or adaptively chosen centers improve the guarantee.
knowledge_statements.title: Expansion-Center Sensitivity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cubic remainder constants are internally consistent, and the property fits expansion-center sensitivity, but no cited source supports the exact lower model and \(L/3\) gap bound. The statement also presents a derivation rather than only the reviewed claim.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient asymptotic regime comparing certified Taylor and AlphaBB gap caps on shrinking boxes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_h\) contain \(c\), let \(\rho_h=\max_{x\in X_h}\|x-c\|_2\le Ch\), and suppose the Hessian is \(L\)-Lipschitz on every \(X_h\). Let the stated Taylor cap be \(T_h=(L/3)\rho_h^3\). For AlphaBB coefficients \(\alpha_i(h)\ge0\) and widths \(d_i(h)\), let its exact perturbation cap be \(A_h=\tfrac14\sum_i\alpha_i(h)d_i(h)^2\). If \(A_h\ge ah^2\) for some \(a>0\), then \(T_h\le(L C^3/3)h^3\), and \(T_h<A_h\) whenever \(0<h<3a/(LC^3)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the AlphaBB perturbation cap remains at least quadratic in box scale while the Taylor radius is linear, the Taylor certified cap is eventually smaller by one order.
assumptions_latex: \(\rho_h\le Ch\) and the Hessian is uniformly \(L\)-Lipschitz.
The comparison concerns certified caps, not exact pointwise errors.

notation.meaning: Exact cap of the AlphaBB perturbation gap

knowledge_statements.title: Cubic-versus-Quadratic Local Gap Scaling

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Certified-Cap Ordering Does Not Imply Model Dominance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interpretive boundary for comparisons based only on worst-case error certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the actual worst-case errors of two lower models be \(E_T,E_A\ge0\), with certified caps \(E_T\le U_T\) and \(E_A\le U_A\). The inequality \(U_T<U_A\) alone implies neither \(E_T<E_A\) nor pointwise dominance of the Taylor model. For example, the compatible values \(E_T=1\), \(U_T=1\), \(E_A=0\), and \(U_A=2\) have \(U_T<U_A\) but \(E_T>E_A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smaller analytic error cap is a stronger guarantee, not proof that the corresponding model is pointwise or actually uniformly tighter.
assumptions_latex: \(E_T\le U_T\) and \(E_A\le U_A\) are valid one-sided error certificates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U_T<U_A\not\Rightarrow E_T<E_A\), and it does not imply pointwise model dominance.

notation.meaning: Certified upper bounds on those errors
