review_flags: standard_field_rationale: comparison of elementary alphaBB and Lipschitz-Hessian gap bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient regime based on worst-case analytic gap bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The alphaBB correction satisfies
\[
0\le f(x)-f_{\alpha}(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i(x_i-\ell_i)(u_i-x_i)
\le\tfrac14\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i(u_i-\ell_i)^2.
\]
For the center-based Taylor model,
\[
0\le f(x)-m_c(x)\le\tfrac{L}{3}\|x-c\|_2^3\le\tfrac{L}{3}\rho_c^3.
\]
Hence the sufficient comparison condition
\[
\tfrac{L}{3}\rho_c^3<\tfrac14\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i(u_i-\ell_i)^2
\]
identifies a regime in which the certified worst-case Taylor gap bound is strictly smaller than the corresponding alphaBB gap bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Taylor models have the better stated worst-case guarantee when their cubic radius bound is smaller than the alphaBB quadratic box-width bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Taylor-Model Advantage Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition correctly compares the two stated analytic upper bounds, not the actual relaxation errors, and its content kind fits the leaf. An inspectable source is needed for this comparative regime claim, and the displayed derivation should be removed from the eventual knowledge statement.

children.title: Regional Hybrid Lower Models
children.top_down_role: Regional schemes selecting or combining alphaBB correction with interval Taylor lower models.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent selection between AlphaBB and interval-Taylor lower-bound values on each member of a finite regional cover.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X=\bigcup_{k=1}^N X_k\). For each \(k\), suppose \(a_k(x)\le f(x)\) and \(t_k(x)\le f(x)\) on \(X_k\), and define
\[
A_k=\inf_{x\in X_k}a_k(x),\qquad T_k=\inf_{x\in X_k}t_k(x),\qquad L_k=\max\{A_k,T_k\}.
\]
Then
\[
L=\min_{1\le k\le N}L_k\le\inf_{x\in X}f(x).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve both constituent lower problems on each region, retain the larger regional bound, and take the minimum across the cover to obtain a valid global lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(X=\bigcup_{k=1}^N X_k\) is a finite cover by nonempty regions.
\(a_k(x)\le f(x)\) and \(t_k(x)\le f(x)\) for all \(x\in X_k\).
The extended-real infima \(A_k\) and \(T_k\) are well defined.
knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Based Regional Model Selection

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Failure Under a Mismatched Validity Region
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of hybrid validity when a constituent is applied outside its certified region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=0\), \(X_1=[-1,0]\), and \(X_2=[0,1]\). The function \(a(x)=x\) is a valid minorant of \(f\) on \(X_1\), but not on \(X_2\). With the valid global minorant \(t(x)=-1\), the attempted hybrid \(h(x)=\max\{a(x),t(x)\}\) satisfies \(h(x)=x>f(x)\) for every \(x\in(0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A regional minorant cannot be carried into another region merely because the other hybrid constituent remains valid there.
assumptions_latex: \(a(x)=x\) is certified only on \(X_1\), while \(t(x)=-1\) is valid on both regions.

notation.meaning: Minorant certified only on the first region
Attempted hybrid on the second region

knowledge_statements.title: Failure Under a Mismatched Validity Region

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed convex combinations of regional AlphaBB and interval-Taylor minorants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a_k,t_k:X_k\to\mathbb R\) satisfy \(a_k(x)\le f(x)\) and \(t_k(x)\le f(x)\) on \(X_k\). For \(\lambda_k\in[0,1]\), define \[h_{k,\lambda_k}(x)=\lambda_k a_k(x)+(1-\lambda_k)t_k(x).\] Then \(h_{k,\lambda_k}\le f\) on \(X_k\). If \(X_k\) is convex and both constituents are convex, then \(h_{k,\lambda_k}\) is convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed convex mixture of valid regional AlphaBB and Taylor minorants remains valid and preserves convexity.
assumptions_latex: \(a_k\le f\) and \(t_k\le f\) on the same region \(X_k\).
For the convexity conclusion, \(X_k\) is convex and both constituents are convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(h_{k,\lambda_k}\le f\) on \(X_k\), with convexity under the additional stated assumptions.
knowledge_statements.title: Convex-Mixture Regional Hybrid

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison of two ways to combine common-domain regional minorants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a,t:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\), where \(X\ne\varnothing\), and define \(A=\inf_{x\in X}a(x)\), \(T=\inf_{x\in X}t(x)\), and \(H=\inf_{x\in X}\max\{a(x),t(x)\}\). Then \[H\ge \max\{A,T\}.\] If \(a\le f\) and \(t\le f\) on \(X\), then \(A,T,H\le\inf_X f\). Strict inequality is possible: for \(X=[0,1]\), \(a(x)=x\), and \(t(x)=1-x\), one has \(A=T=0\) and \(H=1/2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimizing the pointwise maximum of two common-domain minorants can give a strictly stronger regional bound than separately minimizing them and selecting the larger bound.
assumptions_latex: \(a\) and \(t\) are extended-real-valued functions on the same domain.
For lower-bound validity, \(a(x)\le f(x)\) and \(t(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_X\max\{a,t\}\ge\max\{\inf_Xa,\inf_Xt\}\), and the inequality can be strict.
knowledge_statements.title: Modelwise Selection versus Pointwise Hybridization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Common-domain combination of regional AlphaBB and interval-Taylor minorants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_k\ne\varnothing\) and let \(a_k,t_k:X_k\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) satisfy \(a_k(x)\le f(x)\) and \(t_k(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in X_k\). Define \(h_k(x)=\max\{a_k(x),t_k(x)\}\). Then \(h_k\le f\) on \(X_k\) and \(h_k\ge a_k,t_k\) pointwise. If \(X_k\) is convex and both constituent models are convex, then \(h_k\) is convex. For a finite cover \(X=\bigcup_{k=1}^N X_k\), \(\min_k\inf_{x\in X_k}h_k(x)\le\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The pointwise maximum of two lower models valid on the same region is a dominating lower model and preserves convexity; regional infima combine into a global lower bound over a finite cover.
assumptions_latex: \(X=\bigcup_{k=1}^N X_k\) is a finite cover by nonempty regions.
\(a_k\le f\) and \(t_k\le f\) on the same region \(X_k\).
For convexity, \(X_k\) and both constituent models are convex.
knowledge_statements.title: Pointwise-Maximum Regional Hybrid

assumptions_latex: \(a_k(x)\le f(x)\) and \(t_k(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in X_k\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: pointwise maximum preserves common lower-bound validity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise hybridization over a finite regional cover.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
On each region \(X_k\), define
\[
h_k(x)=\max\{a_k(x),t_k(x)\}.
\]
Since both constituent models underestimate \(f\) on \(X_k\),
\[
h_k(x)\le f(x)\qquad(x\in X_k).
\]
Therefore a certified lower bound for the global minimum is
\[
L=\min_{1\le k\le N}\ \min_{x\in X_k}h_k(x)
\le\min_{x\in X}f(x).
\]
Moreover, \(h_k(x)\ge a_k(x)\) and \(h_k(x)\ge t_k(x)\) pointwise. If both constituent models are convex on a convex region \(X_k\), then their pointwise maximum \(h_k\) is also convex there.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On each region, taking the maximum of valid alphaBB and Taylor lower models preserves validity and dominates either constituent lower model pointwise.
knowledge_statements.title: Regional Hybrid Lower Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The pointwise maximum of common lower models is valid, but no source supports the proposed alphaBB–Taylor hybrid. The record must introduce \(N\), the domain and regularity of \(f\), and either assume attainment of \(\min_{x\in X}f(x)\) or use infima. Its statement also contains proof text.
